senses.text: alphabetical letter The thirteenth letter of the alphabet: called $iynN . It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap [or non-vocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice]; and of the letters termed $ajoriy~ap , (TA,) from Al$~ajoru , which means “ the place of the opening of the mouth. ” (TA on the letter j . Cold, or coldness; (S, Msb, K;) accord. to the M, of water: (TA:) but one says gadaApN *aAtu $abamK [ A morning having coldness ]: (S:) and yawomN *uw $abamK A day having coldness. (Ham p.
363.) See also the next paragraph.

Cold, as an epithet, (S, Msb, TA,) applied to water, (S, TA,) and to rain; and one says gadaApN $abimapN , meaning A cold morning. (TA.) [And] Feeling cold: (K:) or feeling cold together with hunger. (AA, S, K.) ― -b2- Also A weapon, or weapons; as being cold: and such has been said to be the meaning [of ↓ ] in the verse cited above. (TA.) ― -b3- And Death; because of its coldness: ― -b4- and Poison; for the same reason. (K. [But see the verse cited above, and the explanation of it.]) -A2- And baqarapN $abimapN A fat ox or cow, or beast of the bovine kind: (K, TA:) but the epithet commonly known is sanimapN , [meaning “having a large hump,”] with s and n . (TA.)
: see $ibaAmN .

(Meyd, K.)
[and ↓ ] A kid, or lamb, having the piece of wood called $ibaAm put into its mouth and tied behind its head, in order that it may not suck its mother. (TA.)

senses.text: 2 and , (MA, K,) inf. n. ta$obiyhN , (S, K, KL,) He made it to be like it, or to resemble it; he assimilated it to it; (MA, KL;) i. q. mav~alahu [meaning thus: and also meaning he likened it to it, or compared it with it; agreeably with the explanation here next following]: (S, * K:) $ab~ahatu Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i I put the thing in the place, or predicament, of the [other] thing, by reason of an attribute connecting them [or common to them ]; which attribute may be real and ideal; real as when one says, “ this dirhem is like this dirhem, ” and “ this blackness is like this blackness; ” and ideal as when one says, “ Zeyd is like the lion ” or “ like the ass ” i. e. in his strength or his stupidity, and “ Zeyd is like 'Amr ” i. e. in his power and his generosity and similar qualities; and
Hence, EalaY Alt~a$obiyhi By way of comparison. ]

And mano A^a$obaha A^abaAhu famaA Zalama , (Meyd, TA,) or ↓ A^bahu famaA Zalama , as some relate it, (TA,) [ Whoso resembles his father, he has not done that which is wrong: ] a prov., meaning, he has not put the likeness in the wrong place; for there is not any one more fit, or proper, for him to resemble than he: or it may mean that the father has not done that which is wrong. (Meyd. [See also Har pp. 667-

8.]) And A$bh Alr~ajulu A^um~ahu , (IAar, K,) and ↓ , (K,) [ The man resembled his mother, ] meaning (assumed tropical:) the man became impotent, and weak. (IAar, K.) And it is said in a trad. of 'Omar, A_in~a All~abana yu$obahu Ealayohi [ Verily one becomes like by feeding upon milk ]: i. e. the infant that is suckled often becomes like the woman who suckles it, because of the milk: (JK:) or Allbn y$bh [app. for All~abanu yu$obahu Ealayohi ]: i. e. one acquires a likeness to the natural dispositions of the woman who suckles [him]: or, as it is also related, ↓ [app. for yuta$ab~ahu Ealayohi ]. (S, TA.) ― -b3- And $r~b AlA^aroDa waAln~axola (assumed tropical:) He gave drink to the land and the palm-trees. (TA.) ― -b4- And $r~b luqomapF biAld~asami (assumed tropical:) [ He imbued, or soaked, a morsel, or mouthful, with grease, or gravy ]. (TA in art. rwg .) ― -b5- And $ar~abotu Alqirobapa , (A 'Obeyd, S,) inf. n. ta$oriybN , (A 'Obeyd, K,) (assumed tropical:) I rendered the water-skin sweet; (K;) I put into the water-skin, it being new, clay and water, in order to render its savour sweet. (A 'Obeyd, S.) ― -b6- And $ur~iba Alz~aroEu Ald~aqiyqa : see 1, in the latter half of the paragraph.

3 , (S, A, K, TA,) inf. n. mu$aArabapN and $iraAbN , He drank with him; namely, a man. (TA.) ― -b2- [And He watered his camels, &c. with his, i. e. with another's : or he drew water with him for the watering of camels &c.:] see an ex. of the latter inf. n. in a verse cited voce $ariybN .
4 see 2, in two places. One says, A^a$orabotu AlA_ibila Hat~aY $aribato [ I made the camels to drink until they were satisfied with drinking
; or I watered the camels, or gave them to drink, &c.]; (S, TA;) [for] A^a$oraba is syn. with saqaY . (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Alv~awobu yu$orabu AlS~Kboga : see

5. And A^u$oriba Alv~awobu HumorapF (tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, was imbued, or saturated, with redness. (A.) And A^a$oraba All~awona (tropical:) He saturated the colour [ with dye ]. (K, TA.) And A^u$oriba lawonFA (assumed tropical:) It was intermixed with a colour; as also ↓ . (TA.) And A^u$oriba AlA^aboyaDu HumorapF (assumed tropical:) The white was suffused, or tinged over, with redness. (S, TA.) ― -b3- [

Hence, A^u$oriba is also said of a sound, as meaning (assumed tropical:) It was mixed with another sound; as appears from the words here following:] His~u AlS~awoti fiY Alfami mim~aA laA A_i$oraAba lahu mino Sawoti AlS~adori (assumed tropical:) [ The faint, or gentle, sound of the voice in the mouth, of such kind as has no mixture of the voice of the chest ]. (K in art. hms .) ― -b4- [Hence also,] A^u$oriba Alz~aroEu : see 1, latter half. ― -b5- And A^u$oriba fiY qalobihi Hub~ahu , (S,) or A^u$oriba Hub~a fulaAnK , (K,) or Hub~a fulaAnapa , (A,) (tropical:) [ He was made to imbibe into his heart the love of him, or of such a man, or of such a female; ] meaning that the love of him, or of her, pervaded, or commingled with, his heart, (S, A, K, TA,) like beverage. (TA.) Whence, in the Kur [i

5 see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- Hence one says, (Mgh,) t$r~b Alv~awobu AlEaraqa , (S, Mgh, * K,) and AlS~iboga , (A, Mgh, L,) (tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, imbibed, or absorbed, (S, A, Mgh, * L, K,) the sweat, (S, Mgh, K,) and the dye; (A, Mgh, L;) as though it drank it by little and little: (Mgh:) and [in like manner] one says, Alv~awobu y$rb AlS~iboga [app. ↓ , (like as one says yu$orabu HumorapF , as shown in the next preceding paragraph,) meaning (assumed tropical:) The garment, or piece of cloth, is made to imbibe, or absorb, the dye ]. (TA.) [It is said that] the verb is not used intransitively in the [proper] language of the Arabs. (Mgh.) [But] one says, t$r~b AlS~ibogu fiY Alv~awobi , meaning (tropical:) The dye pervaded the garment, or piece of cloth: (K, * TA:) and

10 (assumed tropical:) His, or its, colour became intense. (K.) And Ast$rbt Alqawosu HumorapF (assumed tropical:) The bow became intensely red: such is the case when it is made of the [tree called] $aroyaAn . (AHn, (TA.)
11 : see 4, near the beginning.

4 , (S, A, O, K,) inf. n. Ai$oriy^obaAbN , (S, O,) (tropical:) He raised his head like the camel that has satisfied his thirst on the occasion of drinking: (A:) or he stretched forth his neck to look: (S, A, O, K:) not improbably, from Al$~urobu in its well known sense, as though he did so when preparing to drink: (O:) or, as is said in the L, from ma$orabapN as syn. with gurofapN : (TA:) you say, Ai$oraA^ab~a lahu , (S, A,) or A_ilayohi , (K,) or both; (TA;) [the former of which may be rendered He raised his head at it, or he stretched forth his neck at it to look

; or, as also the latter, he stretched forth his neck to look at it; ] namely, a thing: (S:) or A$rA^b~ originally means he stretched forth his neck in preparing to drink water: and then, in consequence of frequency of usage, he raised his head, and stretched forth his neck, in looking; and hence is trans. by means of A_ilaY : (Har p. 152:) or he raised, or exalted, himself. (K, * TA.) ya$oray^ib~uwna liSawotihi , occurring in a trad., means (tropical:) They will raise their heads at his voice to look at him. (TA.) And Ai$oraA^ab~a Aln~ifaAqu waA@rotad~ati AlEarabu , in another trad., means (tropical:) Hypocrisy exalted itself [ and the Arabs apostatized, or revolted from their religion ]. (TA.)

an inf. n. of $ariba [q. v.]. (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) -A2- And a pl., (S, Msb,) or [rather] a quasipl. n., (ISd, TA,) of $aAribN , q. v. (S, ISd, Msb, TA.) -A3- [Golius assigns to it also the meaning of “ Linum tenue, ” as on the authority of Meyd.]

an inf. n. of $ariba [q. v.]; (S, A, Msb, K, &c.;) like ↓ : (S, A, K:) or a simple subst. [signifying The act of drinking ]; (AO, S Msb, K;) as also ↓ . (AO, S, K.) -A2- In the phrase A^axuwka $urobN it is used as [an epithet,] meaning *uw $urobK [which may be regarded as virtually syn. with $aAribN or as similar to this latter but intensive in signification]. (Ham p.

: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places. ― -b2- Also Water, (K, TA,) itself; so some say; (TA;) as also ↓ , (K, accord. to the TA,) with kesr, (TA,) or ↓ , (so in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K,) i. e. water that one drinks; so says AZ: pl. of the former A^a$oraAbN . (TA.) [See also $araAbN .] ― -b3- [And A draught of milk: see an ex. in a verse cited in art. slf , conj.

4.] ― -b4- And A share, or portion that falls to one's lot, of water: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) or so $irobN mino maA='K . (ISk, TA.) It is said in a prov., A=xiruhaA A^aqal~uhaA $irobFA [ The last of them is the one of them that has the least share of water ]: originating from the watering of camels; because the last of them sometimes comes to the water when the watering-trough has been exhausted. (S. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i.

61.]) ― -b5- As a law-term, it means The use of water [or the right to use it ] for the watering of sown-fields and of beasts. (Mgh.) ― -b6- Also A wateringplace; syn. maworidN : (AZ, K:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) A time of drinking: (K:) but they say that it denotes the time only by a sort of tropical application; and they differ respecting the connexion of this meaning with the proper meaning. (MF, TA.)
: see $arabapN , in two places.

A single act of drinking. (S.) ― -b2- And A single draught, or the quantity that is drunk at once, of water. (S.) It is said in a prov., niEoma miEolaqu Al$~arobapi h`*aA [ Excellent, or most excellent, is the traveller's drinking-cup, or bowl, that will hold a single draught, namely, this! ]: the miEolaq is said by As to be a drinking-cup or bowl which the rider upon a camel suspends [to his saddle]: (Meyd:) it is said in describing a camel: (TA:) and it means that, to the place of alighting to which he desires to go, he is content with a single draught, not wanting another: (Meyd, TA:) the prov. is applied to him who, in his affairs, is content with his own opinion, not wanting that of another person. (Meyd.) $arobapu A^abiY Aljahomi [ The draught of Abu-l-Jahm ] is said of a thing that

87.) ― -b4- [In the conventional language of the physicians, it is a term applied to A dose of medicine, such as is drunk and also such as is eaten. ] -A2- Also A palm-tree that grows from the date stone: (K:) pl. $arabaAtN . (TA. [It seems to be there added that $araAy^ibu and $araAbiybu are also its pls.: the former may be like DaraAy^iru pl. of Dar~apN : the latter is app. a mistranscription, and should perhaps be $araAy^iybu , for $araAy^ibu ; like maHaAmiyru for maHaAmiru , &c.])

, (K,) or $urobapN mino maA='K , (S,) The quantity of water that satisfies thirst. (S, K.) ― -b2- $urobapN is also syn. with ↓ [originally an inf. n.] meaning (assumed tropical:) A colour tinged over with another colour; as in the saying, fiyhi $urobapN mino HumorapK (assumed tropical:) [ In him is a colour tinged with redness ]: (S, TA:) [and] (tropical:) somewhat of redness; as in the phrase, fiyhi $urobapN (tropical:) [ In him is somewhat of redness ]: (A:) or (assumed tropical:) a redness in the face: (K:) or (assumed tropical:) whiteness mixed with redness. (IAar, TA voce HusobapN .)

[The act, or habit, of ] much drinking. (K.) One says, A_in~ahu la*Fw $arabapK , meaning Verily he is one who drinks much. (AA, AHn, TA.) -A2- It is also allowable as a pl. of $aAribN [q. v.]. (Msb.) -A3- Also A small trough, (S, K, TA,) made, (S,) or dug, (TA,) around a palm-tree, (S, K, TA,) and around any other kind of tree, and filled with water, (TA,) holding enough to irrigate it fully, (K, TA,) so that it is plentifully irrigated thereby: (S, TA:) pl. ↓ [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which the former is the n. un.,] and [the pl. properly so termed is] $arabaAtN . (S.) ― -b2- And i. q. kurodu daborapK , (K, TA,) which is syn. with masoqaApN : (TA:) [from a comparison of the explanations of all of these words, it seems to mean A channel of water for the irrigation of a plot, o
One who drinks much; (ISk, S, K;) as also ↓ and ↓ . (S.) One says rajulN A^ukalapN $urabapN A man who eats and drinks much. (ISk, S.)
, applied to herbage, i. q. gamolaY ; (O, K;) i. e. Tangled and dense, one part above another. (O.)

, [said to be] the only word of this form except jarab~apN , (K,) [but to this should be added bagat~apN , inf. n. of bagatahu ,] A way, mode, or manner, of being, or acting &c. (S, O, K.) One says, maA zaAla fulaAnN EalaY $arab~apK waAHidapK Such a one ceased not to be [ employed ] upon one affair. (S, O.) -A2- And A tract of land, (K, TA,) soft, or plain, (TA,) producing herbs, but having in it no trees. (K, TA.) ― -b2- [And] The side of a valley. (Mgh.)

A beverage, or drink, (Mgh, L, Msb, K,) of any of the liquids, (Mgh, Msb,) or of anything that is not chewed, (L,) or of whatever kind and in whatever state it be; thus in a copy of the K: (TA:) and syn. with $araAbN are ↓ and ↓ , (K,) accord. to a saying attributed to AZ: (TA:) or these two have another meaning, expl. in the next paragraph: (K:) the pl. of $araAbN is A^a$oribapN ; (Mgh, TA;) or it has no pl., as is said in the K in art. nhr [accord. to one or more of the copies; but see nahaArN , where it is shown that in copies of the K, as well as in the S, the word to which this statement relates is saraAbN , with the unpointed s ]. (TA.) The lawyers [and generally the post-classical writers, and sometimes others,] mean thereby [ Win, and] such beverage as is forbidden. (Mgh.) [Also Si

and ↓ are syn. with $araAbN , q. v.: or both signify Water inferior to the Ea*ob [or sweet ]: (K:) or [ brackish water; i. e.] water between the salt and the sweet: (AO, S:) or water drinkable, or fit to be drunk, but in which is disagreeableness: (Msb:) or the former signifies water that has some degree of sweetness, and is sometimes drunk by men notwithstanding what is in it; and ↓ the latter, water inferior to what is sweet, and not drunk by men save in cases of necessity, but sometimes drunk by cattle: (IKtt, TA:) or ↓ the latter, the sweet: and the former is said to signify water that is drunk: (TA:) or ↓ the latter, water that has no sweetness in it, but is sometimes drunk by men notwithstanding what is in it; and the former, water inferior to this in sweetness, and not drunk by men
Also, $aruwbN , A man who drinks vehemently. (TA.) See also $urabapN : and $ir~iybN . ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A she-camel desiring the stallion. (K.)

: see $araAbN : and $aruwbN ; the latter in five places. -A2- Also One who drinks with another: (S, K:) and one who waters his camels with those of another: of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mufaAEilN : (S:) and one who draws water, or is given to drink, with another. (IAar, K.) You say, huwa $ariyibiY [ He is my companion in drinking

; or in watering his camels with mine: &c.]. (TA.) And a rájiz says, rub~a $ariybK laka *iY HusaAsi kaAlHaz~i biAlmawaAsiY ↓ [ Many a one who waters his camels with thine, or who draws water with thee for the watering of camels, having an evil disposition, his watering &c. is like the cutting with razors ]: i. e., thy waiting for him at the watering-trough is [a cause of] killing to thee and to thy camels. (TA.)

is expl. in the S as meaning A sheep, or goat, which one drives back, or brings back, from the water, when the sheep, or goats, are satisfied with drinking, and which they follow: but in some of the copies in a marginal note stating that the correct word is sariybapN , with the unpointed s . (TA.)
A cup-bearer: or a butler: and a seller of wine or of sirup. (MA.)

a subst. (K) from Ai$oraA^ab~a [q. v.; as such signifying (tropical:) A raising of the head like the camel that has satisfied his thirst on the occasion of drinking: &c.]: (S, K, TA:) like TumaA^oniynapN [from AiTomaA^an~a ]. (K, TA.)
: see $urabapN : and what here next follows.
Addicted to $araAb [i. e. drink, or wine ]; (S, K, TA;) like xim~iyrN ; (S;) as also ↓ and ↓ and ↓ . (TA.) -A2- See also $aruwbN .
[ A tassel: so in the language of the present day: probably post-classical: pl. $araAriybu .]

Drinking, or a drinker: pl. $aAribuwna (Msb) and ↓ , like as SaHobN is of SaAHibN , (S, Msb,) or, accord. to ISd, (TA,) $arobN , which signifies people drinking, (K, TA,) and assembling for drinking, is a quasi.-pl. n. of $aAribN , being like rakobN and rajolN ; and $uruwbN , which is said by IAar [and in the S] to be pl. of $arobN , is pl. of $aAribN , like as $uhuwdN is of $aAhidN ; (TA;) $arabapN also is allowable as a pl. of $aAribN , like as kafarapN is pl. of kaAfirN ; (Msb;) and A^a$orubN is pl. of $arobN , or it may be an anomalous pl. of $aAribN : (MF:) the pl. $uruwb occurs in the saying of El-Aashà, huwa AlwaAhibu AlmusomiEaAti Al$~uruw ba bayona AlHariyri wabayona Alkatano [ He is the giver of female singers to the drinkers, some clad in silk and some in linen ]. (S.) ― -b2- Se

Hence, The mustache; i. e.] the defluent hair over the mouth; (Msb;) or so $awaAribu , (Lh, A, K,) which is the pl., (Lh, S, Msb,) as though the sing, applied to every distinct part: (Lh:) the two [halves] are called $aAribaAni : (S, TA:) or, as some say, only the sing. is used, and the dual is a mistake: (TA:) accord. to AHát (Msb, TA) and AAF, (TA,) the dual is is scarcely ever, or never, used; but accord. to AO, the Kilábees say $aAribaAni , with regard to the two extremities: (Msb, TA:) and the pl., (A, K,) or, accord. to the T &c., the dual, (TA,) signifies the long portions [ of the hair ] on the two sides of the sabalap [q. v.]: (T, A, K, TA:) or (K, TA) $aAribN signifies the sabalap altogether, (A, K, TA,) as some say; but this is not correct. (TA.) One says, Tar~a $aAribu AlgulaAm

[a subst. from $aAribN , made such by the affix p ,] A people, or party, dwelling upon the side ( Daf~ap , in some copies of the K Suf~ap ,) of a river, (S, * A, K,) and to whom belongs the water thereof. (S.)
as syn. with $urobapN : see the latter.

is a noun of place, [and of time,] as well as an inf. n.: [i. e.] it signifies [ A place, and a time, of drinking: or] the quarter ( wajoh ) whence one drinks: (S, TA:) and a place to which one comes to drink at a river or rivulet: (TA:) and ↓ , (S, Msb, K, TA,) not, as is implied in the K, ma$orubapN also, (TA,) signifies [the same, as is indicated in the A

; or] a place whence people drink; (Msb, TA; *) i. q. ma$oraEapN ; (K;) or like a ma$oraEap . (S, TA.) One says, h`*aA ma$orabu Alqawomi and ↓ [ This is the people's, or party's, drinkingplace, or place whence they drink ]. (A.) And it is said in a trad., ↓ , (S, TA,) i. e. [ Cursed is he ] who takes entirely to himself, debarring others from it, a place whence people drink. (TA.) ― -b2- See also $irobN .
(tropical:) A man whose complexion is tinged over [or intermixed ] with redness. (TA.) [See 4: and see also mu$ar~abN .]

A man whose camels have drunk [ until satisfied with drinking: see A^a$oraba near the end of the first paragraph]. (TA.) And A man whose camels are thirsty, or who is himself thirsty. (TA.) AisoqiniY faA_in~aniY mu$oribN is a saying mentioned by IAar, and expl. by him as meaning EaTo$aAnu : it means [ Give thou me to drink, for ] I am thirsty or my camels are thirsty. (TA.)
: see $irobN : and see also $aruwbN .
: see ma$orabN , in three places. ― -b2-

Hence, (A, TA,) An upper chamber; syn. gurofapN ; (S, A, Msb, K, TA;) and Euil~iy~apN ; (S, * K;) both of which signify the same; (MF, TA;) because people drink therein; (A, TA;) as also ↓ : (S, Msb, K, TA:) pl. ma$aAribu , (TA,) syn. with EalaAliY~u , (S,) and ma$orabaAtN . (TA.) ― -b3- And the former, (K, TA,) not, as is implied in the K, the latter also, (TA,) A Suf~ap [i. e. roofed vestibule or the like ]: (K, TA:) or the like of a Suf~ap in the front of a gurofap [expl. above]. (TA.) ― -b4- Also the former, (K, TA,) not, as is implied in the K, both words, (TA,) Soft, or plain, land, in which is always herbage, (K, TA,) i. e. green and juicy herbage. (TA.) ― -b5- See also mi$orabapN . -A2- [Also A cause of drinking: a word of the class of maboxalapN &c.] One says TaEaAmN ma$orabapN Fo
: see the next preceding paragraph.
, (S, A, K,) and MF says that ↓ is allowable in the same sense, mentioning it as on the authority of Fei, [in my copy of whose lexicon, the Msb, I do not find it,] (TA,) A drinkingvessel. (S, A, K.)

(tropical:) A man whose complexion is much tinged over [or much intermixed ] with redness. (TA.) [See also mu$orabN .] ― -b2- mu$ar~abapN is an epithet applied to Certain letters the utterance of which, in pausing, is accompanied with a sort of blowing, but not with the same stress as the [ generality of those that are termed ] majohuwrap : they are zaAY and ZaA=' and *aAl and DaAd : [and Lumsden (in his Ar. Gr. p. 47) states that raA=' belongs to the same class, likewise: and, as some say, nuwn when movent:] Sb says that some of the Arabs utter with more vehemence of voice than others. (TA.)

$rb.sourceCitation: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon · Book I, Part 4, p. 1526

senses.text: Also, (S, A, O, TA,) [aor. ,] inf. n. $arojN , (S, O, K, TA,) He put, or set, together bricks ( labin ), in order, side by side, or one upon another, compactly; (S, A, O, K, TA;) and (O) so ↓ , (O, Mgh, Msb,) with teshdeed, (Msb,) inf. n. ta$oriyjN . (O, Mgh.) ― -b3- And He collected together, (O, K,) or put together, or joined, (L,) any thing or things, one part to another, or one thing to another; (O, L;) as also ↓ . (L.) ― -b4- [And app. He wove palm-leaves: see $riyjapN , below; and see also $ariyTN .] ― -b5- And He mixed (A, O, K) beverage, or wine: and in like manner ↓ he mixed honey &c. with water. (O.) ― -b6- And $arajahu fiY AlA^amori , aor. , (TK,) inf. n. as above, (K, TK,) He was, or became, a partner, or sharer, (K, TK,) with him in the affair. (TK.) -A2-
Also, (O,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He lied; (O, K;) like saraja and sadaja . (O.) -A3- $arija , (O, TA,) with kesr to the r , (O,) He was, or became, beautifully fat. (O, TA.)
2 , inf. n. ta$oriyjN : see above, in three places. ― -b2-

Also, said of pasture, or herbage, It caused the flesh of an animal to be intermixed with fat. (L.) And $ur~ija , said of the flesh of an animal, It was intermixed with fat: (S, O:) or was made to be of two colours by reason of the fat and the flesh: (TA:) and biAl$~aHomi ↓ it (the flesh) became intermixed with fat. (S, O, K.) -A2- And ta$oriyjN also signifies The sewing with stitches far apart. (S, O, K) ― -b2- See also
3 The being like, one to another. (O, K.) One says, $Arjhu He was like to him
; or it, to it: and $aArajaA They two were like, each to the other. (TK.)

4 , (AZ, S, A, O, Msb,) inf. n. A_i$oraAjN ; (K;) and ↓ , (AZ, O,) inf. n. ta$oriyjN ; (K;) and ↓ , (AZ, O,) inf. n. $arojN ; (K;) He closed, or made fast, the [leathern receptacle called] xariyTap (AZ, O, K) or Eayobap , (S, A, O, Msb,) by inserting its A^a$oraAj [or loops ] one into another. (S, A, * O, Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A$rj Sadorahu Ealayohi (tropical:) [ He closed his bosom upon it ]. (A, TA.)
7 , (K,) or An$rjt , said of a bow, (ISk, S, O,) It split. (ISk, S, O, K.)

A place in which water flows from a [ stony tract such as is termed ] Har~ap to a soft, or plain, tract; (S, K;) as also ↓ : (TA:) or the latter signifies [simply] a place in which water flows; and some elide the p , saying $arojN : (Msb:) pl. $iraAjN (S, Mgh, Msb, K, expl. in the Mgh agreeably with the former explanation above, and said in the Msb to be pl. of $arojapN ,) and $uruwjN . (S, K.) -A2- Also A party, or distinct body or class [of men]. (S, K.) One says, A^aSobaHuwA fiY h`*aA AlA^amori $arojayoni i. e. [ They became, in this affair, ] two parties. (S.) And it is said in a trad., A^aSobaHa Aln~aAsu $arojayoni fiY Als~afari [ The people, or men, became two parties in the journey ]; meaning, half of them fasting, and half of them breaking the fast. (TA.) ― -b2- And The like of ano

; or, accord. to IAar, two mixed colours, not black and white: (TA:) and ↓ this latter, also, the two lines of the nayraAni [or two ornamental borders ] of a [ garment of the kind called ] burod , (O, K,) one of which is A^axoDar [here meaning of a dark, or an ashy, dust-colour ], and the other white or red. (O.) ― -b5- And Al$~aroju , like falos [in measure, not to be confounded with Al$~araju ], signifies The [ perinæum, or] part between the anus and the testicles. (IKtt, TA.)

The loops (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) of the [leathern receptacle called] Eayobap , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and of the [tent called] xayomap , (O, TA,) and the like, and of the muSoHaf [or copy of the Kur-án, &c.]: (TA:) [the loops here meant being such as are inserted one into another, to close a bag &c.: see 4:] pl. A^a$oraAjN . (S, Msb.) [And it seems also, from what here follows, to signify A single loop. ] ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) The anus: (Msb, TA:) or hence $araju Ald~uburi signifies (assumed tropical:) the anus. (Mgh.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) The vulva of a woman: (O, K:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b4- And $araju Ald~araAhimi [ The purse for money ]. (M and K in art. A sheep, or goat, having its ear slit (S, Mgh, O, K) lengthwise, (K,) without its being separated: (TA:) or having the ear slit in two, (As, Msb, TA,) as though it were a zanamap [q. v.]: (As, TA:) or $aroqaA='u applied to an ear signifies cut at its extremities, without having anything thereof separated: and applied to a she-goat ( maEozap ), having its ear slit lengthwise, without its being separated: and, as some say, applied to a $Ap , having the inner part of its ear slit on one side with a separating slitting, the middle of its ear being left sound: or, accord. to Aboo-'Alee in the “ Tedhkireh, ” $aroqaA='u signifies having its ears slit with two slits passing through, so as to become three distinct pieces. (M.)

[ Of, or relating to, the east, or place of sunrise; eastern, or oriental ]. ― -b2- laA $aroqiy~api walaA garobiy~apK , (K, TA,) in the Kur [xxiv. 35], (TA,) means Not such that the sun shines upon it at its rising only (Fr, K, TA) nor at its setting only, (Fr, TA,) but such that the sun lights upon it morning and evening: (Fr, K, TA:) or, accord. to El- Hasan, it means not of the trees of the people of the present world, but of the trees of the people of Paradise: Az, however, says that the former explanation is more fit and more commonly receive. (TA. [See also 2; and see $ariymN .]) ― -b3- $arama Alv~ariydapa , aor. and inf. n. as above, and the latter, by poetic license, $aramN , He ate of the sides, or of the edge, of the vrydp [or mess of crumbled bread moistened with broth ]. [In the S and A and K, this is placed as the first of all the meanings in this art.; and in the A, it is mentioned among the meanings that are proper, not tropical; but in my opinion it is tropical. See also $aEavN below.])

2 , inf. n. ta$oEiyvN , He rendered it (i. e. hair) [ shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy: (see 1:) or] matte, or compacted, and dusty: or he rendered him [ shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy, in his hair: or] matted, or compacted, and dusty, in his hair. (TA.) ― -b2- ta$oEiyvN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The separating, disuniting, dispersing, or scattering, a thing. (S.) And (assumed tropical:) The making to separated like as do rivers and branches. (L.) [Hence,] $E~v raA^osa Als~iwaAki (tropical:) [ He made the head of the tooth-stick to become disintegrated
; or separated, disunited, or uncompacted, in its component parts or its fibres

; or rendered it brushy; by bruising it, battering it, or mangling it by blows: see 1]. (A.) ― -b3- $E~v Als~anaA (tropical:) He took of the straggling branches, or sprigs, of the senna, without pulling it up by the roots. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- See also 5, in two places. ― -b5- $E~v Aln~aAsu fiY AlT~aEoni Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) The people took, or began, to impugn his character, censure him, reproach him, or speak against him, by befouling his reputation ( bita$oEiyvi EiroDihi ). (TA, from a trad.) ― -b6- And $E~v minohu (assumed tropical:) He detracted from his reputation; syn. gaD~a minohu and tanaq~aSahu : from Al$~aEavu [as inf. n. of

1 in the last of the senses assigned to it above,] meaning Ainoti$aAru AlA^amori . (L.) ― -b7- And also, inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He repelled from him, or defended him: (K:) or he defended his reputation. (TA.) [Thus it has two contr. meanings.]

4 (tropical:) Such a one was angry by reason of me; syn. gaDiba . (A. [But this I have not found elsewhere; and I almost think that A$Ev , in my copy of the A, may be a mistranscription for $E~v ; and gaDiba , for gaD~a .])

5 see 1, in six places. -A2- ta$aE~uvN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The act of taking; syn. A^axo*N ; (K, TA;) and so ↓ . (TA.) One says, t$E~vhu Ald~ahoru (assumed tropical:) Time, or fortune, took him. (TA.) And t$E~v maAlahu He took his property. (TK.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The eating little of food; (K, TA;) and so ↓ : whence one says, $aE~avotu mina AlT~aEaAmi I ate little of the food. (TA.)

(tropical:) [ May God rectify, or repair, and consolidate, what is discomposed, deranged, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled, of thy, and your, affairs ; (see art. lm ;) or] consolidate thy, and your, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled, state of affairs: (S, A: * [in the latter expressly distinguished as tropical:]) [and so ↓ , and $aEovakumo ; perhaps by poetic license; for] Kaab Ibn-Málik El-Ansáree says, lam~a A@loA_il`hu bihK $aEovFA waram~a bihi A^umuwra A^um~atihi waAlA^amoru munota$iru (assumed tropical:) [ God rectified and consolidated, by him, a discomposed, deranged, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled, state of affairs, and repaired, by him, the affairs of his people,

, applied to hair, Shaggy, or dishevelled: (MA:) [or shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy, or altered in odour, in consequence of its being seldom dressed: (see 1, first sentence:)] or defiled with dust, and matted, or compacted, in consequence of its being seldom anointed. (Msb.) And in a similar sense applied to the head of a misowaAk [or tooth-stick, meaning (assumed tropical:) Disintegrated

; or rendered brushy; by its being bruised, &c.; and so as applied to the head of a wooden peg or stake; as indicated by an explanation of its verb]. (MA.) [And in the TA it is applied to a plant, as meaning (assumed tropical:) Straggling. ] See also A^a$oEavu . ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) A man dirty in the body. (Msb.)
A place of [or in ] the hair that is $aEiv [or shaggy, or dishevelled, &c.]. (TA.)
, and $aEovaAnu Alr~aA^osi : see what next follows.

, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and A^a$oEavu Alr~aA^osi , (K,) and ↓ , (Mgh, TA,) [and $aEivu Alr~aA^osi ,] and ↓ , (TA,) and $aEovaAnu Alr~aA^osi , (K,) applied to a man, (A, Mgh, Msb,) Having the hair shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy, or altered in odour, in consequence of its being seldom dressed: (Mgh:) or having the hair defiled with dust, and matted, or compacted, in consequence of its being seldom anointed: (Msb:) or having the head dusty, (S, A, K, TA,) and the hair plucked, and unanointed: (TA:) fem. of the first $aEovaA='u , applied to a woman: (A, Msb:) and $uEovN [is its pl., and] is applied to horses, as meaning [ having shaggy coats, ] not curried: (S:) or dusty by reason of long journeying. senses.text: 1 , (A, Msb,) inf. n. $aEowa*apN , (A, L, Msb, K,) He practised the art termed $aEowa*ap , expl. below: (A, L, Msb, K:) as also $aEoba*a , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $aEoba*apN : (A, Msb, K:) so some say. (Msb.) [See what here follows.]

Legerdemain, or sleight-of-hand, (A, L, K,) and false miracles, (TA,) and fascinations, (K,) or fascination, (A, L,) or a kind of play, (Msb,) like siHor , (A, L, Msb, K,) making a thing to appear different from what it really is, (L, K,) or showing a man what has no real existence: (Msb:) or making what is false to assume the form of what is true: (TA:) as also $aEoba*apN : (A, Msb:) vulgarly termed $aEobavapN . (TA.) ― -b2- Also Quickness: or lightness, or agility, in any affair. (L.) ― -b3- It is not a word of the language of the people of the desert. (Lth, L, Msb.)

A messenger of princes or governors, (L, K,) who journeys on affairs of importance for them (L) upon post-horses or other beasts appointed for their conveyance: (L, K:) so called because of his quickness. (L.) It is not a word of the language of the people of the desert. (Lth, L.) ― -b2- See also what follows.
and mu$aEowa*N A man who practises the art termed $aEowa*ap ; (L, K;) as also ↓ : (TA in art. Ejb :) improperly called mu$aEobi*N , and surnamed A^abuw AlEajabi . (Eth-Tha'álibee, TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) and $aEura bihi , (K,) which latter is disallowed by some, but both are correct, though the former is the [more] chaste, (TA,) aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. $iEorN (S, Msb, K, &c.) and $aEorN (K, TA) and $aEarN , (TA, and so in the CK in the place of $aEorN ,) but the first is the most common, (TA,) and $iEorapN (Msb, K) and $aEorapN and $uEorapN , (K,) of which last three the first is the most common, (TA,) and $iEoraY and $uEoraY (K) and $aEoraY (TA) and $uEuwrN (Msb, K) and $uEuwrapN , (K,) which is said to be the inf. n. of $aEura , (TA,) and ma$oEuwrN and ma$oEuwrapN (Lh, K) and ma$oEuwraA='u , (K,) which is of extr. form, (TA,) He knew it; knew, or had knowledge, of it; was cognizant of it

; or understood it; (S, * A, Msb, K, TA;) as also $aEara lahu : (Lh, TA:) or he knew the minute particulars of it: or he perceived it by means of [ any of ] the senses. (TA.) Lh mentions the phrase A^a$oEuru fulaAnFA maA Eamilahu and A^a$oEuru lifulaAnK maA Eamilahu [ I know what such a one did or has done ], and maA $aEarotu fulaAnFA maA Eamilahu [ I knew not what such a one did ], as on the authority of Ks, and says that they are forms of speech used by the Arabs. (TA.) [See also $iEorN , below.] ― -b2- $aEara , (A, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $iEorN and $aEorN , (K, TA,) or $aEarN , (so accord. to the CK instead of $aEorN ,) He said, or spoke, or gave utterance to, poetry; spoke in verse; poetized

; or versified; syn. qaAla $iEorFA ; [for poetry was always spoken by the Arabs in the classical times; and seldom written, if written at all, until after the life-time of the author;] (A, Msb, K;) as also $aEura : (K:) or the latter signifies he made good, or excellent, poetry or verses; (K, MF;) and this is the signification more commonly approved, as being more agreeable with analogy: (MF:) or the latter signifies he was, or became, a poet; (S;) as also $aEira , aor. . (TA.) One says, $aEarotu lifulaAnK I said, or spoke, poetry, &c., to such a one. (TS, O, TA.) And lawo $aEura binaqoSihi lamaA $aEara [ Had he known his deficiency, he had not spoken poetry, or versified ]. (A.) -A2- $aAEarahu fa$aEarahu : see
3. -A3- $aEara as a trans. verb syn. with A$Er : see
4. ― -b2- As syn. with $AEr : see

3. -A4- $aEira , aor. , (K,) inf. n. $aEarN , (TA,) His (a man's, TA) hair became abundant (K, TA) and long: (TA:) and said likewise of a goat, or other hairy animal, his hair became abundant. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) He possessed slaves. (Lh, K.)
2 as an intrans. verb: see 4: ― -b2- and as a trans. verb also: see
3 ↓ , (S, K,) aor. of the latter , that is with fet-h, (S, MF,) accord. to Ks, who holds it to be thus even in this case, where superiority is signified, on account of the faucial letter

; or, accord. to most, , agreeably with the general rule; (MF;) He vied, or contended, with him in poetry, and he surpassed him therein. (S, K, MF.) -A2- And $AErhu , (S,) and $AErhA , (A, Msb, K,) and ↓ , (A, K,) He slept with him, and with her, ( naAwamahu , S, and naAma maEahaA , Msb, K, or DaAjaEahaA , A,) in one $iEaAr [or innermost garment ]. (S, A, Msb, K.) -A3- [Reiske, as mentioned by Freytag, explains $AEr as signifying also Tractavit, prensavit, vellicavit: but without naming any authority.]

4 He made him to know. (S.) You say, A$Erhu biAlA^amori and AlA^amora , (K,) the latter of which is less usual than the former, because one says $aEara bihi but not $aEarahu , (MF,) He aquainted him with the affair; made him to know it. (K.) And A^a$oEarotu A^amora falaAnK I made known the affair of such a one. (A.) And A^a$oEarotu fulaAnFA I made such a one notorious for an evil deed or quality. (A.) ― -b2-

A_i$oEaArN , Msb,) He marked it, namely a beast destined for sacrifice at Mekkeh, (S, * Mgh, Msb, * K, TA,) by stabbing it in the right side of its hump so that blood flowed from it, (S,) or by making a slit in its skin, (K,) or by stabbing it (K, TA) in one side of its hump with a miboDaE or the like, (TA,) so that the blood appeared, (K, TA,) or by making an incision in its hump so that the blood flowed, (Msb,) in order that it might be known to be destined for sacrifice. (S, Msb.) ― -b3- [

Hence, app.,] (assumed tropical:) He wounded him so as to cause blood to come. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting the assassination of 'Othmán, A^a$oEarahu mi$oqaSFA (assumed tropical:) He wounded him so as to cause blood to come with a m$qS [q. v.]: (TA:) and in another trad., A^a$oEira A^amiyru Almuw^ominiyna (assumed tropical:) [ The Prince of the Faithful was wounded so that blood came from him ]. (S.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) He pierced him with a spear so as to make the spearhead enter his inside: and A$Erhu sinaAnFA (tropical:) he made the spear-head to enter into the midst of him: [but this is said to be] from A$Erhu bihi “ he made it to cleave to it. ” (TA.) A^a$oEira is said specially of a king, meaning He was slain. (A, TA.) ― -b5- Also He made it to be a distinguishing sign:

and ↓ , (A, Msb, K, but only the latter in my copies of the S and in the O,) two wellknown dial. vars., the like being common in cases of this kind, in which the medial radical letter is a faucial, (MF,) [but the latter I have found to be the more common,] Hair; i. e. what grows upon the body, that is not Suwf nor wabar ; (K;) it is an appertenance of human beings and of other animals: (S, A, Msb:) [when spoken of as used in the fabrication of cloth for tents &c., the meaning intended is goats' hair: (see

[an inf. n., (see 1, first sentence,) and used as a simple subst. signifying] Knowledge; cognizance: (K, TA:) or knowledge of the minute particulars of things: or perception by means of [ any of ] the senses. Would that I knew what such a one did, or has done; (S, * K, * Msb, * TA;) for would that my knowledge were present at, or comprehending, what such a one did, or has done; the phrase being elliptical: (TA:) accord. to Sb, layota $iEoriY is for lyt $iEoratiY , the p being elided as in huwa A^abuw Eu*orihaA [for hw Abw Eu*oratihaA ], (S, TA,) the elision of the p in this latter instance, as Sb says, being peculia

: see A^a$oEaru . ― -b2- [The fem.] $aEirapN signifies [particularly] A sheep or goat ( $aApN ) having hair growing between the two halves of its hoof, which in consequence bleed: or having an itching in its knees, (K, TA,) and therefore always scratching with them. (TA.)
and $aEarapN ns. un. of $aEorN [q. v.] and $aEarN .

The hair of the pubes; (T, Msb, K;) as also ↓ , [accord. to general analogy with tenween,] or ↓ , [and if so, without tenween,] accord to different copies of the K; (TA;) of a man and of a woman; and of the hinder part of a woman: (T, Msb:) or the hair of the pubes of a woman, specially: (S, O, Msb:) and the pubes ( EaAnap ) [ itself ]: (K:) and the place of growth of the hair beneath the navel. [ The star Sirius; ] a certain bright star, also called Almirozamu ; (TA; [but see this latter appellation;]) the star that rises [ aurorally ] after AljawozaA=' [by which is here meant Gemini ], in the time of intense heat, (S, TA,) and after AlhaqoEap [app. a mistranscription for AlhanoEap ]: (TA:) [about the epoch of the Flight, it rose aurorally, in Central Arabia, on the 13th of July, O. S.: (see Aln~avorapu ; and see also manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl :) on the periods of its rising at sunset, and setting aurorally, see dabarN and dabuwrN :] the Arabs say, A_i*aA TalaEati Al$~iEoraY jaEala SaAHibu Aln~axoli yaraY [ When Sirius rises aurorally, the owner of the palm-trees begins to see what their fruit will be]: (TA:) there are two stars of this name; Al$~iEoraY AlEabuwru and Al$~i
fem. of A^a$oEaru [q. v.: under which head it is also mentioned either as a subst. or as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant]. ― -b2- See also $iEorapN .

[ Of, or relating to, poetry; poetical. ― -b2- And also (assumed tropical:) False, or lying ]. Sirius. ] You say, raEayonaA $iEoriY~a AlmaraAEiY We pastured our cattle upon the herbage of which the growth was consequent upon the nawo' [i. e. the auroral rising or setting ] of Al$~iEoraY [or Sirius ]. The young ones of the raxam [i. e. vultur percnopterus ]. (K.)

: see A^a$oEaru . ― -b2- $aEoraAn [app. without tenween, being probably originally an epithet, also] signifies (assumed tropical:) The [ shrub called ] rimov , (K,) or a species thereof, (Tekmileh, TA,) green, inclining to dust-colour: (Tekmileh, K, TA:) or a species of [ the kind of plants called ] HamoD , dust-coloured: (TA:) or HamoD upon which hares feed, and in which they [ make their forms, i. e.] lie, cleaving to the ground; it is like the large A^u$onaAnap [here app. used as the n. un. of A^u$onaAnN , i. e. kali, or glasswort ], has slender twigs, and appears from afar black. (AHn, TA.)
[ A poetaster ]: see $aAEirN . -A2-

(TA.) (Fr, Akh, S, TA.) And A^aSobaHato $aEaAriyra biqirodaHomapa , and biqiro*aHomapa , and biqinodaHorapa and biqid~aHorapa , and biqi*
: see A^a$oEaru . -A2- A^aronabN $aEoraAniy~apN A hare that feeds upon the $aEoraAn [q. v.], and that [ makes its form therein, i. e.] lies therein, cleaving to the ground. (AHn, TA.)

(tropical:) Trees; (ISk, Er-Riyáshee, S, A, K;) as also ↓ : (As, ISh, K:) or tangled, or luxuriant, or abundant and dense, trees; (T, K;) as also ↓ : (Sh, T, K:) or (TA, but in the K “ and ”) trees in land that is soft (K, TA) and depressed, between eminences, (TA,) where people alight, (K, TA,) such as is termed dahonaA=' , and the like, (TA,) warming themselves thereby in winter, and shading themselves thereby in summer, as also ↓ : (K, TA:) or this last signifies any place in which are a xamar [or covert of trees, &c.,] and [ other ] trees; and its pl. is ma$aAEiru . (TA.) One says, A^aroDN kaviyrapu Al$~aEaAri (assumed tropical:) A land abounding in trees [&c.]. (S.) ― -b2- See also the next paragraph, latter half.

(Msb) a call or cry, (A, Mgh, Msb,) by means of which to know one another: (S, A, Mgh, Msb:) and the $iEaAr of soldiers is a sign that is set up in order that a man may thereby know his companions: (TA:) and $iEaAr signifies also the banners, or standards, of tribes. senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. $ufuwfN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and $afiyfN (S, O, K) and $afafN , (CK, [but not in my MS. copy of the K nor in the TA,]) It (a garment, or piece of cloth,) was thin, fine, or delicate, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) so that what was behind it was visible, (S, * IB, Mgh, [for xalaqahu in some copies of the S, and xalofahu in others, I read maA xalofahu , which is the right reading accord. to IB and the TA, agreeably with the reading in the Mgh, which is maA waraA='ahu ,]) or so as to tell what was beneath it: (O, K:) [and it, (a gem, or the like,) was translucent: or was transparent. (See $af~aAfN .)] One says, $af~a Ealayohi vawobuhu His garment was thin, &c., upon him. (S.) ― -b2- ― -b3- And $af~a jisomuhu , aor. , inf. n. $ufuwfN , His body became lean, or emaciated. (S, O, K.) -A2
; or was, or became, redundant. (S, O, Msb, K.)

Hence, in a trad., $af~a naHowFA mino daAniqK It exceeded by about a dAnq . (Sh, O.) And one says, $af~a Ealayoh , aor. ya$uf~u , [so in the L and TA, contr. to rule, probably a mistranscription for ya$if~u ,] inf. n. $ufuwfN ; and ↓ , and ↓ ; [app. meaning, as seems to be indicated by the context, It exceeded it: ] and $afifotu fiY Als~iloEapi [app. a mistranscription for $afafotu ] I gained in, or upon, the the article of merchandise: (TA: [and so, app., ↓ : see $af~aY :]) and fY tijaAratihi ↓ [ He obtained what is termed $if~N in his traffic; i. e.] he made gain, or profit, in his traffic; syn. rabiHa . (S and K in art. rbH .) ― -b2- And sometimes (Msb) it signifies also the contr.; i. e. It fell short

; or was, or became, deficient. (Msb, K.) One says, (O, Msb,) of a dirhem, (O,) h`*aA ya$if~u qaliylFA This falls short, or is deficient, a little. (O, Msb.) And $af~a Eanohu Alv~awobu , aor. , The garment was too short for him. (TA.) -A3- Also $af~a , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) It (a thing, O) was, or became, in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation. (O, K.) -A4- And $af~a laka Al$~aYo'u i. q. daAma and vabata [app. meaning The thing belonged, or pertained, to thee permanently, or constantly

; or may the thing belong, &c.]. (TA.) -A5- $af~ahu , (S, M, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. $af~N (S, M, TA) and $ufuwfN , (M, TA,) It (anxiety) rendered him lean, or emaciated; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ ; (S;) both are also expl. as meaning it rendered him lean, or lank in the belly, so that he became slender: (TA:) or, accord. to the M, it (grief, and love,) pained his heart: or rendered him lean, or emaciated: or deprived him of his reason: and it is said of grief as meaning it manifested what he felt of impatience. (TA.) And $af~a Aln~ufuwsa , as used in a verse of Towbeh Ibn-El- Homeiyir, It hurt and melted the souls. (Ham p.
594.) -A6- See also 8, in two places.
2 see the preceding paragraph, in two places.

4 I preferred them, or judged them to excel. (K.) You say, A^a$ofafotu baEoDa waladiY EalaY baEoDK I preferred some of my children above some. (S. [And the like is said in the Mgh.]) And A^a$ofafotu h`*aA EalaY h`*aA I preferred this above this. (Msb.) ― -b2- And A$f~ fulaAnN Ald~irohama Such a one made the dirhem to exceed: or, made it to fall short. (TA.) -A2- A^a$af~a Ealayohi [if not a mistranscription for A^u$if~a , which I rather think it to be,] He excelled him, or surpassed him. (TA.) -A3- A^a$af~a Alfamu The mouth had in it a fetid odour. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.)
6 I took away his or its, $if~ , i. e. excess, or redundance. (O, K.) ― -b2- See also the next paragraph, in three places.

8 (S, O, K) kul~ahu (K) He drank what was in the vessel, all of it, (S, O, K,) even the $ufaAfap [or last drop or remains ], (O,) not leaving any of it remaining; (S;) [and so Aijotaf~a ;] as also ↓ : (S, O, K:) and ↓ AlmaA='a He drank the water to the uttermost, not leaving any of it remaining; as also ↓ , aor. , inf. n. $af~N : and AlmaA='a ↓ I drank much of the water without having my thirst satisfied. (TA.) [Hence,] in the trad. of Umm-Zara, waA_ino $ariba A@$otaf~a [ And if he drank, he drank up all that was in the vessel ]. (S, O.) And it is said in a prov., ↓ (S, O, TA) i. e. The satisfying of thirst is not from the drinking up all that is in the vessel; for it is sometimes effected by less than this: (O, TA:) it is applied in forbidding one's going to the utmost in an affair, and p

10 , (O, K,) or Ast$f~ maA waraA='ahu , (S, Msb,) He saw what was behind it. (O, Msb, K.) [Thus the former signifies He saw through it: and it is used in this sense both properly and tropically.] ― -b2- Hence the saying to the seller of cloths, Aisota$if~a h`*aA Alv~awoba , [which may be rendered Look thou through this garment, or piece of cloth; but is expl. as] meaning make thou this garment, or piece of cloth, single, [ by unfolding it, ] and raise it, or hold it up, in shade, in order that I may see whether it be close in texture or flimsy. (TA.) ― -b3- Ast$f~ also signifies [agreeably with the explanation of Ast$f~ maA waraA='ahu mentioned above] (assumed tropical:) He distinguished a thing plainly, like as one distinguishes plainly a thing behind glass. (Har p.
244.) ― -b4- And one says, katabotu kitaAbFA faA@sota$af~ahu , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ I wrote a letter, or writing, &c., and ] he examined attentively what was in it. (TA.) -A2- See also

8. -A3- And see 1, in two places. -A4- [Freytag mentions as a signification of Ast$f~ “ Desiderio alicujus rei implevit; ” with AlY before the object: but he names no authority for this; and I doubt its correctness.]
1 : see 1, latter part. ― -b2-

Also, accord. to IAar, (O, TA,) inf. n. $afo$afapN , (K, TA,) It (heat, and cold,) dried it up; namely, a thing, (O, K, TA,) such as herbage, (O, TA,) &c. (TA.) And accord. to AA, Al$~afo$afapu signifies The hoar-frost's burning [meaning blasting ] the herbage of the earth: or the burning of a medicament that is sprinkled upon a wound: (O:) or it has the former of these two meanings, and signifies also the sprinkling of a medicament upon a wound. (K. [But I think that, for wa*ar~u Ald~awaA='i in the K, we should read wa*ar~i Ald~awaA='i , and thus reconcile the K in this case with the O: see, however, what next follows; which may be regarded either as confirming the reading in the K, or as having misled its author, in this instance.]) -A2- Al$~afo$afapu signifies also The sprinkling of uri
2 , said of herbage, It began to dry up. (TA.)

A thin, fine, or delicate, garment or piece of cloth; (AZ, S, Mgh, O, * Msb, K; *) as also ↓ (AZ, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ : (Msb:) you say vawobN $af~N (S, Mgh, Msb) and ↓ (S, Msb) and ↓ . (Msb:) [see also $af~aAfN :] and the garment, or piece of cloth, itself, is termed $af~N and ↓ : (Har p. 70:) [i. e. each of these words is also used as a subst.; and this is perhaps meant in the O and K: or] $af~N signifies also a certain thin, fine, or delicate, veil or covering: or, accord. to Aboo-Nasr, a certain thin, fine, or delicate, veil or covering, of wool, through which one sees what is behind it: (S:) pl. $ufuwfN . (O, Msb, K.) Among the verses of “ the Book ” [of Sb, cited as exs. therein], is the following: lalobosu EabaA='apK wataqar~u EayoniY A^aHab~u A_ilaY~a mino lubosi Al$~ufuwfi [ Verily
: see $af~N , in three places. -A2-

Also, (S, Mgh, O, K,) and ↓ , (L, K,) but the former is that which is well known, (L, TA,) and ↓ , (TA,) Gain, or profit; increase obtained in traffic: and excess, surplus, or redundance: syn. riboHN [q. v.] : and faDolN ; (S, Mgh, O, K;) and ziyaAdapN . (Mgh, TA.) Hence (Mgh) nahaY Eano $if~i maA lam yuDomano , meaning [ He (the Prophet, TA) forbade ] the riboH [i. e. gain, or profit, of that for which one has not made himself responsible to the purchaser]. (O, Mgh.) And one says, lih`*aA EalaY h`*aA $if~q [ There is, or pertains, to this, an excess above this ]. (Ksh in ii.

15.) And qaAla qawolFA $if~FA He said a saying that was a redundance. (TA.) ― -b2- And A deficiency: thus having two contr. meanings. (ISk and S and O in explanation of the first word, K in explanation of the first and second words, and TA in explanation of all.) ― -b3-

Also, the first word, i. q. mahonaA^N : one says to a person when regarding him with a wish for the like of a thing that he has attained, or that he possesses, without desiring that it should pass away from him, $if~N laka yaA fulaAnu [ May it be an unalloyed gratification to thee, O such a one ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And A thing that is little, or small, in quantity; mean, or paltry. (TA.) [See also $afiyfN , last signification.]

: see $afiyfN , last signification. -A2- Also i. q. xif~apN [ Lightness, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- And sometimes it signifies Evilness, or narrowness of the circumstances, ( riq~ap ,) of one's state, or condition. (TA.)
: see $ufaAfapN .

: see $af~N , in two places: -A2- and see $if~N . -A3- Also Cold, as a subst.; (ISk, S, O, Msb;) thus in the saying, wajada fiY A^asonaAnihi $afiyfFA [ He felt, or experienced, in his teeth, cold ]; (S, O;) and so ↓ : (ISk, Msb:) or, as some say, (O,) the hurting, or paining, ( la*oE , [in the CK ladog ,] of cold: (S, O, K:) and intense cold, with rain and wind; and $ifaAfN is its pl.: (TA:) or intense cold [alone]: (Msb:) or a cold wind in which is moisture: (O:) and ↓ signifies the cold of a wind in which is moisture: (S:) or $afiyfN has this last signification; and ↓ , the signification next preceding it: one says, lahaA ↓ $afiyfN A cold and moist wind, having [much] cold and moisture, made him to betake himself to a covert: (IDrd, IF, Msb:) or $afiyfN signifies rain and hail: (O:) or s

A portion of water remaining in a vessel; (S, O, K;) and likewise, of milk: (TA:) or the last drop remaining in a vessel: (Ham p. 239:) IAth says that some of the later writers mention it as being with s . (TA.) Dhu-rRummeh uses the phrase Al$~afaA ↓ , in a verse, as meaning In the remaining portion of the day. (O.)

Extremely [or very ] thin or fine or delicate, so that a thing behind it is visible: (KL:) [ translucent: ] transparent: applied to a gem, or the like; and to a garment, or piece of cloth. (TA.) [See also $af~N .]
: see $afiyfN , in six places.
A garment, or piece of cloth, not well or strongly or compactly [ woven or] made. (O, K.) -A2- See also $afiyfN .
Vehement thirst. (O, K.)

[a noun denoting excess]. It is said in a trad. of Ráfi', fakaAna AlxaloxaAlu A^a$af~a minohaA qaliylFA , meaning [ And the anklet, or pair of anklets, was ] more than they [ in value or weight ]; (syn. A^afoDal and A^azoyad ;) i. e. more [in value or weight] than the dirhems. (Mgh.) And one says, fulaAnN A^a$af~u mino fulaAnK , meaning Such a one is a little greater, or older, ( A^akobaru qaliylFA ,) than such a one. (TA.)
is said by Ibn-Buzurj to be like majofuwfN [part. n. of jaf~ahu ; i. e. Collected
; or collected together and taken away ]. (TA.)

(O, K) and ↓ , (K,) the latter on the authority of IAar, (TA,) Slender, shallow, or weak, in intellect, and evil in disposition. (O, K.) And [both words agreeably with different explanations of the verb] One in whom is, (K,) or, accord. to Saad, one who is as though there were in him, (O,) a trembling, and confusion, (O, K,) resulting from jealousy, (K,) or from vehement jealousy, (O,) and solicitous affection, or pity or compassion, for his Huram [or wives, or women under covert, and household, (in the CK his Haram ,)] as though jealousy wasted his heart, and made him lank and lean: or evil in disposition, and very jealous: and ↓ the latter word, solicitously affectionate
; or pitying, or compassionating. (TA.)
: see the next preceding paragraph, in two places.

senses.text: 1 The primary signification of [the inf. n.] $fr [i. e. $aforN , of which the verb is app. $afara ,] is The act of cutting, or cutting off; syn. qaToEN . (Ham p.

57.) -A2- $afarahaA , (K,) inf. n. $aforN , (TA,) He struck her (a woman's) $ufor (K, TA) in compressing her. (TA.) ― -b2- And $afara [or app. $afara A_inosaAnFA ] He annoyed, molested, harmed, or hurt, a man. (IAar, O, TA.) -A3- $afirato , aor. , inf. n. $afaArapN , She (a woman) was one whose gratification of her venereal lust ( $ahowatuhaA ) soon took place: (K:) or she emitted; [or, app., emitted soon; ] syn. A^anozalato . (TA.) -A4- And $afira , aor. , It decreased, diminished, or became defective or deficient. (IAar, K.)

2 , (K,) inf. n. ta$ofiyrN , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) He compressed her (i. e. a woman, Ibn-'Abbád, O) on the $ufor of her faroj . (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) ― -b2- And $af~arotu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. as above, I eradicated, or extirpated, the thing. (TA.) -A2- $f~r AlmaAlu , (O, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) The property became little: (O, K:) and went away: (K:) from IAar. (TA.) ― -b2- And $f~r said of a man, He gave little. (Ham p.

242.) ― -b3- And $f~rt Al$~amosu (O, K) liloguruwbi (O) (assumed tropical:) The sun became near to setting; (O, K;) being likened to a man whose property has become little, and gone away. (TA.) ― -b4- And in like manner, (TA,) $f~r EalaY A^amorK (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K) and liA^amorK , (Ibn-'Abbád, O,) said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, on the brink, or verge, of the affair, or event, or case. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)
4 is said in the Tekmileh to signify He (a camel) strove, or exerted himself, in running: but perhaps it should be A$gr , mentioned before [in art. $gr ]. (TA.)
: see the next paragraph, in four places.

The place of growth of the eyelash, (Sh, T, S, A, Msb, K,) which is the edge of the eyelid; (S, Msb;) as also ↓ (Kr, A, K) and ↓ : (K:) or, accord. to some, this last signifies the upper side of the inner angle of the eye: (TA:) and with the vulgar, the first signifies the eyelash; but this is [said to be] a mistake: (IKt, Msb:) it occurs, however, in this sense, in a trad. of Esh-Shaabee; (IAth, TA;) and in like manner the pl. occurs in another trad.; but the word $aEar should be considered as understood before it

; or what grows is thus called by the name of the places of growth, and the like of this is not rare: (Mgh:) it is of the masc. gender: (Lh, K:) and the pl. is A^a$ofaArN , (Sb, S, Mgh, Msb,) the only pl. form. (Sb, TA.) [Hence,] one says, ↓ , (Ks, Fr, T, S, Msb, K,) and $uforN , (Lh, Msb, K,) but Sh disallows this latter, (TA,) and ↓ , (Fr, Sgh, K,) (tropical:) There is not in the house any one: (S, Msb, K, &c.:) and maA raA^ayotu ↓ (tropical:) I saw not of them any one: from the $fr of the eye: meaning one having a $fr : (A:) and $fr is also used in this sense without a negation. (TA.) One says likewise, maA tarakati Als~anapu ZuforFA walaA $uforFA (tropical:) The year of drought left not anything: and sometimes they said ↓ , with fet-h, and in this case they said ZaforFA , for assimilat

Also, (S A, Mgh, Msb, K,) and ↓ , (S, A, Msb, K,) The edge, border, margin, brink, brow, (S, Mgh, Msb,) or side, (A, K,) of anything; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as of a valley and the like, (S,) or as of a river &c.: (Mgh and Msb, in relation to the latter word:) one says, Aln~ahori ↓ , and Albiy^ori , and Alqabori , They sat upon the side of the river, and of the well, and of the grave: (A:) and both words signify the side of the upper part of a valley. (K.) ― -b3- And Al$~uforu , (K,) or $uforu Alfaroji , (Msb,) and $uforu AlmaroA^api , (TA,) The edge, (Msb, K,) or border, (TA,) of the vulva, or external portion of the organs of generation, [meaning, of each of the labia majora, ] of a woman: (Msb, K, TA:) pl. A^a$ofaArN : (Msb:) the A_isokataAni are the two sides [or labia majora] of the vulv

[an epithet of which the fem. only is mentioned]. $afirapN and ↓ signify A woman who experiences the gratification of her venereal lust ( $ahowatahaA ) in her $ufor ; so that she emits ( tunozilu ) speedily: or [in the CK “ and ”] who is content with the least of coitus: (K, TA:) contr. of qaEirapN and qaEiyrapN . (TA.)

A large knife; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ , though this is mentioned only by the author of the Mgh; (MF; [but it is not in my copy of the Mgh; and Golius mentions ↓ as having this signification, on the authority of Meyd;]) or a broad knife: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. $ifaArN (Msb, K) and $afaraAtN (Msb) and [coll. gen. n., of which $iforapN is the n. un., or it may be a quasi-pl. n. of $aforapN ,] ↓ . (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (Mgh, TA,) (tropical:) A servant; (S, Mgh, TA;) because of his utility. (TA.) It is said in a prov., A^aSogaru Alqawomi $aforatuhumo (tropical:) The least of the party is their servant. (S, Mgh.) ― -b3- Also A shoemaker's knife. (S, K.) ― -b4- And A piece of iron made broad, and edged, or pointed. (K.) ― -b5- A broad blade: so says the author of the Mgh. (TA. [But not in my copy of the

A jerboa having hair upon its ears: (S:) or having large ears: or having long ears, and bare toes, [in the CK, for AlEaAriY AlbaraAvini , which is evidently the right reading, we find AlEAlY AlbrAvn ,] not quickly overtaken: (K:) it is [ of ] a species of jerboa called DaA^onu AlyaraAbiyEi , the fattest and the best, with ears somewhat long: (TA:) or having long legs, and soft and fat flesh: (K:) it is said that it has a nail in the middle of its shank. (TA. [See tadomuriY~N .]) ― -b2- Dab~N $ufaAriY~N A long and bulky [ lizard of the kind called ] Db~ . (Ham p.

242.) ― -b3- A^u*unN $ufaAriy~apN (as also $uraAfiy~apN [q. v.], TA) A large ear: (K:) or a bulky ear: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or a long ear: (AZ, TA:) or a broad ear, soft in the upper part: (TA:) or an ear having much hair and fur. (Ham p.
The possessor of a $aforap [or large knife ]. (A, * TA.)
, and its dual: see $uforN , last sentence, in three places. -A2- Also One who destroys, or makes away with, his property: so in the Tekmileh. (TA.)

The lip of a camel; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ : (K:) and (tropical:) of a horse: (S, TA:) and (tropical:) of a human being: (K, TA:) or (tropical:) of an Abyssinian, as being likened to that of a camel: (A'Obeyd, TA:) pl. ma$aAfiru . (S, K.) It is said in a prov., A^araAka ba$arN maA A^aHaAra mi$ofarN [lit. External skin hath shown thee what a lip hath transmitted to the stomach; ] meaning, the external appearance hath rendered thee in no need of inquiring respecting the internal state: (S, K:) originally said of a camel; (TA;) for when you see his external skin, whether he be fat or lean, you take it as an indication of the quality of his food. (K, TA.) ― -b2- Also The vulva, or external portion of the organs of generation, of a woman: (R, MF:) but this is strange. (TA.) ― -b3- And (tro
Strait, scanty, subsistence. (O, K.)

senses.text: A tray ( TabaqN ) on which are small saucers, or cups, fayoxaAt and sukur~ajaAt : (O, K:) a Pers. word, (S, O,) arabicized; (S, O, K;) from biy$obaArajo or biy$obaArijo (K, TA) or biy$aArajo ; (as in some copies of the K;) or what people call biy$obaAriajo : (Yaakoob, S:) [i. e. Piy$o PaAro or Piy$o PaAraho , “ pésh pár, ” and “ pésh párah, ” meaning “ sweetmeats presented to a guest: ”] accord. to ElJawáleekee, it signifies different kinds of flesh-meat in TbAyx : [but what this means I know not: I suppose it to be a corruption of some word signifying saucers or the like:] in the “ Kitáb el-Moheet, ” $afaAriyju is said to be pl. of $ufaArijN , signifying a kind of food. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $afoEN , (S, Msb,) He made it to be a $afoE ; (S, K, TA;) meaning (TA) he made it (a single thing) to be a zawoj [i. e. he made it to be one of a pair or couple; and sometimes, he made it to be a pair or couple together ]: (Mgh, TA:) or he adjoined it to, or coupled it with, that which was a single thing: (Msb:) accord. to Er-Rághib, Al$~afoEu signifies the adjoining a thing to its like. (TA.) You say, kaAna witorFA fa$afaEotuhu , (S,) or kaAna witorFA fa$afaEotuhu biA=xara i. e. [ It was a single thing, and ] I made it to be one of a pair, or couple, with another. (Mgh. [In Har p. 194, I find the phrase bA=xr ↓ , expl. in like manner; but $f~Eh thus used I do not find in any lexicon: it may, however, be correctly thus used; for t$f~E , which

Hence, in a trad., ↓ [ Intercede thou: thou shalt have thine intercession accepted ]. (TA.) The saying in the Kur [ii. 117], walaA tanofaEuhaA $afaAEapN [ Nor shall intercession profit it ] means that it shall have no $aAfiE [or intercessor] for his $afaAEap [or intercession] to profit it; being a denial of the $aAfiE ; (Ibn- 'Arafeh, O, K;) and the same is the case in the Kur lxxiv. 49, (Ibn-'Arafeh, O, TA,) and xx.

108. (TA.) $afaEa , inf. n. $afoEN and $afaAEapN , also signifies He prayed, or supplicated: and thus Mbr and Th explain the words of the Kur [ii. 256], mano *aA A@l~a*iY ya$ofaEu Einodahu A_il~aA biA_i*onihi [ Who is he that shall pray, or supplicate, in his presence, except by his permission? ]. ; or becoming convalescent: ― -b2- and then, Medical, or curative, treatment: (TA:) the giving of health; (KL:) inf. n. of $afaAhu [q. v.]: (S, Msb, TA:) ― -b3- and [then], (TA,) A medicine, or remedy: pl. A^a$ofiyapN , and pl. pl. A^a$aAfK . (K, TA.) [
Hence, daAru Al$ifaA='i The hospital. ] ― -b4- [And hence,] one says, $ifaA='u AlEiY~i Als~uw^aAlu (tropical:) [ The remedy of inability is the asking information ]. (TA.)
: see art. $fh .
: see art. $fh .
: see art. $fh .
[ Recovering, or restoring to convalescence; remedial; ] health-giving. (KL.) ― -b2- [
Hence, jawaAbN $aAfK (assumed tropical:) An answer that relieves from doubt. ]
More [and most remedial or] healthgiving. (KL.) -A2- Also A man whose lips do not close together: fem. $afoyaA='u . (TA.) See A^a$ofahu , in art. $fh .

An instrument for perforating; (K;) a thing pertaining to the makers or sewers of boots or shoes or sandals &c.; (S;) [i. e.] the awl used by them: (MA, KL:) and the instrument with which leather, or skin, is sewed: (Mgh, K:) or, accord. to ISk, it is [ an instrument used ] for water-skins and water-bags and the like; and the mixoSaf is for sandals: (S:) [see also art. A$f :] masc. and fem.: (K, * TA:) pl. A^a$aAfK . (Mgh, TA.) ― -b2- Th mentions the saying, A_ino laATamotahu laATamota AlA_i$ofaY [ if thou contend with him in slapping, thou wilt do so with the A$fY ]; meaning that when one does so, it will be against himself. (TA.) ― -b3- And A_i$ofaY Almirofaqi , a phrase used by a poet, means (assumed tropical:) Sharp in the elbow. (TA.)
