senses.text: 1 , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. $aq~N , (S, M, Msb,) He cut it [or divided it ] lengthwise; (TA in art. qd ;) [i. e.] he clave it, split it, rived or rifted it, or slit it; so as to separate it; [i. e. he clave, split, rived or rifted, slit, rent, ripped, tore, broke, or burst, it asunder; ] or without separating it; [i. e. he cracked, chapped, incided or incised, gashed, slashed, furrowed, or trenched, it
; or clave, split, &c., or cut, it open; ] syn. SadaEahu ; (K;) or [more explicitly] Al$~aq~u signifies AlS~adoEu AlbaAy^inu [ the cleaving &c. that separates ]
; or gayoru AlbaAy^ini [ that which does not separate ]

; or AlS~adoEu [ the cleaving, &c.,] in a general sense: (M:) and in like manner, [but with an intensive signification, or implying frequency or repetition of the action, or its application to several objects, generally meaning he clave it, &c., much, or in pieces, or in several places, ] ↓ : (M, K:) you say, $q~q AlHaTaba (S, K) wagayorahu (S) i. e. $aq~ahu [but properly meaning He clave in pieces the firewood &c. ]. (K. [In the CK, $aq~a AlHaTaba is erroneously put for $q~q AlHTb .]) ― -b2- [ $aq~a raA^osahu generally means He clave his head, or his pericranium: and sometimes, as in an instance in the K voce $aqaA^a , he divided the hair of his head. ] ― -b3- $aq~a AlEaSaA [lit. He split the staff ] means (tropical:) he separated himself from the community; (S, K, TA;) and particularly,

; or the cattle are divided &c.;] means we are equal in respect of the property, or cattle: for the Ablmp means the [kind of leaf called] xuwSap , which, when it is split lengthwise, splits in halves: (M:) or, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, the Ablmp is a herb, or leguminous plant, ( baqolapN ,) to which there come forth pods, like [those of] the bean; and when you split them lengthwise, they split in halves, equally, from the first part to the last thereof: $aq~a is in the accus. case as an inf. n., ma$oquwqN being understood. (Har p.

639.) [See also $iq~N .] ― -b6- $aq~a , (S, M, K,) aor. , inf. n. $uquwqN , (M,) said of the canine tooth of a camel, (tropical:) It [ clave the gum and ] came forth: (S, M, K, TA:) [said to be] a dial. var. of $aqaA^a : (S:) and said of the canine tooth of a child, (M, TA,) in like manner, (TA,) meaning it made its first appearance: (M:) and said also of a plant, [as meaning it came forth ] on the ground's first cleaving open from it. (M, TA.) ― -b7-
Also, aor. , inf. n. $aq~N , said of the dawn, (tropical:) It rose; as though it clave the place of its rising and came forth therefrom. (TA.) ― -b8-

Also, aor. , (TA,) inf. n. $aq~N , said of lightning, (tropical:) It [ clave the clouds, and ] extended high, into the midst of the sky, without going to the right and left: (K, TA:) so says A'Obeyd: (TA: [see $aqiyqN :]) and ↓ and ↓ , said of lightning, signify AinoEaq~a [probably meaning the same; (see EaqiyqapN ;) or, as expl. in the S and also in the O, in art. Eq , it was, or became, in a state of commotion, ( taDar~aba ,) in the clouds ]: (M, TA:) or ↓ said of lightning means it spread wide and long. (JK.) ― -b9- $aq~a Als~abiyla (K in art. Ebr ) (assumed tropical:) He passed along the way; as though he cut it, or furrowed it. (TK in that art.) And $aq~a Aln~ahora (assumed tropical:) He crossed the river by swimming. (TA in art. qTE .) ― -b10- $aq~a AlmaA='a (assumed tropical:) He op
; or ceased from speaking; but sometimes, and perhaps in this case, he articulated speech, or the speech: compare a signification of
2.]. (M and L in art. qd .) ― -b13- See also

2 see 1, first sentence. ― -b2- $q~q AlkalaAma , (S, K, TA,) inf. n. ta$oqiyqN , (TA,) (tropical:) He uttered, or pronounced, speech, or the speech, in the best manner: (S, K, TA:) and he sought with repeated efforts, in speaking, to utter, or pronounce, the speech in the best manner. (TA.)
3 , (M, Mgh, Msb,) inf. n. mu$aAq~apN (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and $iqaAqN , (S, M, Msb, K,) the latter inf. n. occurring in the Kur ii.

39 [&c.], (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He acted with him contrariously, or adversely, (S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and inimically; (K;) properly, each of them doing to the other that which was distressing, grievous, or troublesome, so that each of them was in a $iq~ [or side ] other than that of his fellow; (Msb;) or as though he became in a $iq~ , i. e. side, in respect of him: (Mgh:) accord. to Er-Rághib, the inf. n. signifies the being in a $iq~ [or side ] other than that of one's fellow: or it is from $aq~u AlEaSaA bayonaka wabayona SaAHibika [meaning “ the effecting disunion and dissension between thee and thy fellow ”], so that it is tropical: (TA:) or the primary meaning of Al$~iqaAqu is the being [ mutually ] remote. (Ham p.
326.) See also 1, in the first quarter of the paragraph.
4 The palm-trees put forth their $awaAq~ , pl. of $aAq~apN [q. v.]: mentioned by Th, on the authority of some one or more of the BenooSuwáäh. (M.)

5 quasi-pass. of 2: (S, M, K:) said of firewood (S, K) &c. (S) [as meaning It became cloven in pieces ]. See 7, in two places. ― -b2- Said of lightning: see 1, in two places, in the latter half of the paragraph. ― -b3- Said of a horse, (tropical:) He was, or became, lean, or light of flesh; slender and lean
; or lean, and lank in the belly. (A'Obeyd, TA.)

6 , said of two adversaries, or litigants, as also ↓ , They wrangled, quarrelled, or contended, each with the other, (M, TA,) and took to the right and left in contention; (TA;) fiY Al$~aYo'i [ in respect of the thing ]. (M.)

7 quasi-pass. of $aq~ahu as expl. in the first sentence of this art.: [i. e. it signifies It became divided lengthwise, cloven, split, riven or rifted, slit, rent, ripped, torn, broken, or burst, asunder
; or it became cracked, chapped, incided or incised, gashed, slashed, furrowed, or trenched

; or cloven, or split, &c., or cut, open: or it clave, split, &c.:] (S, M:) and in like manner, ↓ is quasi-pass. of $aq~aqahu : [i. e. it signifies it became cloven or split &c., or it clave or split &c., much, or in pieces, or in several or many places: ] (M:) or the former signifies [sometimes] it opened so as to have in it an interstice. (Msb.) waA@no$aq~a Alqamaru , in the Kur liv. I, means And the moon hath been cloven (Bd, Jel) in twain, (Jel,) as a sign to the Prophet: (Bd, Jel:) or shall be cloven on the day of resurrection: but the former is confirmed by another reading, waqadi A^ono$aq~a Alqamaru : (Bd:) or, accord. to Er-Rághib, the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) the case hath become manifest. (TA.) One says, An$q~ Al$~aYo'u biniSofayoni [ The thing became cloven, &c., in halve

8.] ― -b2- [Hence,] An$q~ flaAnN mina AlgaDabi (assumed tropical:) Such a one was as though his interior were filled with anger so that he split. (TA.) ― -b3- And Aino$aq~ati AlEaSaA (assumed tropical:) The affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disordered: (S, K, TA:) and An$q~t AlEaSaA biAlbayoni , and ↓ , (Lth, M, TA,) (assumed tropical:) the affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disorganized, by separation: (Lth, TA:) and An$q~ AlA^amoru (assumed tropical:) the affair, or state of affairs, became discomposed, deranged, or disorganized, being incongruous, or inconsistent. (M, TA.) And An$q~t EaSaA AlT~aAEapi (assumed tropical:) [ The compact of allegiance, or obedience, became broken ]. (M.) ― -b4- An$q~ said of lightning: see 1, in the lat

8 signifies The taking the $iq~ of a thing, (S, K,) i. e. the half thereof. (S.) One says, A$tq~ Al$~aYo'a He took the $iq~ [or half ] of the thing. (TK.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) The taking [or deriving ] a word from a word, (S, K,) with the condition of reciprocal relation in meaning and [ radical ] composition, and of reciprocal difference in form: [and it is of three kinds:] AlAi$otiqaAqu AlS~agiyru is that derivation in which there is a reciprocal relation between the two words in the letters and in the order [ thereof ]; as in Daraba from AlD~arobu : AlA$tqAq Alkabiyru is that in which there is a reciprocal relation between the two words as to the letter and the meaning, exclusively of the order; as in jaba*a from Alja*obu : AlA$tqAq AlA^akobaru is that in which there is a reci

8 in art. xrE ,)] The constructing, or founding, ( bunoyaAn ,) of a thing of, or from, what is originated without premeditation. (M.) ― -b4- And (tropical:) The taking to the right and left, (S, K, TA,) not pursuing the right, or direct, course, (S, TA,) in speech, and in contention, or disputation, or litigation: (S, K, TA:) or Ai$otiqaAqu AlkalaAmi signifies the taking to the right and left in speech: (so in a copy of the M: [but I think that the right reading is AlAi$otiqaAqu fiY AlkalaAmi , agreeably with what here follows:]) you say, A$tq~ fiY AlkalaAmi , and fiY AlxuSuwmapi . (TK.) See also

6. And [in like manner] one says of a horse, A$tq~ fiY Eadowihi (assumed tropical:) He went to the right and left in his running. (M. [See also A^a$aq~u .]) ― -b5- A$tq~ AlT~ariyqu fiY AlfalaApi (tropical:) The road went [or branched off ] into the desert. (TA. [See also

10 He turned the sack upon one of his two sides ( EalaY A^aHadi $iq~ayohi ), in order to pass through a door. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Ast$q~ , as stated by Freytag, is expl. by Jac. Schultens, but on what authority is not said, as signifying “ Prodiit, manifestus evasit. ”]

1 , (JK, S, K,) inf. n. $aqo$aqapN , (S,) said of a stallion [camel], He brayed [ in his $iqo$iqap , or faucial bag ]. (JK, S, K.) [It is said that] the primary meaning of $aqo$aqapN is Loudness of voice

; or the being loud in voice. (JK.) ― -b2- And said of a sparrow, It uttered a cry: (K, TA:) or one says of a sparrow, yu$aqo$iqu fiY Sawotihi [app. meaning It makes a loud twittering in its cry ]. (S.)

sing. of $uquwqN ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) originally an inf. n.; (S, Msb;) An opening forming an interstice in a thing: (Msb:) or a fissure, cleft, chink, split, slit, rent, crack, or the like, syn. SadoEN , in wood or a stick, or in a wall, or in a glass vessel [&c.]: (T, TA:) [or] a place that is ma$oquwq [i. e. cloven or cleft, split, &c.: (see 1, first sentence: and see also ma$aq~N :) and often signifying an incision, a gash, or a furrow, or trench ]: (M, K:) as though an inf. n. used as a subst. in this sense: pl. as above, $uquwqN : (M:) it differs from $uqaAqN , (S, Mgh,) by having a general signification: (Mgh:) accord. to Yaakoob, one says, biyadi fulaAnK $uquwqN (S, Mgh) and birijolihi (S) [i. e. In the hand, or arm, of such a one are cracks, or the like, and in his foot, or leg ]: b

The half (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a thing (S, Msb, K) of any kind; as also ↓ : (K:) or the half of a thing when it is cloven, or split, or divided lengthwise; (M;) as also ↓ . (AHn, S, * M, K.) One says, A^axa*otu $iq~a Al$~aApi and ↓ Al$~aApi I took the half of the sheep or goat: (S, TA:) the vulgar pronounce the $ with fet-h. (TA.) And xu*o h`*aA Al$~iq~a Take thou this ↓ [i. e. half ] of the sheep or goat. (TA.) Hence the trad., taSad~aquwA walawo bi$iq~i tamorapK i. e. [ Give ye alms though it be but] the half of a date; meaning deem not anything little that is given as alms. (TA.) And AlmaAlu bayoniY wabayonaka $iq~a Al$~aEarapi and Al$~aEarapi ↓ , (O, K, * [in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K $q~u , but the former reading appears to be the right, $aq~a being an inf. n. as in a similar s

; or because Eve was created from Adam. (TA.) ― -b8- And (tropical:) A man's brother; (M;) and so ↓ ; (S, M, O, K, TA;) meaning a brother by the father and mother; (TA;) from $aqiyqN as meaning “ either half of a thing that is cloven in halves; ” (S, TA;) or as though the relationship of one were cloven from that of the other: (IDrd, O, K:) pl. of the latter A^a$iq~aA='u . (M, Msb.) ― -b9- And a name for A thing at which one looks: (Lth, O, K:) [but this is app. taken from the following saying of Lth, in which I think Al$~iq~u is a mistranscription for Al$~aq~u , meaning “ the crack, ” &c.:] Al$~aq~u is the inf. n. of $aqaqotu , and Al$~iq~u is a name for that at which one looks [i. e. for the visible effect of the act signified by the verb], and the pl. is Al$~uquwqu [which is well known
Hence, in the Kur [xvi. 7], lamo takuwnuwA baAligiyhi A_il~aA bi$iqi A@loA^anofusi [ Which ye would not reach save with difficulty, or distress, &c., of the souls ]; where some read ↓ . (S, * TA.)

primarily signifies The half of a garment [ consisting of two oblong pieces sewed together, side by side ]: then it was applied to [ such ] a garment as it is [ when complete: in both of these senses it is used in the present day]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or a piece ( qiToEapN ) of a garment: (Mgh:) or the $uq~ap of viyaAb [thus, and thus only, in the S, meaning of garments and of cloths, for it is of both,] is an oblong piece; syn. sabiybapN musotaTiylapN : (M, K:) [it is often applied to an oblong piece of cloth of those pieces of which a tent is composed: ] pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN . (M, Mgh, TA.) One says, fulaAnN yabiyEu $iqaAqa Alkat~aAni [ Such a one sells pieces, or oblong pieces, &c., of linen ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also A piece of a mazaAdap [q. v.]. (B, TA in art. bSr .) ― -b3- And A piece, or

816.) ― -b4- And A far journey; as also ↓ , (S, M, K,) sometimes thus pronounced with kesr: (S:) a far, long journey: a far-extending space: (TA:) or a road difficult to him who travels it: (Mgh:) or [simply] a journey: and i. q. vnyA [so in my copy of the Msb, app. a mistranscription for vaniy~ap , i. e. a mountain-road, &c.]: pl. $uqaqN . (Msb.) ― -b5- And A part, region, quarter, or tract, (Ibn-'Arafeh, Er-Rághib, K, TA,) towards which one draws near, (Ibn-'Arafeh, TA,) or towards which the traveller directs himself, (K, TA,) [like $uk~apN ,] or in the reaching of which one is overtaken by difficulty, or distress; (Er-Rághib, TA;) And ↓ signifies the same. (K.) ― -b6- And Distance; and so ↓ . (K.) ― -b7- See also $iq~N , last sentence but one.

A splinter (S, K) that splits off, (S,) or a piece (M, Mgh, TA) split off, (M, TA,) of a plank, (S, M, K, TA,) or of wood, (TA,) or of a piece of wood, (S, Mgh,) or other thing: (M, TA:) a piece split, or divided, lengthwise, of a staff, or stick, and of a garment, or piece of cloth, &c.: (IDrd, O, K:) and a piece split (K, TA) from anything; such as the half: (TA:) pl. $iqaqN . (O, TA.) One says of him who is angry, AiHotad~a faTaArato minohu $iq~apN fiY AlA^aroDi wa$iq~apN fiY Als~amaA='i (assumed tropical:) [ He became excited by sharpness of temper, or angriness, and he was as though a bit flew from him upon the ground, and a bit into the sky ]. (S, * M, TA: in the S, fY AlArD &c. is omitted.) See also $iq~N , first three sentences. ― -b2- See also $uq~apN , in four places. ― -b3- And
The quality, in a horse, (M, K,) and in a man, (M,) denoted by the epithet A^a$aq~u [q. v.]. (M, K.)
[a pl. of which the sing. is not mentioned] Enemies. (TA.)

A cracking in several places, ( ta$aq~uqN , S, K,) or cracks, (Mgh,) or a certain disease occasioning cracks, (M,) in the pasterns of horses or the like, (S, M, Mgh, K,) and in their hoofs, (M, Mgh,) and sometimes rising to their shanks: so says Yaakoob: (S:) and, accord. to Lth, (Mgh,) and Az, (TA,) a cracking in several places ( ta$aq~uqN ) of the skin, from cold or some other cause, in the hands or arms, and the face: (Mgh, TA:) or it signifies also any crack, or slit, in the skin, from disease: (M, TA:) As says that it is in the hand or arm, and the foot or leg, of a human being, and in the fore leg and kind leg of an animal: (Mgh, TA:) but this is inconsistent with what is said by Yaakoob [as stated voce $aq~N , first sentence]. (Mgh.) See also A^asoEadu : and $arajN .

: see $iq~N , in five places. ― -b2- $aqiyqu Albaroqi [so in a copy of the M, but the right reading may be $aqiyqapu Albaroqi , which occurs in the next sentence of the M,] i. q. Eaqiyqatuhu [expl. in the S, in art. xfw , as meaning Lightning that cleaves the clouds, and extends high, into the midst of the sky, without going to the right and left: but see $aqiyqapN ]. (M.) -A2- Also A calf that has become firm, or strong: (O, K:) and applied likewise to (assumed tropical:) a man [ that has become so; by way of comparison]: (O:) or a bull such as is termed ja*aEN [i. e. in his second, or third, year ]. (JK.)

A certain bird; also called ↓ : (M, K:) and ↓ is the dim. thereof: (K:) AHát says, the ↓ is a very little thing, grayish ( zurayoqaA='u ), of the colour of ashes; ten and fifteen of what are thus called congregate; and I think it to be the ↓ , which is a dux~alap of the dux~al [q. v.]; it is somewhat dusky; and its form is the form of these, but it is smaller than they: it is called ↓ becanse of its smallness: IDrd, in the class of fuEayoEil , mentions ↓ as signifying a certain species of birds [app. as a coll. gen. n., of which the n. un. is with p ]. (O, TA.)

[accord. to Golius, A fissure; as from the KL; but not so expl. in my copy of that work. ― -b2- ] An intervening space or tract between two elongated, or extended, tracts of sand, (S, M, * O, K, * [in the last of which Aljabalayoni is erroneously put for Aljabolayoni ,]) thus expl. to AHn by an Arab of the desert, (TA,) producing herbage: (S, M, O, K:) or a rugged tract between two elongated, or extended, tracts of sand, producing good herbage; (M, TA;) so in the T, as expl. to its author by an Arab of the desert: (TA:) pl. $aqaAy^iqu , (T, S, O, K, TA,) expl. by some as meaning sands themselves: (TA:) or a great piece of sand: or a piece of sand between two pieces thereof. (Ham p.

282.) ― -b3- [In the A and TA voce qiT~u , it is used as meaning A slice cut off of a melon &c.] -A2- A rain, (M,) or a violent rain, consisting of large drops, (K, TA,) wide in extent: so called because the clouds cleave asunder from it: (M, K, TA:) pl. as above. (TA.) ― -b2- The pl., $aqaAy^iqu , is expl. by Az as signifying Clouds that have cloven asunder with copious rains. (O, TA.) ― -b3- $aqiyqapu baroqKi , (O, K,) and Eaqiyqatuhu , both as expl. by Aboo-Sa'eed, (O,) A flash of lightning that has spread (O, K) in the horizon, (O,) or from the horizon: (K: [but see $aqiyqu Albaroqi :]) or $aqiyqapN signifies a flash of lightning that has spread in the breadth of the clouds, and filled the sky: pl. as above. (Ham p.

557.) -A3- A headache, (JK, T, TA,) or a pain, (S, O, K,) or a certain disease, (M,) in the half of the head, (JK, T, S, M, O, K,) [i. e. hemicrania, ] and of the face: (JK, T, S, O, K:) or, accord. to IAth, a sort of headache in the fore part of the head and towards the sides thereof. (TA.) -A4- $aqaAy^iqu Aln~uEomaAni , used alike as sing. and pl., (S, O, K,) having no proper sing., (Msb,) or its sing. is $aqiyqapN ; (M, O, Msb;) [The red, or blood-coloured, anemone; ] a certain plant; (M;) a certain red flower; (Lth, O;) well known; (S, K;) the $aqir ; (Msb;) or, as AHn says, on the authority of AA and Aboo-Nasr and others, it is the $aqirap [n. un. of $aqirN ]; and the sing. of $qAy^q is $aqiyqapN : (O, TA:) it is called $qAy^q AlnEmAn because of its redness, as being likened to the $a
, and with p : see $aquwqapN , in four places.
, meaning One who glories, or boasts, vainly, and praises himself for that which is not in him, is not of the [classical] language of the Arabs. (L, TA.)
A horse with which his rider ex- periences difficulty in striving to master him. (JK.)
A certain mode of jimaAE , (K, TA,) in which the woman lies upon her $iq~ [or side ]. (TA.)

[The bursa faucium, or faucial bag, which is placed behind the palate of the he-camel, and which, when excited, he inflates, and blows out from the side of his mouth; ] a thing resembling the lungs, or lights, which the he-camel protrudes from his mouth when he is excited by lust; (S, O, K;) a skin in the fauces of the Arabian camel, which he inflates with wind, and in which he brays; whereupon it appears from the side of his mouth; so says En-Nadr; and he adds that it does not pertain to any but the Arabian camel, [as is said in the M, and] as Hr says; but this requires consideration; (TA;) [also expl. as] the lahaAp [q. v.] of the he-camel, (M, and Har p. 16,) which he protrudes from his mouth when he brays: (Har ubi suprá:) pl. $aqaA$iqu . (TA.) ― -b2- To this is likened the tongue of t

an appellation applied to a certain xuTobap [i. e. oration, or harangue, or sermon,] of 'Alee, because of his saying to Ibn- 'Abbás, (O, K,) on his having cut short his speech, (O,) in reply to a remark of the latter person upon his not having continued his speech uninterruptedly, tiloka $iqo$iqapN hadarato vum~a qar~ato [ That was a $q$qp that uttered a braying, then became still ]. 5. -A2- $akala Alfarasa biAl$~ikaAli , (S,) or $akala Ald~aAb~apa , (Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. $akolN , (Msb,) He bound [ the horse or] the beast, with the $ikaAl ; (Msb;) [i. e.] he bound the legs of [ the horse or] the beast with the rope called $ikaAl ; as also ↓ , (K,) inf. n. ta$okiylN . (TA.) And $akalotu AlT~aAy^ira [app. I bound the legs of the bird in like manner ]. (S.) And $akalotu Eani AlbaEiyri I bound the camel's $ikaAl between the fore girth and the hind girth; (S;) [i. e.] I put [or extended ], between the hind girth and the fore girth of the camel, a cord, or string, called $ikaAl , and then bound it, in order that the hind girth might not become [ too ] near to the sheath of the penis. (TA in art. Hqb .) ― -b2- And [hence, i. e.] from the $ikaAl of the beast, (TA,) $akala A

; or such gesture, or behaviour, with coquettish boldness, and feigned coyness or opposition; displayed what is termed $ikol , i. e. gunoj and dal~ and gazal ; (K, TA;) and ↓ [signifies the same], i. e. tadal~alato [and in like manner t$k~l is said of a man]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also $akalN below, in two places. ― -b3- And $akilotu A_ilaY ka*aA , with kesr [to the k ], i. q. rakanotu [i. e. I inclined to such a thing
; or trusted to, or relied upon, it, so as to be, or become, easy, or quiet, in mind ]. (O.)
2 , as an intrans. verb: see 4: ― -b2- and see also
5. -A2- $k~lhu , inf. n. ta$okiylN , He formed, fashioned, figured, shaped, sculptured, or pictured, it; syn. Saw~arahu ; (K, TA;) namely, a thing. (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, in three places.

3 signifies The being conformable, suitable, agreeable, similar, homogeneous, or congenial; syn. muwaAfaqapN ; (S, K;) as also ↓ : (IDrd, S, K:) Er-Rághib [strangely] says that Almu$aAkalapu is from Al$~akolu signifying “ the binding, ” or “ shackling, ” a beast [with the $ikaAl ]. (TA.) You say, huwa yu$aAkiluhu [ He, or it, is conformable, &c., with him, or it
; or resembles him, or it ]. (Msb.) And h`*aA AlA^amoru laA yu$aAkiluka i. e. laA yuwaAfiquka [ This affair will not be suitable to thee ]. (TA.) And ↓ They resembled each other. (MA.)

4 [primarily] signifies SaAra *aA $akolK [meaning It, or he, was, or became, such as had a likeness or resemblance, or a like, or match, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, app.,] said of a thing, or case, or an affair; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ , (O, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, $akila , evidently not meant by the author of the K, as it is his rule, after mentioning a verb of this form, to add kafariHa or the like,]) inf. n. $akolN ; (TA;) and ↓ , (K,) inf. n. ta$okiylN ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, dubious, or confused; syn. Ailotabasa , (S, O, Msb, K,) and AixotalaTa , (O, TA,) or Ai$otabaha : (Mgh:) [and ↓ is mentioned in this sense by Golius as on the authority of J (whom I do not find to have mentioned it either in this art. or elsewhere), and by Freytag as on the

5 It (a thing, TA) was, or became, formed, fashioned, figured, shaped, sculptured, or pictured; syn. taSaw~ara . (K, TA.) ― -b2- And He became goodly in shape, form, or aspect. (TK in art. Trz .) ― -b3- t$k~l AlEinabu , (S, K,) and ↓ , and ↓ , (K,) The grapes became in that state in which some of them were ripe: (S, K:) or became black, and beginning to be ripe: (K:) thus in the M. (TA.) ― -b4- See also 4, near the end. ― -b5- And see 1, also near the end.
6 see 3, in two places.
10 is often used by the learned in the present day as meaning He deemed it (i. e. a word or phrase or sentence) dubious, or confused. ]

i. q. $abapN [as meaning A likeness, resemblance, or semblance; a well-known signification of the latter word, but one which I do not find unequivocally assigned to it in its proper art. in any of the lexicons]. (AA, K, TA. [In the CK, and in my MS. copy of the K, in the place of Al$~abahu as the first explanation of Al$~akolu in the K accord. to the TA, we find Al$~ibohu ; but that the explanation which I have given is correct, is shown by what here follows.]) One says, fiY fulaAnK $akolN mino A^abiyhi , meaning $abahN [i. e. In such a one is a likeness, or resemblance, of his father ]: (AA, TA:) and mino A^abiyhi ↓ and ↓ (AA, O, K, TA) and ↓ , (O, K, TA,) [likewise] meaning $abahN , (AA, O, K, TA,) and mu$aAbahapN : (TK:) and ↓ also is syn. with $akolN [in the sense of $abahN ]; (K, TA;)

; or by several boundaries, as in those bodies that have several angles or sides, such as have four and such as have six [&c.]: so says Ibn-El-Kemál: (TA:) pl. [of pauc., in this and in other senses,] A^a$okaAlN and [of mult.] $ukuwlN . (K.) ― -b4- [It often means A kind, sort, or variety, of animals, plants, food, &c.] ― -b5- [And The likeness, or the way or manner, of the actions of a person:] it is said in a trad. respecting the description of the Prophet, saA^alotu A^abiY Eano $akolihi , meaning [ I asked my father respecting the likeness of his actions, or] respecting what was like his actions; accord. to IAmb: or, accord. to Az, respecting his particular way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct: (O:) and ↓ [likewise, and more commonly,] signifies a particular way, course,

; or fit, or proper, for one: you say, h`*aA mino hawaAYa wamino $akoliY [ This is of what is loved by me and of what is suitable to me ]: (K, TA:) and layosa $akoluhu mino $akoliY [ What is suitable to him is not of what is suitable to me ]. (TA.) [And hence, app.,] one says, maA$akoliY wa$akoluhu , meaning What is my case and [what is] his, or its, case? because of his, or its, remoteness from me. (T and TA voce A^um~N .) ― -b7- And sing. of A^a$okaAlN (L, K, TA) signifying Discordant affairs and objects of want, concerning things on account of which one imposes upon himself difficulty and for which one is anxious: (Lth, TA:) and dubious, or confused, affairs: (TA:) or discordant, and dubious, or confused, affairs. (K. [In the CK, Almu$ak~alap is erroneously put for Almu$okilap .]) -A2-
: see the next preceding paragraph, latter part, in two places. -A2-
Also, as an attribute of a woman, Amorous gesture or behaviour

; or such gesture, or behaviour, combined with coquettish boldness, and feigned coyness or opposition; syn. dal~N , (S, O, Msb, K,) and gunojN , and gazalN ; (K; [in the CK, gazol , which is a mistranscription;]) or her gunoj , and comely or pleasing dal~ , whereby a woman renders herself comely or pleasing; (TA;) and ↓ signifies the same. (K.) One says AimoraA^apN *aAtu $ikolK [ A woman having amorous gesture or behaviour; &c.]. (S, O, Msb.)

, in a sheep or goat, The quality of being white in the $aAkilap . (S, O. [See A^a$okalu .]) [In this sense, accord. to the TK, an inf. n., of which the verb is ↓ , said of a ram &c.]. ― -b2- And in an eye, The quality of having what is termed $ukolap [q. v.]. (S, O.) [Accord. to the TK, in this sense also an inf. n., of which the verb is ↓ , said of a thing, as meaning It had a redness in its whiteness. ]

: see $akolN , first signification. ― -b2- One says also, fiyhi $ukolapN mino sumorapK [ In him, or it, is an admixture of a tawny, or brownish, colour ], and $ukolapN mino sawaAdK [ an admixture of blackness ]: (TA:) [or] $ukolapN signifies redness mixed with whiteness: (Sh, Msb, TA:) in camels, (K, TA,) and in sheep or goats, (TA,) blackness mixed with redness, (K, TA,) or with dust-colour: in the hyena, accord. to IAar, a colour in which are blackness and an ugly yellowness: (TA:) in the eye, a redness in the white: (Mgh:) or, in the eye, i. q. $uholapN [q. v.]: (K:) or, accord. to AO, (TA,) the like of a redness in the white of the eye; (S, O, TA;) and such was in the eyes of the Prophet; (O;) but if in the black of the eye, it is termed $uholapN : (S, O, TA:) and the like is in the ey
A woman using, or displaying, what is termed $ikol , i. e. gunoj and dal~ and gazal [meaning amorous gesture or behaviour, &c.], (K, TA,) in a comely, or pleasing, manner. (TA.)

fem. of A^a$okalu [q. v.]. (S, O.) -A2- Also A want; syn. HaAjapN ; and so ↓ , (S, O, K, [both of these words twice mentioned in this sense in the K,]) and ↓ ; this last and the second on the authority of IAar; (O;) accord. to Er-Rághib, such as binds, or shackles, ( tuqay~id ,) a man [ as though with a $ikaAl ]. (TA.) One says, ↓ [&c.] i. e. HaAjapN [ We have a want to be supplied to us on thy part; meaning we want a thing of thee ]. (S, O.) -A3- Also i. q. mudaAhanapN . (So in the O and TA. [But whether by this explanation be meant the inf. n., or the fem. pass. part. n., of daAhana , is not indicated. Words of the measure faEolaA='u having the meaning of an inf. n., like bagoDaA='u , are rare.])

, of which the pl. is $ukulN , (S, O, Msb, K,) the latter also pronounced $ukolN , (TA,) i. q. EiqaAlN [ A cord, or rope, with which a camel's fore shank and arm are bound together ]: (S, O:) [or, accord. to the TA, by EqAl is here meant what next follows:] a rope with which the legs of a beast ( daAb~ap ) are bound: (K:) a bond that is attached upon the fore and hind foot [or feet ] of a horse [or the like ] and of a camel: (KL:) [ hobbles for a horse or the like, having a rope extending from the shackles of the fore feet to those of the hind feet: so accord. to present usage; and so accord. to the TK, in Turkish kwstk : Fei says only,] the $ikaAl of the beast ( dAb~p ) is well known; and the pl. is as above. (Msb.) In relation to the [camel's saddle called] raHol , (K, TA,) accord. to As

Also, in a horse, (tropical:) The quality of having three legs distinguished by [ the whiteness of the lower parts which is termed ] taHojiyl , and one leg free therefrom; (S, O, K, TA;) [this whiteness] being likened to the EiqaAl termed $ikaAl : (S, O:) or having three legs free from taHojiyl , and one hind leg distinguished thereby: (S, O, K, * TA: *) accord. to A'Obeyd, it is only in the hind leg; not in the fore leg: (S, O:) or, accord. to AO, (TA,) having the whiteness of the taHojiyl in one hind leg and fore leg, on the opposite sides, (Mgh, * TA,) whether the whiteness be little or much: (TA:) [when this is the case, the horse is said to be *uw $ikaAlK mino xilaAfK : see
3 (last sentence) in art. xlf :] the Prophet disliked what is thus termed in horses. (O.)
(tropical:) Foam mixed with blood, appearing upon the bit-mouth, or mouth-piece of the bit. (Z, O, K, TA.)
: see $akolN , first signification. ― -b2- Also A whiteness between the Ei*aAr [which see, for it has various meanings,] and the ear. (Ktr, S, O. [See also $aAkilapN .])
: see $awokalapN . ― -b2- One says, AijoEali AlA^amora $awokalFA waAHidFA , meaning Make thou the affair, or case, [ uniform, or] one uniform thing. (Fr, TA in art. bA^j .)

: see $akolN , former half, in two places. -A2- Al$~aAkilapu , also, signifies The flank; syn. AlxaASirapu , i. e. AlT~afoTafapu : (S, O:) [or,] in a horse, the skin that is between the side ( EuroD ) of the xaASirap and the vafinap , (K, TA,) which latter means [the stifle-joint, i. e.] the joint of the faxi* and saAq : or as some say, the $aAkilataAni are the two exterior parts of the TafoTafataAni [or two flanks ] from the place to which the last of the ribs reaches to the edge of [ the hip-bone called ] the Haroqafap on each side of the belly. (TA.) One says, A^aSaAba $aAkilapa Alr~amiy~api , meaning [ He hit ] the xaASirap [or flank ] of the rmy~p [or animal shot at ]. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, A^aSaAba $aAkilapa AlS~awaAbi (tropical:) [ He hit the point that he aimed at, of the thing

, (so in the O, as on the authority of IAar,) or ↓ , (so in the K,) thus says EzZejjájee, but Fr says the former, [like IAar,] (TA,) i. q. raj~aAlapN [as meaning The footmen of an army or the like]: (Fr, IAar, Ez-Zejjájee, O, K, TA:) or mayomanapN [meaning the right wing of an army]: or mayosarapN [meaning the left wing thereof]. (Ez-Zejjájee, K, TA.) ― -b2- And i. q. naAHiyopN [probably as meaning The side, region, quarter, or direction, towards which one goes; like $aAkilapN , as expl. by Akh and others, in a saying mentioned voce $akolN ]. (IAar, O, K.) -A2- Also i. q. EawosajapN [i. e. A tree of the species called Eawosaj , q. v.]. (IAar, O, K.)
: see $akolaA='u , above.

More, and most, like; syn. A^a$obapu : so in the saying, h`*aA A^a$okalu bika*aA [ This is more, or most, like to such a thing ]. (S, K. *) ― -b2- Also Of a colour in which whiteness and redness are intermixed; (S, Msb, K;) applied to blood; and, accord. to IDrd, a name for blood, because of the redness and whiteness intermixed therein; (S;) [and] applied to a man; (Msb;) or to anything: (TA:) or in which is whiteness inclining to redness and duskiness: (K:) or it signifies, with the Arabs, [ of ] two colours intermixed. (TA.) [Hence,] it is applied to water, (K, TA,) as meaning (tropical:) Mixed with blood: (TA: [see an ex. in a verse cited voce Hat~aY :]) pl. $ukolN . (K.) And the fem., $akolaA='u , is applied as an epithet to an eye, (S, K,) meaning Having in it what is termed $ukolapN

: see $akolN , first signification. ― -b2- Also i. q. lubosN [meaning (assumed tropical:) Dubiousness, or confusedness ]. (K.) -A2- See also $akolaA='u , in two places. -A3- Also A single tree of the species called A^a$okal [q. v.]. (S, K.)

, from A^a$okala in the first of the senses assigned to it above, signifies Entering among [meaning confused with ] its likes. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence, app., or] accord. to Sh, from $ukolapN meaning “ redness mixed with whiteness, ” it signifies (assumed tropical:) Dubious, or confused. (TA.) [Used as a subst.,] it has for its pl. mu$okilaAtN [and ma$aAkilu also: for] one says, huwa yafuk~u Alma$aAkila , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ He solves ] the things, or affairs, that are dubious, or confused. (TA.) ― -b3- m$kl [app. mu$okilN ], applied to a horse, means Having a whiteness in his flanks. (AA, TA in art. dEm .)
Endowed with a goodly aspect, or appearance, and form. (TA.)

A horse bound, or shackled, with the $ikaAl [q. v.]. (O, TA.) ― -b2- And (tropical:) A horse distinguished by the whiteness in the lower parts of certain of the legs which is denoted by the term $ikaAlN [q. v.]: (S, Mgh, * O, TA:) such was disliked by the Prophet. (S.) [See also muHaj~alN .] ― -b3- And (tropical:) A writing restricted [ in its meaning or pronunciation ] with the signs of the desinential syntax [ and the other syllabical signs and the diacritical points ]. (AHát, TA.)

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. $akomN , He bitted him; [namely, a horse or the like;] he put the bit ( $akiymap ) into his mouth. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence], $akama AlwaAliYa , (S, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He bribed the wAlY [i. e. prefect, or the like ]; as though he stopped his mouth with the $akiymap , (S, K, TA,) i. e. the [bit, or] iron thing of the lijaAm . (TA.) And $akama faAhu biAlA_itaAwapi i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He stopped (lit. bitted ) his mouth ] with the bribe. (TA in art. Atw .) ― -b3- And faEala fulaAnN A^amorFA fa$akamotuhu (assumed tropical:) Such a one did a thing, or performed an affair, and I settled, or established, it. (Lth, TA.) ― -b4- And $akamahu , (S, K,) aor. as above, (S,) and so the inf. n.; (K;) and ↓ ; (Th, K;) He repaid, requited, compensated, o
4 see the preceding paragraph.

(S, K, &c.) and ↓ ; (K;) of the latter, ISd says, “ I think it to be a dial. var., but I am not certain of it; ” (TA;) A repayment, requital, compensation, or recompense; (El-Umawee, A' Obeyd, S, K;) and $ukobN is a dial. var. thereof: (TA:) when the gift is initial, it is termed $ukodN : (S:) or a substitute

; or thing given, received, put, or done, by way of replacement or exchange: (Ks, TA:) and (K) a gift; (As, K, TA;) as also $ukodN ; (As, TA;) or the latter signifies a gift without compensation: (TA:) or $ukomN signifies a benefaction, bounty, or gratuity; syn. nuEomaY . (Lth, TA.)
A lion: (K:) expl. in this sense as occurring in a verse of Aboo-Sakhr El-Hudhalee: or, accord. to Skr, as there used, quickly, or soon, angry
; or violently angry. (TA.)
: see $akiymapN , in three places. ― -b2- Also The loop-shaped handles of the cooking-pot. (S, K.)

[ expl. by Golius as meaning “ Malitia indolis, contumacia, ” as on the authority of the KL, is app. a mistake for $akaAsapN , which I find expl. in the KL as signifying the “ being evil in nature, or natural disposition, ” but not $kAmp . ― -b2- Freytag explains it as meaning also Likeness; a signification of $akiymapN , also mentioned by him; but for this he names no authority, and I know of none.]

, in the lijaAm , [The bit-mouth, or mouthpiece of a pit; i. e.] the transverse piece of iron in the mouth of the horse, in which is the faA^os [q. v.]; (S, K;) as also ↓ : (S:) [see also lijaAmN , and misoHalN :] or ↓ is pl. of $akiymapN , as also $akaAy^imu and $ukumN , (K, TA,) this last with two dammehs, [but written in the CK $ukomN ,] or [rather ↓ is a coll. gen. n., and] $ukumN is said by some to be pl. of $akiymN , not of $akiymapN . (TA.) ― -b2-

Hence, [as used in phrases mentioned below,] (TA,) (tropical:) Resistance, or incompliance: (S, TA:) disdain, scorn, or disdainful and proud incompliance or refusal: and self-defence from wrong treatment: (K:) and self-magnification, pride, or haughtiness; syn. $amamN ; Als~am~u in the copies of the K being a mistake for Al$~amamu : (TA:) firmness, strength, or vehemence, of spirit; (TA, and Ham p. 140;) and evilness of nature or disposition: (Ham ibid:) strength of heart: (IAar, TA:) hardiness; courage, or courage and energy

; or determination; syn. EaAriDapN : vigorousness, strenuousness, or energy: (TA:) also [simply] nature, or natural disposition; syn. TaboEN . (K, TK: in the CK AlT~abaEu is [erroneously] put in the place of AlT~aboEu .) One says, fulaA=nN *uw $akiymapK (tropical:) Such a one is resistant, or incompliant: (S, TA:) or disdainful, or scornful; resistant, unyielding, or incompliant: one who defends himself from wrong treatment: proud: hardy: courageous: one possessing prudence or discretion, or firmness or soundness of judgment. (TA.) And fulaAnN $adiydu Al$~akiymapi , meaning [in like manner] (tropical:) Such a one is firm, strong, or vehement, of spirit; (S, TA, and Ham p. 140;) disdainful, or scornful; resistant, unyielding, or incompliant; (S, K, TA;) so says ISk: (TA:) or, as some say, o
; or perspicuity of speech with quickness, or sharpness, of intellect; and much hardiness, or courage, or courage and energy, or determination. (Ham p.

140.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) Likeness, or resemblance. (K.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) A compact, or covenant; syn. EahodN : (K, TA:) in some copies of the K, Alfahodu is erroneously put for AlEahodu . (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (K,) first pers. $akawotu , (S, Msb,) of which $akayotu is a dial. var., (K in art. $kY ,) aor. , (S, Msb,) [and of the latter ,] inf. n. $akowN , (S, Msb,) or $akowaY , (K,) or this is a simple subst., (S, Msb,) also pronounced $akowFY , (K,) and $ikaAyapN , (S, K,) with kesr, (K,) in which the Y is [said to be] substituted for w because most inf. ns. of the measure fiEaAlapN of verbs ending with an infirm radical letter are of verbs of which that letter is Y , (TA,) or this also is a simple subst., (Msb,) and $akaApN , (S, K,) or this too is a simple subst., (Msb,) and $akaAwapN , (K,) and $akiy~apN , (S, K,) is a trans. verb; (S, Msb, K;) and ↓ signifies the same; (S, K;) as also ↓ : (K:) one says, $akaA A^amorahu A_ilaY A@ll~`hi and ↓ [i. e. A$tkY A^amorahu ], and ↓ [i. e. t$k~Y A^

; or] he told to God the weakness of his condition: (TA:) and $akawotu fulaAnFA and ↓ [ I complained to such a one of his conduct to me ]; (S;) [or] $akaA fulaAnFA means he told such a one of his evil conduct to him: (TA:) and $akaA fulaAnFA A_ilaY fulaAnK He complained of such a one to such a one: (MA:) [and $akawotu A_ilayohi ka*aA I complained to him of such a thing: ] see 4: and [in like manner] A_ilayohi ka*aA ↓ He complained to him of such a thing: (MA:) and minohu ↓ [ I complained of him, or it; like $akawotuhu ]: (Msb:) Er-Rághib says, Al$ikaAyapu is The showing, or revealing, of grief, or sorrow; whence the saying in the Kur [xii. 86], A_in~amaA A^a$okuw bav~iY waHuzoniY A_ilaY A@ll~`hi [ I only show my grief and my lamentation to God ]; and in the same [lviii. 1], A_ilaY A@ll~`hi

2 , inf. n. ta$okiyapN ; and ↓ ; and ↓ ; (K;) or, accord. to Th, only this last; (TA;) The women took for themselves, or made, a $akowap [q. v.] for the churning of milk; (K, TA;) because it was little in quantity; the $kwp being small, so that only a small quantity can be churned in it: (TA:) or, as in the T, $k~Y and ↓ he took for himself, or made, a $akowap : (TA:) [or] so ↓ : (S:) and so ↓ . (IKtt, TA.) -A2- $ak~aY $aAkiyahu , inf. n. ta$okiyapN , expl. in the K as meaning kaf~a Eanohu and Tay~aba nafosahu , is a foul mistranscription: correctly, sal~aY $aAkiyahu , meaning “ He comforted his complainer, and consoled him for that which had befallen him; ” as in the Tekmileh. (TA.)
3 , inf. n. mu$aAkaApN , He complained of him, i. q. $akaAhu : or he told of his deceit, guile, or circumvention, and his vices, or faults. (TA.)

4 [ He made him, or caused him, to complain; ] he did to him that which made him, or caused him, to have need to complain of him. (S, Msb.) He increased his annoyance and complaining. (Az, K, TA.) ― -b2- And He removed, or did away with, his complaint

; or made his complaint to cease; (S, * Mgh, Msb, K;) he caused him to be pleased or contented [ and so relieved him from his complaint ]; syn. A^aEotabahu mino $akowaAhu ; (S, and Har p. 337;) i. e. A^aroDaAhu ; (Har ibid.;) and he desisted from that of which he complained: (S, * Msb:) thus it has two contr. significations. (S, K.) Hence the saying, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) in a trad., (TA,) A_ilaY rasuwli A@ll~`hi Har~a Alr~amoDaA='i ↓ fiY SiyaAminaA falamo yu$okinaA [ We complained, to the Apostle of God, of the heat of the burning ground, in our fasting, ] and he did not remove, or cause to cease, our complaint. (Mgh, * Msb, TA.) And [hence] one says, A$kY fulaAnFA mino fulaAnK , meaning He took for such a one, from such a one, what pleased or contented him [ and so relieved him from complainin

5 He expressed complaint or lamentation, pain, grief, or sorrow; syn. tawaj~aEa ; (Msb and K in art. wjE ;) he made complaint or lamentation. (MA, KL.) See 1, in four places. ― -b2- [Hence] one says, t$k~Y $aA=y^iY A^aroDa ka*aA , meaning (assumed tropical:) [ My sheep or goats ] forsook such a land, [ as though they complained of it, ] and did not go near it. (TA. [But I have substituted $aAy^iY for what is there written $AkY , an evident mistranscription.]) -A2- See also 2, in two places.

[ The sun; ] the body of the solar light, that runs its course in the firmament: (Lth, * TA:) it is fem.: (S, * Msb, K:) and has neither dual nor pl.: (Msb:) or it has a pl., [though this is not used in a pl. sense,] namely, $umuwsN , (S, K,) as though they called every part of it a $ms , like as they said mafaAriqu for maforiqN . (S.) When it is made determinate without the article Al , [as] in the name Eabodu $amosa , meaning The Servant of the Sun, (Msb, K,) i. e., of this luminous object, (Msb,) the $ms of heaven, because they used to worship it, (K,) it is imperfectly decl., (Aboo- 'Alee, Msb, K,) because it is determinate and of the fem. gender, (Aboo-'Alee, K,) or because it is a proper name and of the fem. gender and altered from Al$~amos : (Msb:) and a poet says, kal~aA wa$amosa l

Also, (K, TA,) or $amosN , (Msb,) A certain ancient idol. (Msb, K.) Accord. to Ibn-El-Kelbee, it is this that is meant by the proper name mentioned above; and if so, it is perfectly decl.: (Msb:) and some say that it is this also that is meant in the words of the poet cited above, and that he makes the word imperfectly decl. because he uses it as a proper name of the image ( AlS~uwrap ). (TA.) -A2- $amosN also signifies A kind of necklace or collar: (S, K:) or a pendant, or suspended ornament, ( miEolaAq ,) of the necklace or collar upon the neck: or the collar of a dog: (TA:) or a kind of women's ornament: of the masc. gender: (Lh, TA:) pl. $umuwsN . A certain tree, (O, K,) below the stature of a man, having knotted, or jointed, rods, and small, dark-red blossoms, smaller than the jasmine: (O:) the bees feed upon it; (O, K;) and men eat its tender extremities, being rendered healthy, or sound, thereby; ( yataSaH~aHuwna bihi ;) and it has a hot quality in the mouth; and is sweet in odour: (O:) clothes become sweet-scented by adhering to it, (O, K, * TA,) i. e. to its blossom, agreeably with what is said in the “ Book of Plants, ” not to the tree, to which the pronoun refers in the O and K; (TA;) and its honey is clear, (O, K,) very clear, and is well known: it is a pasture; and grows in the plains, and near to seed-produce. A separate, or distinct, party, or sect, (O, K, TA,) of men: this is the primary signification: so called from their agreeing together, and following one another: or, accord. to some, the Y is originally w , and it is from $uw~aEa qawomahu , which means “ he collected his people or party: ” (TA:) the followers and assistants (S, O, Msb, K) of a man: (S, O, K:) any people that have combined in, or for, an affair: (Msb, TA:) accord. to Az, persons who follow, or conform with, one another, [ though ] not all of them agreeing together: (TA:) and any assistant and partisan of a man: (O, TA:) [for] the word is applied to one and to two and to a pl. number and to the male and to the female, (K, TA,) without variation: (TA:) the pl. is $iyaEN and A^a$oyaAEN , (S, * O, Msb, K,) the latter a pl. pl.

(TA.) ― -b2- Afterwards, Al$~iyEapu became a name of A particular party [or sect ]; (Msb, K;) being predominantly applied to all who took as their friends, or lords, 'Alee and the people of his house: (K:) those who followed 'Alee, saying that he was the [ rightful ] Imám after the Apostle of God, and believing that the office of Imám should not depart from him and his descendants: (KT:) they are an innumerable people, who are innovators; the extravagant zealots among them are the Imámeeyek, who revile the Two Sheykhs [ Aboo-Bekr and 'Omar ]; and the most extravagant of them call the Two Sheykhs disbelievers: some of them rise to the pitch of [ that misbelief which is termed ] Alz~anodaqap [q. v.]. The reed-pipe of the pastor; (IAar, O, K;) the instrument with which the pastor blows; so named because he calls together the camels with it: (A, TA:) or the sound of the pastor's reed-pipe. Information, an announcement, a piece of news, a narrative, or a story, spreading

(IAar, O, K.) ― -b2- [(assumed tropical:) A thing scattered, or dispersed, or in a state of dispersion: fem. with p : pl. of the latter $awaAy^iEu ; which may also be pl. of the former applied to a rational being, like fawaArisu pl. of faArisN .] One says, jaA='ati Alxayolu $awaAy^iEa (assumed tropical:) The horsemen came scattered, or dispersed, or in a state of dispersion; as also $awaAEiYa ,

Filled; (O, K;) applied to a vessel. (K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) Very rancorous, malevolent, malicious, or spiteful; filled with baseness, meanness, or sordidness. (K, TA. senses.text: 1 , (K,) [aor. ya$iymu ,] inf. n. $ayomN , (TA,) He hid, or concealed, the thing in the thing: (K, TA:) and he inserted the thing in the thing. (TA.) [Hence,] $Am sayofahu , (K,) first pers. $imotuhu , (S,) aor. as above, (K,) inf. n. $ayomN , (TA,) He sheathed his sword; (S, K;) and [in like manner] $Am nabolahu [ He put his arrows into the quiver ]: (TA:) and the former signifies also He drew his sword: thus having two contr. meanings: (S, K:) A 'Obeyd doubted of the latter meaning; and Sh knew it not; but the verb is said to have this meaning in a verse of ElFarezdak. (TA.) It is said in a trad. of Aboo-Bekr that a complaint was made to him against Khálid Ibn-El-Weleed, and he said, laA A^a$iymu sayofFA sal~ahu A@ll~`hu EalaY Almu$orikiyna i. e. I will not sheath a sword [ which God has

319.] And $Am Als~aHaAba He looked at the clouds from afar: and [in like manner,] Aln~aAra the fire. (TA.) It is said in a prov., laA ta$imi Algayova faqado A^awodaY Aln~aqado i. e. [ Look not thou hoping for rain, for ] the lambs have perished: addressed to him who mourns for that which has past. (Meyd.) And one says, fulaAnN muwsirN walaA A^a$iymuhu mino faqorK (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one is wealthy, and I do not look at him in hope by reason of poverty ]; meaning that he is independent of him. (Z, TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] $imo maA bayonahumaA (tropical:) Compute thou, or estimate, or consider, (K, TA,) and look, or see, (TA,) what [ relation, or difference, ] is between them two. (K, TA. [In the CK, $ay~ama is erroneously put for $imo ; and qad~arahu , in the explanation, for qad~
Also, (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. $ayomN and $uyuwmN , He made a valid charge, or assault, or attack, in war, or battle. (K.) -A4-

Also, (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) He (a man) had a black raqomap [app. meaning spot, or mole, i. e. $aAmap ,] apparent in his skin. (K.) And $iyma , inf. n. $ayomN , [perhaps a mistranscription for $ayamN ,] He was marked with a $aAmap [or mole ]: or, as some say, [the pass. part. n.] ma$oyuwmN [signifying “ marked with a $Amp ”] has no verb: and AZ says that ↓ , signifying the having upon him a $Amp , has no known verb: (TA:) or $ayamN is an inf. n. signifying the having upon him $aAm [i. e. moles ]. (Ham p.

361.) -A5- $aAma fulaAnFA , (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) He soiled the legs, or feet, of such a one with dust, or earth: (K, TA:) in [some of] the copies of the K, gay~ara rijolayohi biAl$~iyaAmi ; but correctly, [as in the CK and in my MS copy of the K,] gab~ara ; and accord. to the M, from Al$~iyaAm , [meaning that the verb is derived from this word,] i. e. Alt~uraAb . (TA.)

(TA.) ― -b3- And t$y~mhu Al$~ayobu (tropical:) Hoariness came upon him, (K, TA,) and became intermixed upon him: or, accord. to IAar, became abundant upon him, and spread; (TA;) as also tasan~amahu . (IAar, M and TA in art. snm .) -A2- t$y~m A^abaAhu He resembled his father in $iymp i. e. nature, or natural disposition. (IAar, K, TA.)

(AO, TA.) ― -b3- And $iymu AlA_ibili (assumed tropical:) Such as are black, of camels: sing., masc. and fem., as above: (TA:) occurring in this sense in a verse of Aboo-Dhueyb, as related by AA: but as heard by As, in this verse, $uwmuhaA , and thought by him to be a pl. [originally $uyom ] of A^a$oyamu . (S.) See also A^a$

[See 1, of which it is an inf. n.] See also subaAtN . ― -b2- Als~abotu , (M, K,) or yawomu Als~aboti , (S, Msb,) [ The sabbath, or Saturday; ] one of the days of the week; (M, K;) the seventh of those days: (M:) so called because the creation commenced on the first day of the week and continued to [the end of] Friday, and on the sbt there was no creation, the work having ceased thereon: or, as some say, because the Jews ceased thereon from work, and the management of affairs: (M, TA:) or because the days [of the week] end thereon: (S, TA:) Az says that he errs who asserts it to have been so called because God commanded the Children of Israel to rest thereon, and that God created the heavens and the earth in six days, whereof
; or a long time

; or a space, or period, of time, whether long or short; &c.]; as also ↓ . (S, M, K.) And [hence] ↓ means (assumed tropical:) The night and the day: (S, M, K:) Ibn Ahmar says, wakun~aA wahumo kaA@bonaYo subaAtK tafar~aqaA siwFY vum~a kaAnaA munojidFA watahaAmiyaA [ And we were, with them, like the night and the day that parted asunder alike, then became one going towards Nejd and one going towards Tihámeh ]: (S, K:) such, they say, is the meaning: (S:) or, as IB says, on the authority of Aboo-Jaafar Mohammad Ibn-Habeeb, AbnA sbAt were two men, one of whom saw the other in a dream, and then one of them awoke in Nejd, and the other in Tihámeh: or they were two brothers, one of whom went to the east to see where the sun rose, and the other to the west to see where it set. (L, TA.) -A2- Also A

; or very cunning &c.; (K, TA;) silent, or lowering his eyes, looking towards the ground; (TA;) and ↓ signifies the same. (K, TA.) ― -b4- A man who sleeps much; (K;) i. e. kaviyru Als~ubaAti . (TA.) See also masobuwtN . -A4- See also what next follows.

A certain plant, resembling the xiTomiY~ [or marsh-mallow ]; (Kr, M, K;) as also ↓ , (K [there expressly said to be with fet-h],) or ↓ : (M [so written in a copy of that work]:) said to be a certain plant used for tanning. (MF.) See the next paragraph.

The hides, or skins, of oxen; (M, K;) whether tanned or not tanned: so some say: (M:) or (so accord. to the M, in the K and TA “ and, ” but the w is omitted in the CK,) any tanned hide; (As, AA, M, K;) said to be so called [because the tanning removes the hair,] from Als~abotu , “ the act of shaving: ” (AA, TA:) or such. as is tanned with qaraZ [q. v.]: (M, K:) or only ox-hides tanned: so says AHn on the authority of As and AZ: (TA:) or ox-hides tanned with qaraZ , (S, Mgh,) whereof are made [ the sandals called ] ↓ : (S) these are hence thus called: (Mgh:) they are sandals having no hair upon them: (M, Msb:) or sandals tanned with qraZ : (AA, TA:) accord. to Az, they are thus called because their hair has been shaven off ( subita , i. e. Huliqa ,) and removed by a wellknown process in tan

, (M, L, K,) like filiz~N , (TA,) [in a copy of the M erroneously written sibot ,] A certain plant; [ anethum graveolens, or dill, of the common garden-species; ] an arabicized word, from [the Pers.] $ibit~ [or $ibito ]: (AHn, M, L:) or i. q. $ibit~N ; both words arabicized from $iwi*o [or $iwido ]: (K:) asserted by some to be the same as san~uwtN [q. v.]: (M, L:) Az says that $ibit~N , the name of a well-known herb, or leguminous plant, is an arabicized word; that he had heard the people of El-Bahreyn call it sibit~N , with the unpointed s , and with t ; that it is originally, in Pers., $iwi*o ; and that it has another dial. var., namely, sbT [i. e. sibiT~N ]. (El-Jawáleekee, TA.)
: see sabotN , in the middle of the paragraph. -A2- Also Goats, collectively. (K.)

A [ desert such as is termed ] SaHoraA=' : (AZ, K:) or A^aroDN sabotaA='u is like SaHoraA='u : or a land in which are no trees: (M:) and i. q. ↓ [i. e. a bare land; as though shorn of its herbage]: (TA:) pl. sabaAtiY~u . (M.) ― -b2-
Also, [in like manner] a fem. epithet, Having spreading, or expanded, ears, whether long or short. (K.)

, and sabotiy~apN , and subotiy~apN ; and the dual. of sibotiY~N , applied to a pair of sandals: see sibotN , in four places.
, with kesr, Foolish, stupid, or of little sense; (K, TA;) confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; without understanding. (TA.)

primarily signifies Rest [like sabotN ]: (S, Msb:) and hence, sleep: (S, K:) or heavy sleep: (Msb:) or sleep that is hardly perceptible ( xafiY~ , M, K, [in some copies of the K, as mentioned by Freytag, xafiyf , i. e. light, ]), like a swoon: (M:) or the commencement of sleep in the head [ and its continuance ] until it reaches the heart: (Th, M, K:) or the sleep of one who is sick; i. e. light sleep: (TA:) and ↓ signifies the same as subaAtN . (T, TA.)

Hence, in the Kur [lxxviii. 9, and in like manner the word is used in xxv. 49], wajaEalonaA nawomakumo subaAtFA ; (S;) i. e. qaToEFA ; as though a man, when he slept, were cut off from [the rest of] mankind: (IAar, TA:) or sbAt is when one is cut off, or ceases, from motion, while the soul still remains in the body; i. e., the text means, And we have made your sleep to be rest unto you: (Zj, TA:) or we have made your sleep to be a cutting off from sensation and motion, for rest to the animal forces, and for causing their weariness to cease: or, to be death: (Bd:) or, to be rest unto your bodies by the interruption of labour, or work. (Jel.) -A2- See also sabotN , latter half, in three places.
A she-camel that goes the pace termed sabotN : or constantly going the pace termed EanaqN . (M.)

, (S, M, K,) as also sabanodFY , (S,) Bold, or daring; (S, M, K;) as an epithet applied to anything [i. e. man or brute]: the Y is added to render it quasi-coordinate to the class of quinqueliteral-radical words, not to denote the fem. gender, for it receives p as a termination [to denote the fem.], becoming sabanotaApN ; (S;) and has tenween. (TA.) A poet applies the fem. epithet to a she-camel. (S.) ― -b2- Also The leopard; (S, M, K;) so too with p ; (AHeyth, L in art. sbd ;) and so sabanodFY : probably thus called because of his boldness, or daringness: (S:) or, as some ay, the lion: fem. with p : or the fem, signifies a bold, or daring, lioness: or a she-camel of bold, or daring, breast; but this last is not of valid authority: (M:) and a beast of prey [absolutely]: (L in art. syd :) p

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. saboHN (Msb, K) and sibaAHapN , (S, * K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He swam, syn. EaAma , (S, * K,) biAln~ahori and fiyhi [ in the river ], (K,) or rather biAlmaA='i (MF, TA) or fY AlmaA='i (Msb) [i. e. in the water ], for it is likewise in the sea, and in a pool, and also in any expanse: (MF, TA:) [or he swam upon the surface, without immersing himself; for,] accord. to Z, there is a difference between EawomN and sibaAHapN ; the former signifying the “ coursing along in water with immersion of oneself; ” and the latter, the coursing along upon water without immersion of oneself. (MF, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Aln~ujuwmu tasobaHu fiY Alfalaki (A, TA) (tropical:) The stars [ swim, or glide along, or] pass along, in the firmament, with a spreading forth. (TA.) It

34 and xxxvi. 40, with reference to the sun and the moon, (Bd and Jel in xxi. 34,) with which the stars are meant to be included, (Jel ibid.,) kul~N fiY falakK yasobaHuwna , i. e. (assumed tropical:) All [ glide or] travel along swiftly, [ in a firmament, ] like the swimmer (Bd and Jel ibid.) upon the surface of the water, (Bd ibid.,) or in the water; (Jel ibid.;) wherefore the form of the verb used is that which is appropriate to rational beings, (Bd and Jel ibid.,) swimming being the act of such beings. (Bd ibid.) ― -b3- And [hence] one says, sabaHa *ikoruka Al$~amosi wa Alqamari ↓ (tropical:) [ Thy fame has travelled as far as the sun and the moon; lit., swum along the tracts along which swim the sun and the moon ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- [

Hence, likewise, as inf. n. of sabaHa , aor. as above,] saboHN also signifies (tropical:) The running of a horse (S, L, K, * TA) in which the fore legs are stretched forth well [ like as are the arms of a man in swimming ]. (L, K, * TA.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) The being quick, or swift. (MF.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) The being, or becoming, remote. (MF.) ― -b7- And (assumed tropical:) The travelling far. (K.) You say, sabaHa fiY AlA^aroDi (assumed tropical:) He went, or travelled, far, in, or into, the land, or country: (O, TA:) and sabaxa : both thus expl. by Abu-l-Jahm El-Jaafaree. (TA.) ― -b8- And (assumed tropical:) The journeying for the purpose of traffic ( taqal~ub [q. v.]); and [a people's] becoming scattered, or dispersed, in the land, or earth. (K.) And (assumed tro

2 signifies The declaring [God] to be far removed, or free, from every imperfection or impurity, or from everything derogatory from [his] glory; syn. tanoziyhN , (S, O, Msb, TA,) and taqodiysN : (Msb:) the magnifying, celebrating, lauding, or praising, and glorifying, God; and declaring Him to be far removed, or free, from everything evil. (TA.) You say, sab~aHa A@ll~`ha , (T, A, Mgh, Msb, TA,) and sb~H lil~`hi , (Kur lvii.
1 &c., and A,) in which the l is redundant, (Jel in lvii.

1 &c.,) inf. n. tasobiyHN , and suboHaAnN is a subst. that [sometimes] stands in the place of the inf. n., (T, TA,) or it is an inf. n. of which the verb is sabaHa , (K, TA,) He declared God to be far removed, or free, from every imperfection or impurity &c., (A, Mgh, TA,) or from what they say [ of Him ] who disacknowledge [ his attributes ]; (Msb;) [i. e. he declared, or celebrated, or extolled, the perfection or purity, or absolute glory, of God; ] and he magnified, celebrated, lauded, or praised, God, by the mention of his names, saying suboHaAna A@ll~`hi and the like: (Msb:) and sb~H [alone], (Mgh, K,) inf. n. tasobiyHN , (K,) he said suboHaAna A@ll~`hi ; (Mgh, K;) as also ↓ , inf. n. suboHaAnN ; (K, TA;) the latter, which is like $akara , inf. n. $ukoraAnN , a dial. var. mentioned by

73 and last verse, means Therefore declare thou the remoteness from what is unsuitable to his majesty by mentioning the name of thy Lord, or by mentioning the Lord, for the pronouncing of the name of a thing is the mentioning of it, [i. e., of the thing itself,] the great name, or the great Lord: (Bd:) or it means therefore pray thou commencing with, or uttering, the name of thy Lord [ the great name or Lord]: (Kull p. 211:) [for] ― -b2- tasobiyHN also signfies The act of praying. (K, Msb.) You say, sab~aHa meaning He prayed. (A, Mgh.) And [particularly] He performed the [ supererogatory ] prayer of [ the period termed ] AlD~uHaY . (TA.) And fulaAnN yusab~iHu A@ll~`ha , i. e. ↓ , meaning Such a one performs prayer to God, either obligatory or supererogatory: [but generally the latter: (see

is the inf. n. of sabaHa as syn. with sab~aHa [q. v.]; (K, TA;) and is a subst. that [sometimes] stands in the place of the inf. n. of the latter of these verbs, i. e. in the sense of tasobiyHN . (T, TA.) ― -b2- suboHaAna is a proper name in the sense of Alt~asobiyH , and [for this reason, and also because it ends with A and n ,] it is imperfectly decl., and is also invariable; being put in the accus. case in the manner of an inf. n. (Mgh.) You say suboHaAna A@ll~`hi , meaning I declare [or celebrate or extol ] the remoteness, or freedom, of God [ from every imperfection or impurity, or from everything derogatory from his glory, i. e.] from the imputation of there being any equal to Him, or any companion, or anything like unto Him, or anything contrary to Him

; or from everything that should not be imputed to Him: (L:) [ I declare, or celebrate, or extol, his absolute perfection or glory or purity: or extolled be his absolute perfection &c.:] or I declare the remoteness of God, or his freedom ( baraA='ap ), from evil, (Zj, * S, K, TA,) or from every evil; (TA;) and [especially] from the imputation of his having a female companion, and offspring: (K:) or I declare God's being very far removed from all the foul imputations of those who assert a plurality of gods: (MF:) [it sometimes implies wonder, and may well be rendered how far is God from every imperfection! &c.:] in this case, sbHAn is a determinate noun; (K;) i. e., a generic proper name, for Alt~asobiyH , like as bar~apu is for Albir~u . The t [says J] is not the denotative of the fem. gender: (S:) it is like that in rijaAlaAtN (S, K) and Ham~aAmaAtN , as masc. pls.: (S:) but IB says, the t in this word is the denotative of the fem. gender; for it is an epithet applied to jimaAlN , which is fem. as a [broken] pl.; as is shown by the saying AljimaAlu saArato , and raEato , &c.: and he adds, J's saying that it is like rjAlAt and Hm~AmAt is a mistake, inasmuch as he confounds rjAlAt with Hm~AmAt ; for rijaAlN is a fem. pl., as is shown by one's saying Alr~ijaAlu xarajato , and saArato ; but Ham~aAmN is masc., and should not regularly have a pl. with A and t , but, as Sb says, it has this pl. form, like some other masc. words
A proud and self-conceited gait, with an affected inclining of the body from side to side. (M, K.)
: see what next follows.

and ↓ Tall, or long. (M, K.) ― -b2- Also the former, A certain bird having a very long neck, (S, K,) which one sees always in shallow water; surnamed A^abuw AlEayozaAri . (S.) [Freytag says, on the authority of Dmr, that it is also called mAlk AlHzyn . See art. mlk .]

senses.text: 1 , aor. (S, Msb, K) and (Yoo, Msb, K) and , (Yoo, Msb,) inf. n. saboEN , (Msb,) He was, or became, the seventh of them: (S, Msb, K:) or he made them, with himself, seven: (S in art. vlv :) or it signifies, (S, and so in some copies of the K,) or signifies also, (Msb, and so in some copies of the K,) he took the seventh part of their property, or possessions. (S, Msb, K.) And He made them, they being sixty-nine, to be seventy with himself. (A 'Obeyd, S in art. vlv .) And sabaEa also signifies He made sixteen to be seventeen. (T in art. vlv .) ― -b2- sabaEotu lahu AlA^ay~aAma , aor. , inf. n. as above, I completed to him the days by making them seven: and ↓ signifies the same in an emphatic manner. (Msb.) [See also

2.] ― -b3- sabaEa AlHabola , (K,) aor. , inf. n. as above, (TA,) He made the rope, or cord, of seven strands. (K, TA.) ― -b4- subiEa Almawoluwdu The infant had its head shaven, and an animal [generally a goat] sacrificed by way of expiation for it, on the seventh day [ after its birth, (commonly called yawomu Als~ubuwEi ,) agreeably with an ordinance of Mohammad; the sacrifice being for the expiation of original sin]. (IDrd.) -A2- sabaEa Alganama He (a wolf) seized the sheep, or goats, and broke their necks, or killed them, or made them his prey, (S, K, TA,) and ate them. (TA.) ― -b2- subiEati AlwaHo$iy~apN The female wild animal had her young, or young one, eaten by the sabuE [or beast, or bird, of prey ]. (TA.) ― -b3- sabaEahu He stole it; [as though, like a sabuE , he made it his prey;]
2 , inf. n. tasobiyEN , He made it seven
; or called it seven; (S, K;) as also ↓ . (TA.) See also

1. ― -b2- He made it to have seven angles, or corners; to be heptagonal. (K.) ― -b3- He (God) gave him his reward, or recompense, seven times, or seven fold. (K.) An Arab of the desert said to a man who had done a good act to him, (TA,) sab~aEa A@ll~`hu laka May God give thee thy reward, or recompense, seven times, or seven fold. (K, TA.) The Arabs also said, sab~aEa A@ll~`hu laka A^ajorahaA May God multiply to thee the reward, or recompense, for it; meaning, for this good act: (Aboo-Sa'eed:) [for] tasobiyEN is used by them to signify the act of multiplying, though it be more than seven fold. (TA.) And sab~aEa A@ll~`hu lifulaAnK is used as meaning May God make a thing to be followed by another thing to such a one; in relation to good and to evil; as also tab~aEa lahu . (TA.) And sab~aEa A@

3 (K,) inf. n. of sAbE , (TK,) The performing of the act of coïtus, (IAar, Th, K,) with a woman. (TK.) ― -b2- The vying with another in the endeavour to surpass him in obscene, or lewd, language, and in frequency of coïtus, and in speaking plainly of such subjects as should only be alluded to, in relation to women: (IAar, K: *) such seems to be its meaning in a trad. in which the doing this is forbidden. (IAar.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Mutual reviling, vilifying, or vituperating; (K, TA;) when each of two men assails the other with foul language, such as displeases him: (TA:) this is said by some to be its meaning in the trad. in which it is forbidden. (TA.)

4 , said of a party of men, It became seven: (S, K:) also, it became seventy. (M and L in art. vlv .) ― -b2- Said of a man, it signifies He was, or became, one whose camels came to the water on the seventh day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]. (S, K.) ― -b3- AsbE liA@moraA^atihi : see

2. ― -b4- A^asobaEato She brought forth her seventh offspring. (TA in art. bkr .) ― -b5- AsbEhu : see 2, first signification. -A2- It (a road) abounded with sibaAE [or animals of prey ]. (TA.) ― -b2- AsbE Alr~uEoyaAnu The pastors had their beasts fallen upon by the sabuE [or animal of prey ]. (Yaakoob, S, K.) -A3- AsbEhu i. q. A^aToEamahu Als~abuEa [which may be rendered He gave him as food the animal of prey, or he gave him as food to the animal of prey; but it seems from what here follows that the former is meant]: (S, K:) in the “ Mufradát, ” [ he gave him as food ] the flesh of the sabuE . (TA.) -A4- He gave him, or delivered him, (namely, his son,) to the Zuw^uwrap [which means both nurse and nurses ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- He left him to himself
; or left him without work, or occupation; namely, his slave; syn. A^ahomalahu . (S, K.) [See musobaEN .]

fem. of saboEapN , q. v. -A2- See also sabuEN in two places. -A3- Als~aboEu The place to which mankind shall be congregated (K, TA) on the day of resurrection. (TA.) Hence the trad., (K, TA,) which relates that while a pastor was among his sheep, or goats, the wolf rushed upon him, and took from them a sheep, or goat, and the pastor pursued him until he rescued it from him; whereupon the wolf looked aside towards him, and said to him, (TA,) mano lahaA yawoma Als~aboEi , meaning Who will be for it [namely, the sheep, or goat, as aider, or defender, ] on the day of resurrection? (K, TA:) thus expl. by I Aar, and mentioned by Sgh and the author of the L: (TA:) but to this is contradictory, or repugnant, yaEokuru , [in the CK erroneously written yaEokaru ,]) the saying of the wolf, (K, TA,) af

(S, Msb, K) and ↓ , (Mgh, Msb,) of which the former is a contraction, (Msb,) A seventh part; one of seven parts; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ ; (S, Msb, K;) the last not heard by Sh on any authority beside that of AZ: (TA:) pl. of the first (Msb) and second (Mgh, Msb) A^asobaAEN . (Mgh, Msb, TA.)
Hence, A^asobaAEN AlquroA=ni [ The seven sections, or volumes, of the Kur-an, ] in which one reads: said to be postclassical. (Mgh.) -A2- See also A^usobuwEN , in three places.

A certain Zimo' of the A^aZomaA=' of camels; (T, S, K;) i. e. their coming to the water on the seventh day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]; (K;) or [in other words, which have virtually the same meaning,] their remaining in their places of pasturing five complete days, and coming to the water on the sixth day, not reckoning the day of the [ next preceding ] return from the water. (Az, TA.) You say, waradato A_iboluhu siboEFA His camels came to the water &c. (S, K.) ― -b2- Also The seventh young one, or offspring. (A in art. vlv .)
: see what next follows.

(S, Sgh, Msb, K) and ↓ , (Sgh, Msb, K,) a dial. var., (Sgh, Msb,) and the form in common use with the vulgar, (Msb,) adopted also by several readers of the Kur in v. 4, (Msb, TA,) and often occurring in the poems of the Arabs, (TA,) and ↓ , (Sgh, K,) a form adopted by two readers of the Kur in the place above mentioned, and perhaps a dial. var., (Sgh, TA,) The animal of prey; the rapacious animal; (K;) [ whether beast or bird; being sometimes applied to the latter, as, for instance, in the K, voce mixolabN ; but generally to the former:] or whatsoever has a fang, or canine tooth, with which it makes hostile attacks, and seizes its prey; (Msb;) such as the lion, [to which it is particularly applied by most of the Arabs in the present day,] and also (TA) such as the wolf and the lynx and the

, (S, K,) sometimes pronounced ↓ but some disallow this latter, and say that it is pl. of saAbiEN , (K,) [ Seven; ] a well-known number; and called one of the perfect numbers: (TA:) fem. saboEN . (S, K.) You say, saboEapu rijaAlK [ Seven men ]: and saboEu nisowapK [ seven women ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- A^axa*ahu A^axo*a saboEapK : see sabuEapN . ― -b3- wazona saboEapK means Of the weight of seven mavaAqiyl : (S, K:) one says, A^axa*otu minohu miAy^apa dirohamK wazona saboEapK , meaning [ I took, or received, from him a hundred dirhems ] every ten whereof were of the weight of seven mithkáls. (TA.) [But see dirohamN .] ― -b4- A_iHodaY mino sboEK [lit. One of seven; ] means (assumed tropical:) a great, momentous, or difficult, thing, or affair: (Sh, K: *) an affair difficult to decide: perhaps as b

; or many; as Bd says, in ix. 81, and as is indicated, though not plainly declared, in the TA. See 2: and see also saboEuwna . ― -b9- Respecting a peculiar pronunciation of the people of El-Hijáz, and a case in which saboEap is imperfectly decl., see valaAvapN . See also sit~apN .] ― -b10- saboEapa Ea$ara [indecl. in every case, meaning Seventeen, ] is pronounced by some of the Arabs saboEapa Eo$ara : and [the fem.] saboEa Ea$orapa , thus in the dial. of El- Hijáz [and of most of the Arabs], is pronounced saboEa Ea$irapa in the dial. of Nejd. (S in art. E$r .) -A2- See also sabuEapN , in two places.
: see saboEapN .

and ↓ , the latter a contraction of the former, The lioness. (ISk, S, Msb, K.) Hence the saying, ↓ , (ISk, S, K,) or Als~aboEapi , (Msb,) He seized him with the seizing of a lioness, (ISk, S, K,) or of the lioness, (Msb,) which is more impetuous ( A^anozaqu ) than the lion, (ISk, S,) or more bold than the lion: (Msb:) or the saying is, A^axa*ahu A^axo*a saboEapa (S, K) he seized him with the seizing of Seb'ah, who was a certain strong man, (Ibn-El-Kelbee, S,) or a certain insolent and audacious rebel, (Ibn-El-Kelbee, Lth, K,) of the Arabs, (TA,) whom one of the kings of El-Yemen seized, and, after having cut off his hands and feet, or arms and legs, crucified; [so that the meaning is, he punished him with the punishment of Seb'ah; ] and hence it was said, laA^uEa*~iban~aka Ea*aAba saboEapa
[ Of, or relating to, an animal of prey. ]
[ Seventy; ] a well-known number; (K;) the round number that is between sit~uwna and vamaAnuwna . (TA.) ― -b2- The Arabs also use it as meaning [ Seventy or more

; or] many. (TA.) Thus it is used in the Kur [ix. 81], where it is said, A_ino tasotagofiro lahumo saboEiyna mar~apF falano yagofira A@ll~`hu lahumo , meaning If thou beg forgiveness for them many times, even then God will not forgive them; not that God would forgive them if forgiveness were begged more than seventy times: (Bd, * TA:) and saboEapN and saboEumiAy^apK and the like are used in the same manner. (Bd.) ― -b3- [Also Seventieth. ]

[ as meaning Seven and seven, or seven and seven together, or seven at a time and seven at a time, seems not to have been used; for] A'Obeyd says that more than A^uHaAda and vunaA='a and vulaAva and rubaAEa has not been heard, excepting Eu$aAra . (TA in art. E$r .)
[app. Wont to frighten ]: (TA: [in which the meaning here given seems to be indicated.])
: see A^usobuwEN , in four places.

dim. of sabuEapN , q. v.

A garment, or piece of cloth, seven cubits, or seven spans, in length. (TA.) ― -b2- A great and tall camel; (En-Nadr, K;) [as though seven cubits in height: ] fem. with p . (K.). And subaAEiY~u Albadani , (S, K,) applied to a man, has the like meaning; (K;) complete, or full-grown, in body; (S, TA;) [or seven spans in height; for] when a boy has attained seven spans, he is a man. (S, voce xumaAsiY~N , q. v.)

[act. part. n. of 1: generally meaning Seventh ]: pl. sabaEapN . (K.) You say, kunotu saAbiEahumo [ I was the seventh of them ]. (S, K.) And h`*aA h`*aA ↓ , meaning saAbiEuhu [ This is the seventh of this: not the seventh part; though the former has also this latter meaning]. (TA.) And huwa saAbiEu saboEapK [ He is the seventh of seven ]. (TA.) And huwa saAbiEN sit~apF [ He is making six to become seven ]. (TA.) ― -b2- A_ibilN sawaAbiEu [pl. of saAbiEapN ] Camels coming to the water on the seventh day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]. (TA.) [See siboEN .] ― -b3- [ saAbiEa Ea$ara and saAbiEapa Ea$orapa , the former masc. and the latter fem., meaning Seventeenth, are subject to the same rules as vaAliva Ea$ara and its fem., expl. in art. vlv , q. v.]

A certain number of days; (S, * Msb, K; *) i. e. seven days; a week; (Msb;) also termed ↓ , (Lth, Msb, K,) by some of the Arabs; (Lth, Msb;) [and ↓ , as shown by what follows:] pl. of the first A^asaAbiyEu . (Msb, TA.) One says, ↓ [in the sense of A^usobuwEayoni , which is more common,] i. e. I remained at his abode two weeks. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The seventh day; and so ↓ ; as in a trad., where it is said, A_i*aA kaAna yawoma subuwEihi , meaning When his seventh day after the celebration of his marriage is come. (TA.) [↓ is used in this sense in the present day: and also as meaning The seventh day after childbirth; in which sense it is generally to be understood when used unrestrictedly; as this day is celebrated with more rejoicing than the former: also as meaning the seventh day after the

Given, or delivered, to the Zuw^uwrap [which means both nurse and nurses ]: (Skr, S, TA:) this is the primary signification: (Skr:) or whose mother dies, and who is therefore suckled by another; (K; in which the next following signification may be regarded as implied, TA;) left to himself
; or left without work, or occupation; applied to a slave; syn. muhomalN : (Skr, S:) or mutorafN , (Sgh, K,) [which has the same and other significations

; or] which is [here] nearly the same as muhomalN , for he who is muhomal is usually mutoraf : (TA:) or one who is left to himself with the sibaAE [or animals of prey ] so that he becomes like one of them in mischievousness, or noxiousness, or evilness: (AO, K:) or who is left to himself and not restrained from his daringness, so that he remains daring: and a slave left to himself, and daring; left until he has become like the sabuE : (TA:) or one whose origin is suspected; (K;) whose father is not known: (Er-Rághib, Sgh:) or a bastard: (K:) or one whose lineage is of slaves, (K, TA,) or ignoble, (TA,) up to seven male ancestors, (K, TA,) or, to seven female ancestors; (TA;) or, to four male ancestors; (En-Nadr, K;) or whose lineage is traced up to four female ancestors all of them slaves:

One whose camels come to the water on the seventh day [ counting the day of the next preceding watering as the first ]. (TA.) -A2- A slave finding a sabuE [or rapacious animal ] among his sheep, or goats. (Aboo-Sa'eed Ed-Dareer, S.)

, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) with fet-h (S, Msb) to the first and third letters, (Msb,) like maroHalapN , (K) and ma*oA^abapN , with an inseparable p , (Sb,) A land containing, (S,) or abounding with, (Mgh, Msb, K,) sibaAE [or animals of prey ]. (S, Mgh, Msb, K.)

A verse consisting of seven feet. (TA.) ― -b2- A camel having, in the middle part of his back, between the withers and the rump, seven vertebrae redundant [app. meaning in size ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [See also muval~avN .]

A rope consisting of seven strands. (M, voce mavoluwvN .) -A2- With p , A cow, (S, TA,) [app. meaning a wild cow,] or [other] female wild animal, (TA,) whose offspring has been eaten by the sabuE [or beast, or bird, of prey ]. (S, TA.)
The place of a sabuE [or beast, or bird, of prey ]. (TA.)
