senses.text: 1 , (Msb, K, &c.,) aor. (MA, Msb) and , (MA,) inf. n. subuwgN , (Msb, K, &c.,) It (a garment [&c.]) was complete, full, ample, or without deficiency: (MA, Msb:) it (a thing, Lth, Msb, of any kind, JK, Msb, such as a garment, TA, a coat of mail, JK, Msb, TA, and the like, TA, and hair, JK, TA) was long, (JK, Msb, K,) from above to below, (Msb,) or reaching to, or towards, the ground. (Lth, K.) [Hence,] *uw subuwgK [ The ample, or long, &c.,] was the name of a coat of mail belonging to the Prophet. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also] sabagato quSayoraY Alfarasi The qSyry [app. here meaning the rib next the flank ] of the horse was of full length. (TA.) ― -b3- And sabaga AlmaTaru (tropical:) The rain approached the earth, and extended. (TA.) ― -b4- And sabagati Aln~iEomapu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. as abo

2 , inf. n. tasobiygN , She (a camel, As, JK, S, or a pregnant female, K) cast her young one, or fœtus, (As, JK, S, K,) in an incomplete state, (TA,) or when its hair had grown, (As, S, K,) or when its fur had grown; (JK;) accord. to the T, (TA,) i. q. A^ajohaDat : (JK, TA:) or, accord. to AA, sab~agati AlA_ibilu biA^awolaAdihaA the camels cast their young abortively; and, in like manner, accord. to Lth, one says of all pregnant females: (TA:) [see also sab~aqat :] the epithet applied to her is ↓ , without p . (As, K, TA.)

4 He made it complete, full, ample, or without deficiency; (Msb;) he made it wide; namely, his garment [&c.]: and he made it long; namely, [his garment, and the like, and] his hair, (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Asbg A@ll~`hu Ealayohi Aln~iEomapa (S, Msb, * K *) (tropical:) God made the benefit, or boon, complete, full, or ample, to him. (S, * Msb, * K, * TA.) And Asbg lahu fiY Aln~afaqapi (assumed tropical:) He expended upon him what was completely sufficient for his wants; bestowed upon him amply. (TA.) ― -b3- And Asbg AlwuDuwo'a , (K,) inf. n. A_isobaAgN , (S,) (tropical:) He performed completely the [ ablution termed ] wDw' , (S, K, TA,) making it to reach to the proper places thereof, and giving fully to every member its due. (K, TA.) -A2- And Asbg He put on a wide, or an ample, [or a long, ]
: see musobigN .

(tropical:) Plentifulness, and pleasantness or easiness, and softness or delicacy, of life. (K, TA.) One says, A_in~ahumo lafiY sabogapK mina AlEayo$i (tropical:) Verily they are in a state of plentifulness, &c., of life. (TA.)

, applied to a thing (JK, S) of any kind, (JK,) Complete, full, ample, or without deficiency: (S, TA:) [and] long. (JK.) You say, diroEN saAbigapN A coat of mail that is wide, or ample, (S, K, * TA,) and long: (K, TA:) or such that one drags it upon the ground, or [ that falls ] against one's ankles, by reason of length and ampleness: pl. sawaAbigu . (TA.) And *anabN saAbigN A complete, a full, or an ample, tail. (S.) And dalowN saAbigapN (tropical:) A long dlw [or leathern bucket ]. (TA.) And naAqapN saAbigapu AlD~aroEi (tropical:) A she-camel full, or without lack or defect, in the udder: (Lth, and so in the K accord. to the TA:) or saAbigapu AlD~uluwEi without lack or defect, and long, in the ribs. (So in copies of the K.) And EajiyzapN saAbigapN and A^aloyapN saAbigapN (Msb, K) signify
More [and most ] complete, full, ample, or free from deficiency [ in breadth and in length ]: occurring in this sense in a trad., relating to a coat of mail. (TA.)
: see what next follows.

(JK, S, K) and tasobagapN and ↓ and tasobagN , (JK, K,) the first of which is the most chaste, (TA,) I. q. migofarN [q. v.]: (JK:) or a portion of the mail of the coat of mail, that is conjoined to the helmet, and protects the neck: (JK, S, K:) for the helmet becomes lengthened ( tasobugu ) thereby; and but for it, there would be between it and the opening at the neck of the coat of mail an intervening space: (S:) or the mail composing the raforaf of the helmet, at the bottom thereof, with which the man protects his neck, and which is also called the migofar : or, accord. to “ the Book of the Coat of Mail and the Helmet, ” by AO, the raforaf of the helmet is other than its tasobigap ; for he says that, of helmets, there is that which has a raforaf , [consisting of] rings [or mail] encompas

, (S, A, L, TA,) in the O and K ↓ , like EunuqN , which seems to be a mistranscription, copied by the author of the K, accord, to his usual practice, from the O, (TA,) A man having upon him a coat of mail such as is termed saAbigapN . (S, A, O, L, K.)
is expl. by Kr as meaning The young that is cast by its mother after the soul has been blown into it. (TA. [But see its verb,
A she-camel that usually casts her young abortively: but a term not well know, (IDrd, TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. (O, Msb, K) and , (O, K,) but the former is of higher authority, or more usual, (O, TA,) inf. n. saboqN , (S, Msb,) He preceded him; he was, or became, got, went, or came, before him, or ahead of him; he outwent, or outstripped, him; he had, got, or took, precedence of him; syn. taqad~amahu ; (K, TA;) in running, and in everything. (TA.) Some read, in the Kur [xxi. 27], laA yasobuquwnahu biAlqawoli , thus, with damm, meaning They say not [anything] without his having taught them: (O, TA:) or they say not anything until He has said it: originally, laA yasobuiqu qawoluhumo qawolahu [ their saying does not precede his saying ]: this reading is from the phrase saAbaqotuhu fasabaqotuhu , [expl. below,] aor. of the latter A^asobuquhu . (Bd.) See

3. ― -b2- sabaqa Alfarasu fiY AlHalobapi The horse outstripped, or came in first, among those started together for a wager, or in the race-ground. (O, K.) Hence the trad. of 'Alee, sabaqa rasuwlu A@ll~`hi waSal~aY A^abuw bakorK waval~ava Eumaru (assumed tropical:) [ The Apostle of God came in first in the race, and Aboo-Bekr came in next, and 'Omar came in third ]. (O, TA.) [And sabaqa used in like manner with the objective complement understood means He preceded, &c., as above; and hence, he was, or became, first, foremost, or beforehand; he had, or got, the priority, or precedence. And He was, or became, one of the first or foremost: see saAbiqN . See also qaSabu Als~aboqi in art. qSb .] ― -b3- sabaqa Aln~aAsa A_ilaY AlA^amori [ He preceded the other people; was, or became, before them

; or had, got, or took, precedence of them; in betaking, or applying, himself to the affair ]. (S, K.) And in like manner one says, lahu saboqN fiY h`*aA AlA^amori To him belongs priority, or precedence, in this affair; like saAbiqapN ; syn. qudomapN . (A, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence,] sabaqa wahomuhu A_ilaY $aYo'K fagaliTa fiyhi (assumed tropical:) [ He preconceived a thing, and therefore made a mistake, or erred, respecting it ]. (Msb, in explanation of duxila Ealayohi .) [And sabaqa *ihonuhu A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i means in like manner (assumed tropical:) He preconceived the thing: or his mind adverted hastily, before reflection, or without premeditation, to the thing; from what next follows.] ― -b5- sabaqa A_ilayohimo He went, or passed, hastily, or quickly, to them. (TA.) ― -b6- [And hence,] sabaqa A

8. And sabaqahu AlqaYo'u , (S, Msb, K, all in art. *rE ,) i. e. sabaqahu fiY Alxuruwji A_ilaY fiyhi [meaning (assumed tropical:) The vomit came forth to his mouth before he was aware ]. (TA in that art.) [And sabaqa Alqalamu (assumed tropical:) The pen anticipated, skipping over something, in transcribing.] ― -b7- One says also, sabaqotu EalayohK , meaning (tropical:) I overcame him. (TA.) senses.text: 1 , (S, MA, Msb,) aor. ; (Msb;) and safuha , [aor. ;] (S, Msb;) inf. n. safahN and safaAhapN (S, MA, Msb, K *) and safaAhN , (S, MA, K, *) [all mentioned in the MA as of the former verb, and so in the TA when that verb is trans., but properly] the first is of the former verb, and the second is of the latter verb, (S, Msb,) and so is the third; (S;) He (a man, S) was, or became, such as is termed safiyh ; (S, TA;) [i. e.] he was, or became, unwise, witless, or destitute of wisdom or understanding, or [rather] lightwitted. (MA.) ― -b2- The phrase safiha nafosapu , [of which an instance occurs in the Kur ii. 124, and] to which gabina raA^oyahu and baTira Eayo$ahu and A^alima baTonahu and wafiqa A^amorahu and ra$ida A^amorahu are similar, was originally safihato nafosu zayodK [or rather safiha

2. ― -b3- safiha Ealayohi signifies jahila [i. e., when thus trans. by means of EalaY , He feigned ignorance to him ]; as also safuha , (K, TA,) and ↓ . (K.) ― -b4- And safihotu naSiybiY [and it is implied in the K that one says safahotu nSybY also, but only the former is authorized by the TA,] I forgot my share, or portion. (Th, K, TA.) ― -b5- And safaha SaAHibahu , aor. , He overcame his companion in what is termed musaAfahap [inf. n. of 3, q. v.]. (K.) You say, ↓ fasafahahu . (TA.) ― -b6- safihati AlT~aEonapu , (JK, K, TA,) inf. n. safahN , (TA,) (tropical:) The spear-wound, or the like, emitted blood which came from it quickly (JK, K, TA) and dried up ( wajaf~a [in the TK wixf ]): (K, TA:) so in the A. (TA.) ― -b7- safiha Al$~araAba , (S, K,) inf. n. safahN , (TA,) He drank much of the

3. And safiha AlmaA='a (tropical:) He drank the water immoderately. (TA.) ― -b8- And safihotu and safahotu signify $ugilotu , (so in the CK,) in [some of] the copies of the K $agalotu , but the right reading is $ugilotu [i. e. I was occupied, or busied, or diverted from a thing]: or, accord. to the copies of the K, ta$ag~alotu ; but correctly, or $agalotu [i. e. I occupied, or busied, or diverted from a thing]. (TA.)

5. ― -b2- [Hence,] sifihihu , inf. n. tasofiyhN , (S, Msb, K,) signifies jaEalahu safiyhFA [i. e. He, or it, made him to be, or he pronounced him to be, lightwitted, &c.]; as also ↓ ; (K, TA;) on the authority of Akh and Yoo: (TA:) or he attributed to him what is termed safah [i. e. lightwittedness, &c.]: (S, Msb:) or he said to him that he was such as is termed safiyh . Msb.) And sf~h Aljaholu Hilomahu Ignorance made him light, inconstant, unsteady, irresolute, or fickle; syn. A^aTaA$ahu and A^axaf~ahu . (TA.) See also 1, in three places.

3 , (S, MA, K,) inf. n. musaAfahapN , (S, KL,) He acted [ in a lightwitted manner, ] foolishly, or ignorantly, with him; (MA, KL;) showed lightness, levity, weakness of mind, and lack of Hilom [or gravity, &c.], with him. (KL.) You say, saAfahahu fasafahahu : see 1, near the end of the paragraph. [ sAfhh in this instance may mean as above, or may have the meaning here next following.] ― -b2- He reviled him

; or he reviled him, being reviled by him; syn. $aAtamahu : whence the prov., safiyhN lamo ↓ [ A lightwitted person found not a reviler, or mutual reviler ]; (K, TA;) mentioned in the S. (TA.) [See also

5.] ― -b3- sAfh Ald~an~a , (S, K,) or AlwaToba , (S,) (assumed tropical:) He sat with ( qaAEada ) the dn~ [or wine-jar ], (S, K,) or the wTb [or milk-skin ], (S,) and drank from it while after while. (S, K.) And sAfh Al$~araAba (tropical:) He exceeded the due bounds in respect of the beverage, or wine, drinking it without measure; (K, TA;) as also ↓ . (K.) And saAfahotu AlmaA='a (tropical:) I drank the water immoderately, (Lh, TA,) or without measure. (A, TA.) [See also 1, near the end of the paragraph.] ― -b4- And saAfahati Aln~aAqapu AlT~ariyqa (tropical:) The she-camel kept to the road, or way, (A, K, TA,) or took to it, (A, TA,) with a vehement pace: (A, K, TA:) or was light, or agile, in her pace, or going. (TA.)

4 I found him to be safiyh [i. e. lightwitted, &c.]. (TA. [There said to be tropical; but I see not why.]) ― -b2- A^asofahaka A@ll~`h Al$~araAba (assumed tropical:) May God make thee to drink of the beverage, or wine, without having thy thirst satisfied thereby: or A^asofahahu A@ll~`hu God made him, or may God make him, to drink without having his thirst satisfied: (S, accord. to different copies:) or Asfh A@ll~`hu fulaAn~aA AlmaA='a God made, or may God make, such a one to drink much water. (TA.)

5 The winds became in a state of commotion. (TA.) ― -b2- tsf~ht Alr~iyHu Al$~ajara , (S,) or AlguSuwna , (K, TA,) and Alr~iyHu ↓ AlguSuwna , (Ham p. 359,) The wind made the trees, (S,) or the branches, (K,) to bend, or incline: (S, K:) and put the branches in motion: (K, and Ham ubi suprà:) or ruffled, and put in motion, the branches. (TA. [There said to be tropical: but see what is said of the primary signification of safahN , below.]) ― -b3- [Hence,] it is said in a prov., furaArapN tasaf~ahato qaraArapF A lamb, or kid, made a sheep, or goat, to incline [to silly behaviour]: applied to the old whom the young incites to lightwittedness ( Als~afah ) and levity. (Meyd. [See also a similar prov. in Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii.

253.]) ― -b4- tsf~hhu Eano maAlihi He deluded him, or beguiled him, of his property. (S, K.) ― -b5- tsf~h Ealayohi He acted with safaAhap [i. e. lightwittedness, &c.], or foolishly, towards him. (MA.) ― -b6- And tasaf~ahotu Ealayohi signifies A^asomaEotuhu [as meaning I reviled him ]. (S.) [See also

6 : see 1, in the last quarter of the paragraph. ― -b2- [And tsAfhwA They behaved in a lightwitted, foolish, or ignorant, manner, one with another. See also 3, which has a similar meaning. ― -b3- And They reviled one another: as seems to be indicated in the TA. See also Har p. 522: and see, again,

3.] ― -b4- tasaAfahu A^a$odaAquhaA , in a verse of Khalaf Ibn-Is-hák El-Bahránee, [describing swift camels,] means Their sides of the mouth casting forth their foam, one at another: like the saying of El-Jarmee, tasaAfahu A^a$odaAquhaA biAll~ugaAmi [ Their sides of the mouth casting forth the foam, one at another ]. (TA. [ tsAfh , there written without any syll. signs, is app. thus, (for tatasaAfahu ,) not tusaAfihu .])

, (S, TA,) as also ↓ and ↓ , (TA,) [all mentioned as inf. ns. in the first paragraph of this art.,] primarily signifies xif~apN [in its proper sense of Lightness ], and motion, commotion, or agitation. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And hence (S, TA) the first, (S, K, TA,) like each of the others, (K, TA,) signifies [generally Lightwittedness, or the like; ] the contr. of HilomN ; (S, K, TA;) [i. e.] xif~apN [as meaning lightness or levity, inconstancy, unsteadiness, irresoluteness

; or lightness or levity, &c., and hastiness; for, as is said in the TA in art. rjH , the contr. of HilomN is described by the terms xif~apN and EajalN , like as HilomN is described by the term viqalN ]; and slenderness, shallowness, or weakness, of judgment; qualities which deficiency of intellect, or understanding, necessarily involves: (Bd in ii. 12, in explanation of safahN :) or xif~apu HilomK [i. e. slightness of gravity or staidness or sedateness or calmness &c.]: or jaholN [i. e. ignorance, or silliness or foolishness ]: (K, TA:) all of which explanations are nearly alike: (TA:) or safahN is a deficiency in intellect or understanding: (Msb:) or a lightness, or levity, accidental to a man, arising from joy or anger, inducing him to act unreasonably and unlawfully. (KT.)
: see the next preceding paragraph.

[ Having the quality termed safahN ; i. e., accord. to the explanation of the primary signification of the latter, above, Light; and in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation: ] applied to a camel's nose-rein, (S, K,) light: (S:) or quivering; (K, TA;) because of the she-camel's shaking it, and contending in pulling it. (TA: but there said to be, when thus applied, tropical.) Dhu-rRummeh says, EalaY Zahori miqolaAtK safiyhK jadiyluhaA i. e. [ Upon the back of a she-camel that had brought forth but once and not conceived after, ] whose nose-rein was light. (S. In the TA, zimaAmuhaA is here put in the place of jadiyluhaA .) And one says also naAqapN safiyhapu AlzimaAmi , (K, TA,) meaning [ A she-camel whose nose-rein is light, or quivering: or] light, or agile, in pace or going. (TA: in
: see safyhN . ― -b2-
Also, applied to a man, (assumed tropical:) Vehemently thirsty: and so saAhifN . (Az, TA.)

(tropical:) A valley filled [ with water ]: (K, TA:) as though it exceeded the due bounds, and became such as is termed safiyh : imagined to be from A^sofahotuhu signifying “ I found him to be safiyh . ” (TA.)

, (K, TA, in the CK [erroneously] musofihN ,) as also masohafapN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) Food that incites [in the CK yutoEibu is erroneously put for yaboEatu ] to the drinking of much water. (IAar, * K, TA.)
act. part. n. of 3, q. v.

senses.text: 1 , (S, M,) aor. yasofuw , inf. n. sufuw~u , (S, TA,) like Euluw~u , (TA,) or safowN , (so accord. to a copy of the M,) He was quick, or swift, in walking, or going, and in flying. (S, M.) -A2- safati Alr~iyHu Alt~urAba , (S, M, Mgh, K,) aor. tasofiy , (S, K,) inf. n. safoyN , (S, M,) The wind raised the dust, or made it to fly, and carried it away, or dispersed it; (S, Mgh, K;) and cast it: (Mgh:) or bore it, carried it, or carried it away; (M, K;) as also ↓ , (K,) a dial. var. of weak authority, mentioned by Sgh on the authority of Fr; (TA;) [or it may be thus expl. by a mistake originating from the fact that] IAar mentions safati Alr~iyHu and A^sofato , [as syn.,] but [in a sense to be expl. hereafter,] not making either of them trans.: (M:) [and ↓ Alr~iyHu Alt~uraAba occurs in the M an

454. [It is there indicated that the meaning is AinohaAla .]) -A3- safiYa : see safFA , below. -A4- safiyato yaduhu His hand became much cracked, or chapped, (K, TA,) in consequence of. work. (TA.) -A5- And safiYa , [aor. yasofaY ,] inf. n. safFA and safaA='N , He was, or became, lightwitted
; or unwise, witless, or destitute of wisdom or understanding; i. q. safiha , inf. n. safahN and safaAhN ; (M, K;) as also ↓ . (Az, K.)

1. -A2- sAfAhu , (S, K,) inf. n. musaAfaApN and sifaA='N , i. q. saAfahahu [ He acted in a lightwitted manner, foolishly, or ignorantly, with him ]. (S, K.) -A3- And He treated him medically, or curatively: (K:) from safaA='N . (TA. [But see sifaA='N , below.])

4 He took for himself a mule such as is termed safowaA=' , i. e. quick [&c.]. (K.) -A2- A^sofato said of the wind, intrans. and trans.: see 1, in two places. -A3- AsfY said of corn, It became rough, or coarse, in the extremities [or awn ] of its ears. (S, K.) ― -b2- Asft said of buhomaY [or barley-grass], It let fall its safaA [or prickles, or awn, or extremities ]. (M, K.) ― -b3- And AsfY said of a man, He took the prickles [or awn or extremities ] of the buhomaY [or barley-grass ]. (TA.) -A4-

Also, said of a man, He removed dust, or earth, ( safFA , TA) from one place to another. (Az, K.) -A5- And Asft said of a she-camel, (tropical:) She became lean, or emaciated, (K,) so that she was like the safA [or prickles of barley-grass ]. (TA.) -A6- See also 1, last sentence. -A7- AsfAhu It (an affair, or event, M) incited him (a man, K) to unsteadiness, and levity. (M, K.) ― -b2- And hence, perhaps, (M,) AsfY bihi He did evil or ill, or acted ill, to him, or with him, (M, K,) i. e., his companion. (M.)
8 i. q. AiSoTarafahu , (Sgh, K,) i. e. He turned away his face. (TK.)

Lightness, thinness, or scantiness, in the hair of the forelock, (S, M, Mgh, K,) of the horse, in which it is discommended, (S, * Z, Mgh,) and of the mule and ass, in both of which it is commended: (Z, Mgh:) or shortness, and scantiness, of the forelock: accord. to Th, it is ↓ , with medd: which is metaphorically used by a poet as meaning scantiness in milk. (M.) [Accord. to the TK, the former is an inf. n., of which the verb is ↓ , said of a horse, as meaning He was, or became, light, thin, or scanty, in the forelock. ] ― -b2- And, accord. to IAar, A whiteness [or a tinge thereof ] in the hair [of a horse]: particularly said by him in one place to be such as is termed A^adoham , and such as is A^a$oqar . (M, in art. sfw .) -A2-

Also, [but more properly written safFY , the last radical in this case being Yi ,] Dust, or earth; (S, M, K;) and so ↓ : (TA:) or this is applied to earth, or dust, [as meaning pouring down, ] from safaY Alt~uraAbu [expl. above]: (Ham p. 454:) the former signifies dust, or earth, though not raised and carried away, or dispersed, by the wind: or, accord. to the T, whatever is raised and carried away, or dispersed, by the wind: (TA:) accord. to IAar, dust, or earth, taken forth from a grave or a well: (M:) safaApN is a more special term, (S,) the n. un., (M,) safaApN mino turaAbK signifying a collection ( kub~apN ) of dust, or earth. (Ham p.

810.) -A3- Also Any kind of tree having prickles, or thorns: (K: [but this seems to have been erroneously taken from what here follows:]) the prickles [or awn or beard ] of buhomaY [or barley-grass ], (S, M,) and of the ears of corn, [ of wheat or barley, (TA in art. xd$ ,)] and of anything having prickles: accord. to Th, the extremities of buhomaY : n. un. safaApN , as above. (M.) -A4- Also Leanness, or emaciation, (K, TA,) in consequence of disease. (TA.) -A5- It is also an inf. n. of safiYa as syn. with safiha , expl. above. (M, K.)

: see the first sentence of the next preceding paragraph: it is expl. in the K [and also in the M] as signifying A stopping, stopping short, or ceasing, of the she-camel's milk: and ISd cites [in the M, after Th], from a poet, the phrase faY A^alobaAnihin~a safaA='u [ending a verse,] referring to [she-camels such as are termed] qalaAy^iS : but Az relates it differently, fiY A^alobAbihin~a with b [in the place of n ]; saying that safaA='N means lightness, or levity, in anything; and ignorance; and that the phrase, as he cites it, means in whose faculties of understanding is lightness. (TA.) [See 1, last sentence: and] see also what next follows.

, accord. to the K, signifies A medicine, or remedy: [see 3, last signification:] but this requires consideration; for it is said in the M, [↓ signifies unsteadiness, and levity; and IAar says,] Als~afaA='u from Als~afiY~u is like Al$~aqaA='u from Al$~aqiY~u . (TA.)

Dust raised, or made to fly, and carried away, or dispersed, by the wind; (S, K;) and (K) so ↓ , (M, K,) i. q. ↓ ; a possessive epithet, or of the measure faAEilN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN . (M. [See another explanation of saAf voce safFA , from the Hamáseh. Freytag explains both safiY~N and saAfK , as on the authority of the K, as epithets applied to the wind, not to the dust.]) ― -b2- Also Clouds; [app. as being driven by the wind;] syn. saHaAbN . (S.) -A2- And i. q. safiyhN [ Lightwitted, &c.: see 1, last sentence]. (M, K.) [And it seems to be indicated in the S that ↓ is syn. with saAfihN , which is syn. with safiyhN .]
: fem. saAfiyapN , pl. sawaAfK : see this last in the next paragraph: ― -b2- and for the first, see safFA : and safiY~N , first sentence. -A2- See also safiY~N again, last sentence.

Dust, syn. gubaArN : (M, K:) or dust ( turaAbN ) and dry herbage or the like: (Ham p. 445:) or dust ( turaAbN ) with the wind: (M:) or wind that bears, or carries, or carries away, dust, (M, K, TA,) much, upon the surface of the earth, impelling it against men: (TA, and in like manner in the Ham ubi suprà:) and ↓ , (TA,) pl. of riyHN saAfiyapN , (Ham ubi suprà,) winds that raise the dust, or make it to fly, and carry it away, or disperse it: you say, laEibato bihi Als~awaAfaY [ The winds raising the dust, &c., made sport with him, or it ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Also Tracks, or streaks, upon a pool put in motion by the wind: so says Freytag; but he names not any authority for this.]

applied to a horse, (As, S, M, Mgh,) Light, thin, or scanty, in the hair of the forelock: (As, S, M, Mgh, K:) or short and scanty therein: fem. safowaA='u : (M:) [and accord. to some, it seems to be in like manner applied to a mule and an ass: (see safFA :)] one says farasN A^asofaY and bagolapN safowaA='u : (Mgh:) [or,] accord. to As, A^asofaY in the sense first expl. above is not applied to anything but a horse: applied to a mule, it means (assumed tropical:) quick, or swift: (S:) or bagolapN safowaA='u signifies (tropical:) a she-mule that is quick, or swift, (S, M, A, K, TA,) like the wind, (A, TA,) active, or light, (S,) of middling make, compact and strong in the back; (M, TA;) and in like manner safowaA='u is applied to a wild she-ass. (M.) ― -b2- Accord. to IAar, AlA^asofaY applied
[and, accord. to Golius, ↓ , mentioned by him as on the authority of the K, in which, however, I do not find it, nor did Freytag,] A calumniator, or slanderer. (K.)
: see safiY~N .

senses.text: 1 , aor. , inf. n. saqabN , He, or it, was, or became, near. (Msb.) saqabN is syn. with qurobN . (S, A, K.) You say, saqibato daAruhu , (S, and so in the K accord. to the TA,) with kesr [to the q ], (S,) [inf. n. as above;] or saqabat , (so in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K and in my copy of the Mgh,) inf. n. saqobN , (so in my copy of the Mgh,) or suquwbN ; (K;) [but I believe the verb to be correctly saqibat , like its syn. Saqibat , and the inf. n. to be correctly saqabN , and perhaps suquwbN also;] His house was near; (S, Mgh, K;) as also ↓ . (S, K.) It is said in a trad., AljaAru A^aHaq~u bisaqabihi , meaning [ The neighbour has a better, or the best, claim to pre-emption] by reason of his being near: (S, * A, Msb:) or the b is a connective of AHq~ with its complement, (Mgh, Msb,)

4 He made him, or it, to be near: (K:) or Asqb daArahu he made his house to be near. (S.) [And so with S .] -A2- See also the paragraph above. -A3- A^asoqabato is also said of a she-camel, meaning She brought forth mostly males. (A, * TA.) [And Asqb He got, or got mostly, male offspring. ] In the following saying, (S, TA,) of Ru-beh, describing the two parents of a man eulogized [by him], (TA,) wakaAnati AlEirosu Al~~atiY tanax~abaA lifaHolK A^asoqabaA ↓ [ And the wife whom he chose was generous, or noble, or fair, one that brought forth, or brought forth mostly, male offspring, to a male that begot, or begot mostly, such offspring, ] the last word is a verb, in the pret. tense, not an epithet applied to fHl . (S, * TA. [In the former, only the second hemistich is cited.])
6 was probably used as meaning Their tents, or houses, were near together: see the part. n. of this verb below.]

The young one of a camel: or, when just brought forth: (K:) or only the male young one of a camel: (S, K:) [see also SaqobN :] when a she-camel has brought forth her young one, the latter, when just born, is called saliylN , before it is known whether it is a male or a female; but when it is known, if it is a male, it is called saqobN : (As, TA:) the female is not called saqobapN , (S, K,) but HaAy^ilN : (S:) or it is [sometimes] called by the former of these appellations: (K:) [see De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, 2nd ed., ii. 358: and see saqobapN below:] the pl. is A^asoqubN [a pl. of pauc.] and siqaAbN and suquwbN and suqobaAnN . (K.) A^a*al~u mina Als~uqobaAni bayona AlHalaAy^ibi [ More vile than the male young ones of camels among the milch camels ] is a prov. [from a verse of Keys Ibn-El-Kh

; or fatness, softness, thinness of the skin, and plumpness. (S. [See also SaqobN .]) Applied to a branch, Juicy, thick, and long: (Az, TA: [and so SaqobN :]) or anything of the like kind full and complete. (ADk, TA.) In the following verse, cited by Sb, wasaAqiyayoni mivola zayodK wajuEalo saqobaAni mamo$uwqaAni makonuwzaA AlEaDalo saqobaAni signifies TawiylaAni [ tall ], and is also written SaqobaAni : (Sh, TA:) [so that the meaning may be, And two waterers, or givers of drink, like Zeyd and Jo'al: they being two tall persons, light of flesh, compact in the muscles: I suppose humaA to be understood before the latter hemistich; because of the ns. in the nom. case: and I have substituted makonuwzaA for manokuwzaA , the reading in the TA, doubtless a mistranscription:] or it is for mivola s
inf. n. of saqiba [q. v.]. (Msb.) -A2- See also saAqibN , in three places.
The female foal of a wild ass. (S, K, * TA.) ― -b2- [See also saqobN , of which, in the first of the senses assigned to it above, it is said by some to be the fem.]

A bit of cotton which a woman afflicted (K, TA) by the death of her husband, in the Time of Ignorance, after shaving her head, and scratching her face, (TA,) used to make red with her blood, (K, TA,) i. e. her own blood, (TA,) and put upon her head, making its extremity to protrude from a hole, or rent, of her qinaAEi [or head-covering ], in order that people might know her to be so afflicted. (K, * TA.)
a pl. of saqobN [q. v.]. (K.) ― -b2- Also The hind legs of camels: (IAar, K:) pronounced also with S . (IAar, TA in art. Sqb .)
: see saAqibN .
: see saqobN , last sentence. ― -b2- Also A baker's kneading-board: or his rolling-pin. (MA.)

[in the CK vAqb ] Near; (A, Msb, K;) and likewise with S ; (A;) as also ↓ (Msb) and ↓ , [likewise pronounced with S ,] (Mgh, K, * TA,) for *uw saqabK , or it may be an inf. n. used as a subst. or an epithet, (Mgh,) and ↓ . (K, * TA.) You say makaAnN saAqibN A near place: (A:) and ↓ and ↓ a near place of alighting or abode: (K, * TA:) and mino daArihi ↓ My house is near his house. (Mgh.) ― -b2- Also Distant: (Msb, K:) this meaning is mentioned by some, as well as the former: (Msb:) thus it has two contr. meanings: (K:) the latter of these is mentioned in the Mj; and the following verse is cited as a proof thereof; tarakota A^abaAka biA^aroDi AlHijaAzi waruHota A_ilaY baladK saAqibi [ Thou leftest thy father in the land of El-Hijáz, and wentest to a distant country ]. (MF, TA.)
A man tall and slender. (Suh, TA.)
or A^aSoqabu , occurring in a trad., accord. to different relaters, Nearer [and nearest ]. (TA in art. Sqb .)
: see saAqibN , in two places.
The dam of a saqob [q. v.]; as also ↓ : (K:) [or] the latter signifies a she-camel that usually brings forth males. (S.)
: see what next precedes: and see a verse cited above, conj.
Their tents, or houses, are near together. (K.)

senses.text: 1 , (S,) aor. , inf. n. saqorN , (TA,) The sun scorched, or burned, him, altering the colour of his complexion and shin, (S, * TA,) and pained him, or pained his brain by its heat: (TA:) melted and heated him, or it. (TA.) And saqaratohu Aln~aAru The fire altered the colour of his skin
; or scorched his skin, and altered its colour; as also Saqaratohu . (Bd in liv.
The heat, and hurtful action, of the sun. (K.)

Hell: (S, K:) one of the [proper] names thereof: (S:) Aboo-Bekr says, There are two opinions respecting this word: some say, that the fire of the world to come is thus called, and that the derivation of the word is unknown, and that it is imperfectly decl. because it is determinate and a foreign word: others say that it is from saqaratohu Al$~amosu , because it melts the bodies and souls, and that it is an Arabic word; and he who holds it to be such says that it is imperfectly decl. because it is determinate and of the fem. gender. (TA.)
The vehemence of the stroke of the sun. (S.)
A day vehemently hot. (S in this art., and K in art. smqr .) This is its proper place. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , (S, M, K,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. samorN and sumuwrN , (M, K,) He held a conversation, or discourse, by night: (S:) or he waked; continued awake; did not sleep: (M, K:) and ↓ may signify the same
; or may be of the same class as A^ahozala and A^asomana , and thus signify he had, or came to have, a samar [or conversation, or discourse, by night ]. (M.) [See also
3.] ― -b2- samarati AlmaA$iyapu , aor. , inf. n. sumuwrN , (assumed tropical:) The cattle pastured by night without a pastor

; or dispersed themselves by night: (M, TA:) [or simply pastured by night; for] one says, A_in~a A_ibilanaA tasomuru , meaning (assumed tropical:) Verily our camels pasture by night: (TA:) and samarati AlA_ibilu layolatahaA kul~ahaA (tropical:) The camels pastured during their night, the whole of it. (A.) And samarati AlmaA$iyapu Aln~abaAta (assumed tropical:) The cattle pastured upon the herbage; (M, K;) aor. as above: (M:) [or pastured upon the herbage by night: like as one says,] samara Alxamora (assumed tropical:) He drank mine, or the mine, (K, TA,) by night: (TA:) and baAtuwA yasomuruwna Alxamora (tropical:) They passed, or spent, their night drinking wine, or the wine. (A.) ― -b3- See also samiyrN , in three places. -A2- samura , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. ; (K;) and samira , (S, K, in a

2 , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. tasomiyrN ; (S;) and ↓ , (S, M, Mgh, &c.,) aor. (M, Msb, K) and , (M, K,) inf. n. samorN ; (M, Msb;) or the former has an intensive signification; (Msb;) [ He nailed it; i. e.] he made it fast, firm, or strong, (M, Mgh, K,) with a nail [or nails ]; (S, * M, * Mgh, Msb, K; *) namely, a door [&c.]. (Mgh, Msb.) [See also sarodN .] -A2- sm~r All~abana , (M, TA,) inf. n. tasomiyrN ; (S;) and ↓ , (K, TA,) aor. ; (TA;) He made the milk thin with water; (S;) made it to be what is termed samaAr [q. v.]. (M, K.) -A3- sm~r , inf. n. as above, is also syn. with $am~ara (S, M, K) and A^arosala . (M, K.) You say, sm~r sahomahu He discharged, or shot, his arrow; (M, TA;) as also ↓ : (K, TA:) or the former, he discharged it, or shot it, hastily; (K;) opposed to xaroqala ;
; or let it take its course. (M, TA.)
3 , (M,) inf. n. musaAmarapN , (S, A,) He held a conversation, or discourse, with him by night. (S, M.) [See also 1, first sentence.]
4 see 1: ― -b2- and samiyrN , in four places: -A2- and see also
11 : see 1, in the latter half of the paragraph.

Conversation, or discourse, by night; (S, M, K;) as also musaAmarapN . (S, A. *) It is said in a trad., Als~amaru baEoda AlEi$aA='i , or, accord. to one relation, Als~amoru , Conversation or discourse by night is after nightfall. (TA.) And you say, laA A^afoEaluhu Als~amara waAlqamara I will not do it as long as men hold conversation or discourse in a night when the moon shines: (S:) or as long as men hold conversation or discourse by night, and as long as the moon rises: (Lh, M:) or ever. (M.) [See also below. The pl., A^asomaArN , is often used as meaning Tales related in the night, for amusement: but this usage is probably post-classical.] ― -b2- (tropical:) Conversation, or discourse, by day. (TA.) ― -b3- A place in which people hold conversation or discourse by night

; or in which they make, or remain awake; (M, K;) as also ↓ ; (S, * M, K;) which latter is expl. by Lth as signifying a place in which people assemble for conversation or discourse by night. (TA.) ― -b4- A people's assembling and holding conversation or discourse in the dark. (TA.) ― -b5- And hence, (TA,) The dark

; or darkness. (As, M, K, TA.) So in the saying Halafa biAls~amari waAlqamari He swore by the darkness and the moon. (As.) ― -b6- Night: (M, K:) you say, A^atayotuhu samarFA I came to him in the night. (A.) ― -b7- A night in which there is no moon: hence the saying laA A^afoEalu *`lika Als~amara waAlqamara I will not do that when the moon does not rise nor when it does rise. (Fr.) [See also above.] ― -b8- The shade of the moon. (M, K.) ― -b9- The light of the moon; moonlight; accord. to some, the primary signification; because they used to converse, or discourse, in it. (TA.) ― -b10- The time of daybreak: you say, Turiqa Alqawomu samarFA The people were come to at daybreak. (AHn, M.) ― -b11- See also samiyrN .

A certain kind of tree, (M, K,) well known; (K;) i. q. TaloHN [the gum-acacia-tree; acacia, or mimosa, gummifera ]; (Msb;) or [ a species ] of the TaloH , (S,) of the kind called EiDaAh , (Mgh, Msb,) having small leaves, short thorns, and a yellow fruit ( baramap ) which men eat: there is no kind of EDAh better in wood: it is transported to the towns and villages, and houses are covered with it: (M:) its produce is [ a pod ] termed HubolapN [q. v.]: (TA in art. Hbl :) [the mimosa unguis cati of Forskål (Flora Aegypt. Arab., pp. cxxiii. and 176:)] n. un. samurapN : (M, Mgh, Msb, K:) [in the S, samurN is said to be pl. of samurapN : but it is a coll. gen. n.:] the pl. of samurapN is samuraAtN , and A^asomurN , a pl. of pauc., of which the dim. is ↓ . (S.) It is said in a prov., A^a$obaha $ar

[ A tawny, or brownish, colour, of various shades, like the various hues of wheat; (see A^asomaru ;) duskiness; darkness of complexion or colour; ] a certain colour, (S, Msb,) well known, (Msb,) between white and black, (M, K,) in men and in camels and in other things that admit of having it, but in camels the term A^udomapN is more common, and accord. to IAar it is in water also; (M;) in men, the same as wuroqapN [ in camels ]; (IAar, TA;) a colour inclining to a faint blackness; (T, TA;) the colour of what is exposed to the sun, of a person of whom what is concealed by the clothes is white: (IAth:) from samarN signifying the “ shade of the moon. ” (TA.)
: see Als~aAmirapu .
Camels that eat the tree called samur . (AHn, M, K.)
The [ demon called ] guwl . (Sgh, K.)

Thin milk: (S:) milk containing much water: (Th, M, K:) or [ diluted ] milk of which water composes two thirds: n. un. with p , signifying some thereof. (M.) ― -b2- [See also a tropical usage of this word in a prov. cited voce rabaDN .] -A2- [In the present day it is also applied to A species of rush, growing in the deserts of Lower and Upper Egypt, of which mats are made for covering the floors of rooms; the juncus spinosus of Forskål, (Flora Aegypt. Arab., p. 75,) who writes its Arabic name “ sammar; ” the juncus acutus of Linn.]
, applied to a she-camel, (K, TA,) Swift: (K:) or generous, excellent, or strong and light, and swift. (TA.)

i. q. ↓ ; (M, A, K;) i. e. A partner in conversation, or discourse, by night. (TA.) You say, A^anaA samiyruhu and ↓ [ I am his partner &c.]. (A.) ― -b2- Afterwards used unrestrictedly [as signifying (assumed tropical:) A partner in conversation, or discourse, at any time ]. (TA.) ― -b3- [Golius and Freytag add the meaning of A place of nocturnal confabulation; as from the K; a sense in which this word is not there found.] ― -b4- Aibonu samiyrK The night in which is no moon: [ contr. of Aibonu vamiyrK :] a poet uses the phrase A@bonu samiyrK ↓ , meaning As long as the moonless night allows the holding conversation, or discourse, in it. (M. [See also another explanation of this phrase in what follows.]) ― -b5- samiyrN is also syn. with dahorN [as meaning Unlimited time, or time without end ]

Hence, or because people hold conversation, or discourse, in them, (S,) AibonaA samiyrK means The night and the day. (S, M, K.) You say, A@bonaA samiyrK ↓ , (S, K,) and laA A=tiyka Alx , (M,) and A@bonu samiyrK ↓ , and Als~amiyru ↓ , (M, K,) and A@bonaA samiyrK ↓ , and A@bonu ↓ samiyrK , (Lh, M, K,) and Als~amiyru ↓ , (K,) i. e. [ I will not do it, and I will not come to thee, ] ever, (S,) or in all time, (M,) or while night and day alternate. (K.) And laA A^afoEaluhu samiyra All~ayaAliY (S, M) [ I will not do it ] to the end of the nights. (M.) ― -b6- AibonaA jaAlisK wasamiyrK is expl. by AHeyth, in his handwriting, as meaning Two roads that differ, each from the other. (Az, TA.)

A certain kind of ships. (S.) [ sumayoriY~N signifies the same, (Golius on the authority of Meyd.,) applied to A single ship of that kind. ] ― -b2- IAar mentions the saying, A^aEoTayotuhu sumayoriy~apF mino daraAhima kaA^an~a Ald~uxaAna yaxoruju minohaA , without explaining it: [ISd says,] I think he meant, [ I gave him ] daraAhim sumor , i. e. dusky dirhems, as though smoke were issuing from them by reason of their duskiness: or dirhems of which the whiteness was fresh. (M.)

[The sable; mustela zibellina, or viverra zibellina; ] a certain beast, (Mgh, K,) or animal, (Msb,) well known, (Mgh,) found in Russia, beyond the country of the Turks, resembling the ichneumon; in some instances of a glossy black; and in some, of the [ reddish ] colour termed $uqorap : (Msb, TA:) costly furred garments are made of its skin: (K, TA:) pl. samaAmiyru . (Msb.) ― -b2- Also A jub~ap [or any garment ] made with its fur. (TA.)
A companion of [or one who habitually indulges in ] conversation, or discourse, by night. (M, K.)

A man holding, or who holds, a conversation, or discourse, by night: (S:) pl. sum~aArN (S, M, K) and sum~arN . (TA.) It is also a quasi-pl. n., (M, K,) [as such occurring in a verse cited voce murim~N , in art. rm ,] and is syn. [as such] with sum~aArN , signifying persons holding, or who hold, conversation, or discourse, by night: (S, M:) or persons waking, continuing awake, not sleeping; as also ↓ [a fem. sing., and therefore applicable as an epithet to a broken pl. and to a quasi-pl. n. and to a coll. gen. n.]: (M, K:) saAmirN is a pl. [or rather quasi-pl. n.] applicable to males and to females: (T, TA:) or it is a sing., and, like other sings., is used as a qualificative of a pl. only when the latter is determinate; as in the phrase tarakotuhumo saAmirFA [ I left them holding a convers

: see saAmirN . -A2- Als~aAmirapu (M, Msb, K) and ↓ (TA) [ The Samaritans; a people said to be ] one of the tribes of the Children of Israel; (M;) or a sect, (Msb,) or people, (K,) of the Jews, differing from them (Msb, K) in most, (Msb,) or in some, (K,) of their institutes: (Msb, K:) Zj says, they remain to this time in Syria, and are known by the appellation of ↓ : (M:) most of them are in the mountain of n-Nábulus: (TA:) ↓ is the rel. n. of Als~aAmirapu . (M, Msb, K.)
, and its pl.: see the next preceding paragraph.

[ Tawny, or brownish; dusky; dark-complexioned or dark-coloured; ] of the colour termed sumorapN [q. v.]: (S, M, K, & c.:) fem samoraA='u : (Msb, & c.:) and pl. sumorN . (A.) You say baEiyrN A^asomaru A camel of a white colour inclining to $uhobap [which is a hue wherein whiteness predominates over blackness ]. (M.) And qanaApN samoraA='u [ A tawny spearshaft ]. (M.) And HinoTapN samoraA='u [ Tawny wheat ]. (M.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Als~amoraA='u Wheat: (S, Msb, K:) because of its colour. (Msb.) And AlA^asomaraAni Wheat and water: (AO, S, K:) or water and the spear. (S, K.) ― -b3- AlA^asomaru , also, signifies Milk: (M:) or milk of the gazelle: (IAar, M, K:) app. because of its colour. (M.) ― -b4- And [for the same reason] Als~amoraA='u signifies also Coarse flour, or flour of the third quality
dim. of A^asomurN : see samurN , in two places.
A nail; a pin, or peg, of iron; (Mgh;) a certain thing of iron; (S, K) a thing with which one makes fast, firm, or strong: (M, K:) pl. masaAmiyru . (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2-
Also, (K, TA,) or misoamAruA_ibilK , (A, O,) (tropical:) A good manager of camels; (A, O, K, TA;) a skilful, good pastor thereof. (A.)

Nailed; made fast, firm, or strong, with a nail [or nails ]. (S, * Mgh.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A man, (TA,) having little flesh, strongly knit in the bones and sinews. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And, with p , (tropical:) A woman, (M,) or girl, or young woman, (A, O, K,) compact, or firm, in body, (M, A, O, K,) not flabby in flesh. (M, O, K.) -A2- Eayo$N masomuwrN (tropical:) A turbid life: (M, O, * K, * TA:) from samaArN applied to milk. (M, TA.)
: see samiyrN , in two places.

(ISh, O, K. [It seems to be intentionally indicated in the O and K, by what immediately precedes the explanation of this phrase, which explanation is A^aEoTihi , that AlxaraAja is to be understood after it.])
[written without any syll. signs, and therefore probably samorajo ,] sing. of samaAriju , (TA,) which signifies Even, or plain, places [or tracts ] of land. (T, * Ibn-'Abbád, O, TA. *)

and ↓ , (S, O, K,) each a Pers. word arabicized, (S, O,) [or rather a compound of the Pers. siho “ three ” and the Arabic mar~aho for mar~ap “ a time, ”] The levying of the [ tax called ] xaraAj at three several times [or instalments ]: (S, O, K:) or the name of the day on which payment of the xaraAj is received; (K;) thus the former word is expl. by ISh; (O;) the day of the collecting of the xrAj ; (Ibn-'Abbád, ISd, O, TA;) a day when the foreigners, or Persians, ( AlEajam ) levy the xrAj at three several times [or instalments ]: also mentioned as written with $ . ; or one who acts as an intermediary between the seller and the buyer, (Lth, Mgh, K,) for effecting the sale; whom people call dal~aAlN , because he directs the purchaser to the merchandise, and the seller to the price: (TA:) pl. samaAsirapN : (Mgh, K:) a Pers. word, arabicized: (Lth, Mgh:) or one who sells wheat to the people: (M, TA:) or (TA, in the K “ and ”) the possessor of a thing: (K:) or (TA, in the K “ and ”) one who has the care of a thing. (K.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A messenger, or mediator, ( safiyrN ,) between two lovers or friends. senses.text: 1 , and , and , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. samoTN , (S, M, Msb,) namely, a kid, (S, M, Msb, K,) and a lamb, (M,) He removed its hair, (Msb,) or wool, (K,) or cleansed it of the hair, [or wool, ] (S,) by means of hot water; (S, Msb, K;) in order to roast it; (S;) or it is generally done for this purpose: (TA:) or he plucked from it the [ hair, or] wool, after putting it into hot water. (A.) ― -b2- [And It scalded it: for] you say, of boiling water, yasomuTu Al$~aYo'a [ it scalds the thing ]. (TA.) -A2- samaTahu , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (M,) also signifies He hung it; suspended it; namely, a thing; (M, K;) as also ↓ , inf. n. tasomiyTN : (TA:) or the latter, he hung it, or suspended it, upon, (S, K,) or by means of, (so in some copies of the K and in the TA,) sumuwT , (S, K,) meaning thongs,
2 see 1, in two places. ― -b2- sam~aTotu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. tasomiytN , also signifies I kept, or clave, to the thing: hence a verse cited voce dariynN . (TA in art. drn .)
5 It (a thing, TA) was, or became, hung, or suspended. (K.)

A thread, or string, having upon it beads (S, Mgh) or pearls; (Mgh;) otherwise it is called silokN : (S, Mgh:) a string of beads or the like; (M, K;) so called because it is hung, or suspended; (M;) a single string thereof; like yako rasano [in Persian]; a necklace of two strings thereof being called *aAtu simoTayoni : (IDrd:) or it signifies, (M,) or signifies also, (K,) a necklace longer than the mixonaqap : (IDrd, M, K:) or [simply] a necklace: (Msb:) pl. sumuwTN : (M, K:) which also signifies the things that are suspended ( maEaAliyqu ) from necklaces. (TA.) ― -b2- A thong, or strap, that is suspended from the horse's saddle; (S, K;) sing. of sumuwTN . (S.) ― -b3- The redundant part of the turban, which is left hanging down upon the breast and the shoulder-blades: (K:) pl. as above. (T

, (M, K,) and ↓ , (S, M, K,) and ↓ , (M, K,) which last is pl. of samiyTN , (TA,) A sandal, or sole, that is of a single piece [ of leather, not of two or more pieces sewed together, one upon another ], ( TaAqN waAHidN , S, TA,) in which is no patch: (S, M, K:) or the last, (S,) or all, (M,) not having a second piece sewed on to it; (AZ, S, M;) as also ↓ . (So in the K, voce farodN .) ― -b2- [ vawobN sumuTN (the latter word occurring twice in art. ljf in the TA, and there opposed to mubaT~anN , and said to be masc. and fem.,) i. q. ] ↓ A garment having no lining; [either] a TayolasaAn , or such as is of cotton: (ISh, K:) but one does not say kisaA='N simoTN nor miloHafapN simoTN , because such are not [ever] lined: (ISh:) or [accord. to some] simoTN signifies a garment that is lined below;

A rank of people: (M, K:) or a side, or lateral part or portion: (Msb:) each of the two sides, or lateral portions, of men, and of palmtrees. (S, Msb.) You say, qaAma bayona Als~imaATayoni He stood between the two ranks. (TA.) And qaAma Alqawoma Hawolahu simaATayoni The people stood around him in two ranks. (TA.) And humo EalaY simaATK waAHidK They are according to one order. (K.) And ma$aY bayona Als~imaATayoni He walked between the two sides. (S, Msb.) And xu*uwA simaATaYi AlT~ariY~i Take ye the two sides of the fresh, or moist. (TA.) And AijoEali AlA^amora simaATFA waAHidFA Make thou the affair, or case, [ uniform, or] one uniform thing. (Fr, TA in art. bA^j .) ― -b2- The part of a valley which is between the upper extremity and the lower: (M, K:) pl. sumuTN . (K) ― -b3- simaATu AlT~aEa

and ↓ , applied to a kid, (S, M, Msb, K,) and to a lamb, (M,) Of which the hair, (Msb,) or wool, (K,) has been removed, (Msb, K,) or cleansed of its hair [or wool ], (S,) by means of hot water; (S, Msb, K;) in order to its being roasted: (S:) or of which the [ hair or] wool has been plucked off from it, after its having been put into hot water: (M:) or the former, plucked of its [ hair or] wool, and then roasted with its skin: (Lth:) and a roasted sheep or goat: the former word of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN . (TA.) -A2- See also samiyTN , and its pl. A^asomaATN , voce sumuTN ; the pl. in three places.
Boiling water, that scalds ( yasomuTu ) a thing. (TA.) -A2- Hanging a thing by a rope behind him; from Als~umuwTu [pl. of Als~imoTu ]. (TA.)
: see samiyTN .

senses.text: 1 , (S, Msb, K, *) aor. , (K,) inf. n. samoEN (S Msb, K) and simoEN , or this latter is a simple subst., (Lh, K,) and samaAEN , (S, K,) or this last [also] is a simple subst., (Msb,) and samaAEapN and samaAEiyapN (K) and masomaEN , (TA,) [ He heard it, (namely, a thing, as in the S,) or (tropical:) him; ] and ↓ , (Msb, K,) also written and pronounced Ais~am~aEa ; (K, TA;) and ↓ ; (Msb;) are syn. with samiEa (Msb,K) as trans. By itself; (Msb;) and AstmE [also] in sys. With samiEa [ as trans. by itself]: (Ham p. 694, where occurs a usage of its act. part. n. showing the verb to be trans. by itself:) or ↓ denotes what is intentional, signifying only he gave ear, hearkened, or listened: but samiEa , [as also ↓ and ↓ ,] what is unintentional, as well as what is intentional. (Msb.) You say, sami

36 and xxxviii. 6, S, K, TA.) [When trans. by means of li alone, or A_ilaY , it denotes what is intentional.] You say, samiEotu lahu , (S, Msb, TA,) and A_ilayohi , (S, TA,) meaning I gave ear, hearkened, or listened, to him, or it; (S, Msb, * TA;) and lh ↓ (Msb,) or Alyh , and Ais~am~aEotu , (S, TA,) signify the same; (S, Msb, TA;) and so lh ↓ , (S, Msb, K,) and Alyh . (K.) It is said in the Kur [xxxvii. 8], accord. to different readings, laA yasomaEuwna A_ilaY AlmalaA_i AlA^aEolaY , and ↓ , They shall not listen [ to the archangels ]: (S:) or the former has this signification, they shall not listen to the angels (Bd, Jel) in heaven, (Jel,) or the exalted angels: (Bd:) and ↓ the latter, they shall not seek, or endeavour, to listen &c. (Bd.) And in the same [xvii. 50], ↓ bihi A_i*o yasotam

2 [inf. n of sm~E , as also tasomiEapN , q. v. infrà, voce sumoEapN ,] is syn. with ↓ [The making one to hear ]. (K.) You say, sm~Ehu AlS~awota and ↓ [ He made him to hear the sound ]. (S.) And sm~Ehu AlHadiyva (TA) and ↓ (S, TA) [ He made him to hear the narra- tive ]; both signifying the same. (TA.) Hence, in a trad. respecting the throwing of the pebbles [at Minè], yusohilu occurs as meaning He betakes himself to the interior of the valley. (TA.) ― -b2- Also They used smoothness, or easiness, ( suhuwlap ,) with men: opposed to A^aHozanuwA . (TA.) [See also
3.] -A2- Ashl is also trans., signifying He found [a thing, a place, &c.,] to be smooth or soft, plain or level, or smooth and soft. (Ham p.

675.) ― -b2- Ashl AlT~abiyEapa (S) or AlbaTona , (Msb, K,) said of medicine, (S, Msb, K,) It relaxed, or loosened, the bowels; syn. A^alaAna , (K,) or A^aTolaqa . (Msb.) (JK.) ― -b3- Als~ahowu also signifies Als~ukuwnu (JK, S, K) and All~iynu (JK, S,) [app. as an inf. n., i. e. as meaning The being still, or quiet, and gentle; though it is immediately added in the S that the pl. is sihaA='N ; for it seems that an early transcriber of the S has omitted to insert after All~aynu the words waAls~aAkinu waAll~ay~inu : see sahowN below]. 4 He (a man, TA) constructed what is termed a sahowap (K, TA) in a bayot [or chamber &c.]. (TA.)

[often written Als~uhaY ] A certain dim star, (S, K,) in [ the asterism called ] banaAt naEo$ AlkuboraY , (S, [in the K, erroneously, bnAt nE$ AlS~ugoraY ,]) by the middle star of those thus called; (TA;) [i. e.] a small star by that called AlEanaAqu , ( which latter is the middle star [ ] of the three in the tail of Ursa Major, Kzw,) by looking at which persons try their powers of sight; (Kzw, TA;) mentioned in art. qwd [voce qaAy^idN , q. v.]; (K;) [it is the star 80, by ;] also called ↓ , which is the diminutive. (TA.) It is said in a prov., A^uriyhaA Als~uhaA waturiyniY Alqamara [ I show her Es-Suhà and she shows me the moon ]. (S, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. vol. i. pp. 527—
9.]) And one says, A^an~aY yalotaqiY suhayolN waAls~uhaA How can Suheyl [or Canopus ] meet Es-Suhà? for the former is southern and the latter is northern. (Har p.

[an inf. n. used as an epithet,] Easy; applied to a man, and to an affair, (K, TA,) and to an object of want: (TA:) and so [the fem.] sahowapN , applied to a mare; and applied to a she-mule as meaning easy in pace, that does not fatigue her rider: the epithet sahowN , however, is not applied to a he-mule: so in the T: (TA:) [but] it is applied to a he-camel, meaning easy to ride: and sahowapN to a she-camel, (K, TA,) meaning gentle, easy to ride: and raAhK ↓ , applied to a he-camel, means [likewise] gentle in pace; and so [the pls.] sawaAhK rawaAhK applied to camels: (TA:) [and so ↓ applied to a mare; for] a certain mare was named Als~ahowaA='u because of the gentleness of her pace. (TA.)

Also, applied to water, Cool, sweet, or limpid; easy of descent in the throat. (K, * TA.) And qawosN sahowapN A bow that is compliant, (K, TA,) and easy. (TA.) And riyHN sahowN A gentle wind: [or a quiet, gentle wind: ] pl. sihaA='N : (TA:) a poet (said to be El-Hárith Ibn- 'Owf, TA) says, tanaAwaHati Alr~ayaAHu lifaqodi EamorKw wakaAnato qabola maholikihi sihaA='aA i. e. [ The winds blew violently for the loss of 'Amr; but they were before his death ] quiet and gentle. (S, TA.) One says also A^aroDN sahowapN Soft land, without barrenness. (TA.) -A2- And Als~ahowu means The moon, in the language of the Nabathæans. (JK.)
: see sihowaA='N

An instance, or a case, of unmindfulness, forgetfulness, neglectfulness, heedlessness, or inadvertence. (Msb.) -A2- A rock, or great mass of stone, (K,) in the dial. of Teiyi, who call nothing else by this name: so in the M: or, accord. to the T, in that dial., the rock, or great mass of stone, upon which the waterer [app. of camels ] stands: (TA:) or a rock, or great mass of stone, standing up, not having any foundation [app. meaning not partly imbedded ] in the ground: and in the dial. of Teiyi, a single stone, great or small. (JK.) ― -b2- A bayot [app. here meaning booth, or the like, ] which the Arabs of the desert set up at the water, and by the shade of which they shelter themselves. (TA.) A Suf~ap [or kind of roofed vestibule, or the like, or a covering for shade and shelter ], (K,

; or simply a shelf, or ledge projecting from a wall, (see raf~N and TaAqN ,)] in which, or upon which, a thing is placed: (ISd, K:) or a small bayot [or chamber ], (S, K,) descending into the earth, having its roof elevated above the ground, (S,) resembling a small xizaAnap [or closet, or storeroom ], (S, K,) in which are [ deposited ] the household-goods, or furniture and utensils; thus as heard by A'Obeyd from more than one of the people of El-Yemen: (S:) or it signifies, (K,) or signifies also, (JK,) four sticks, or pieces of wood, (JK, K,) or three, (K,) which are placed crosswise, one upon another, and upon which is then put anything of the household-goods, or furniture and utensils: (JK, K:) so in the M: (TA:) and (accord. to the T, TA) i. q. kanoduwjN , (K,) which means a small clo
: see sahowN : -A2- and see also what here follows.

, (IAar, JK, S, TA,) like siEowaA='N and tihowaA='N , all with kesr, on the authority of IAar, but in the K ↓ , (TA,) A [ portion, or short portion, such as is termed ] saAEap , of the night; (S, K, TA;) and (S, TA) the first part thereof: (JK, S, TA:) or it may be like ↓ , [which is app. in this case with tenween, and] which seems to mean a period in which people are unmindful of the places, or ways, in which things are, or should be, sought by them
; or shwAn may be from saAhiyapN , expl. below: and mina All~ayoli ↓ signifies the same as siEow and saEow [and sihowaA=' ] and siEowaA' . (Ham p.
708.) One says, laqiytuhu baEoda sihowaA='K mina All~ayoli i. e. [ I met him after a portion, or short portion, of the night
; or] after the first part of the night had passed. (JK.)
: see saAhK : -A2- and see also sihowaA='N .
dim. of Als~uhaA , q. v.

Unmindful, forgetful, neglectful, heedless, or inadvertent; (JK, S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ ; (S, K;) whence the prov., A_in~a AlmuwaS~ayona banuw sahowaAno (S) i. e. Only the unmindful [lit. the sons of the unmindful ] are such as require to be enjoined: (S, Meyd:) or, as some say, by bnw shwAn are meant all mankind; because all become unmindful: but the most correct explanation is, that those who are enjoined to do a thing are subject to unmindfulness: it is applied to him who is unmindful of pursuing that which he is commanded to do: and shwAn may be syn. with [the inf. n.] sahowN

; or it may be an epithet, syn. with saAhK , and is applied to Adam, because he forgot his cove- nant, so that bnw shwAn may mean the sons of Adam, and hence, the unmindful. (Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 3-
4.]) ― -b2- See also sahwN .
A tract of land long and wide, without any covert of trees, or the like, [ to obstruct the view, or] to repel the eye. (JK, and Ham p.
and A^asohaA='apN : see what follows.

, (JK, TA,) in the K, erroneously, ↓ , (TA,) i. q. A^alowaAnN [generally signifying Colours; but also meaning sorts, or species; and here used in this latter sense, as is indicated in the TA]: a pl. having no sing.: (K, TA:) so in the M: (TA:) or it signifies, (JK,) or signifies also, (TA,) various sorts ( DuruwbN muxotalifpN , JK, TA) of pace of camels; like A^asaAhiyju : (TA:) and its sing. is ↓ . (JK.)

senses.text: 1 , (Lth, M, Msb, K,) aor. yasuwo'u , (Lth, Msb,) inf. n. sawo'N , (Lth, M,) or sawaA='N , like saHaAbN , (K,) [but the former is that which is commonly known,] It (a thing, Lth, M) was, or became, evil, bad, abominable, foul, unseemly, unsightly, or ugly. (Lth, M, Msb, K.) It is used in this sense, (IKt, TA,) or [rather] is like biy^osa , (Bd, Jel,) in the Kur [xvii. 34], where it is said, saA='a sabiylFA [ Evil, &c., is it as a way of acting ]: (IKt, Bd, Jel, TA:) which is like the saying, saA='a h`*aA ma*ohabFA [ Evil, &c., is this as a way of acting or believing, &c.]: the noun being in the accus. case as a specificative. (IKt, TA.) And so in the saying, saA='a maA faEala fulaAnN SaniyEFA [ Evil, &c., as an action, is that which such a one has done ]. (TA.) ― -b2- One says also, suw^ot

4.] ― -b2- One says also, suw^otu wajoha fulaAnK , aor. A^asuwow^uhu , inf. n. masaA='apN and masaAy^iyapN , (Lth, TA,) i. q. qabaHotuhu [i. e. I said, May God remove the person (lit. the face ) of such a one far from good, or prosperity, &c.]. (TA. [It is said in a copy of the M, that suw^otu lahu wajohahu means qab~aHotuhu : but I think that the right explanation is qabaHotuhu , without tesh-deed, meaning I said to him, qabaHa A@ll~`hu wajohaka : see art. qbH .])
2 [ He corrupted, or marred ]. You say, saw~i walaA tusaw~iy^o Rectify thou, and do not corrupt, or mar. (A, TA.) [See also

4.] ― -b2- sw~A^ Ealayohi He said to him A^asaA^otu [ Thou hast done ill ]. (M.) You say, saw~aA^otu Ealayohi maA SanaEa , (S,) or SaniyEahu , (K,) i. e. fiEolahu , (TA,) inf. n. tasowiy^apN and tasowiYo'N , I discommended to him what he had done, or his deed; and said to him A^asaA^ota [ Thou hast done ill ]. (S, K.) And A_ino A^asaA^otu fasaw~iy^o EalaY~a [ If I do ill, say thou to me, Thou hast done ill ]. (S.)
4 , [inf. n. A_isaA='apN ,] He did evil, or ill

; or acted ill; contr. of A^aHosana : (S, M, K:) [and so] AsiA=' fiY fiEolihi . (Msb.) You say, AsA=' A_ilayohi (S, K) and lahu and Ealayhi and bihi (TA) He did evil or ill, or acted ill, to him. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- [See also A^asowaY , in several senses, in art. swy .] -A2- AsA='hu He corrupted it, or marred it; (M, K;) [ did it ill; ] did it not well; namely, a thing. (M.) It is said in a prov., A^asaA='a kaArihN maA Eamila [ An unwilling person did ill what he did ]; relating to a man who was compelled against his will, by another, to do a thing, and marred it, or did it not well: it is applied to the man who seeks an object of want and does not take pains to accomplish it. (M, Meyd. *) See also 1, in two places, in the former half of the paragraph. [And see

8 He experienced evil, or that which he disliked or hated, (S, * K, TA,) or displeasure, (TA,) or grief, or anxiety. (M, TA.) AisotaA='a lahaA occurs in a trad. as meaning He (the Prophet) became displeased, or grieved, or anxious, on account of it; i. e., on account of a dream that had been related to him: or, accord. to one relation, the right reading is AisotaA=lahaA , meaning “ he sought the interpretation of it, by consideration. ” (TA.)

is an inf. n. of saA='a , (Lth, S, M, K,) intrans., (Lth, M,) and trans.: (S, M, K:) and is also used as an epithet, applied to a man, (M, Msb, and Ham p. 712,) and to an action. (Msb.) You say rajulu sawo'K (S, M, Msb, K) [ A man of evil nature or doings

; or] a man who does what is evil, displeasing, grievous, or vexatious: (M, TA:) and rajulu Als~awo'i [ the man of evil nature or doings &c.]: (S, K:) and *iy^obu Als~awo'i [ the wolf of evil nature &c.], as in a verse cited voce A^aHaAla , in art. Hwl : (S:) and Eamalu sawo'K [ a deed of evil nature ]: (M, Msb:) and Eamalu Als~awo'i [ the deed of evil nature ]: (Ham p. 498:) and naEotu sawo'K [ an epithet of evil nature ]: (O and K in art. sHq :) and saEofu sawo'K a bad commodity: (O and TA in art. sEf :) and if you make the former word determinate [by means of the article Al ], you use the latter as an epithet [also], (M, * Msb, and Ham, p. 712, *) and you say Alr~ajulu Als~awo'u [ the evil man, or the man who does what is evil &c.]: (Msb, and Ham p. 712:) and AlEamalu Als~awo'u [ the ev

is the subst. from saA='ahu ; (S, M, * K;) [so, app., accord. to the generality of the lexicologists;] or inf. n. (Ksh and Bd in ii. 46) of say~iy^N , (Ksh ibid.,) or of saA='a , aor. yasuwo'u , (Bd ibid.,) or of saA='ahu [q. v.]; (TA;) signifying Evilness, badness, abominableness, foulness, or unseemliness; [and displeasingness, grievousness, or vexatiousness; ] as, for instance, of natural disposition, and of doings: (Ksh ubi suprà:) vitious, immoral, unrighteous, sinful, or wicked, conduct: [hence, ramaAhu bisuwo'K : see art. rmy :] anything disapproved, or disallowed

; or regarded as evil, bad, abominable, foul, or unseemly: (S, TA:) [ an evil action or event: ] evilness of state or condition: harm, injury, hurt, mischief, or damage: (IB, TA:) anything that is mentioned as being say~iy^ [i. e. evil, &c.]: (Lth, TA:) any evil, evil affection, cause of mischief or harm or injury, noxious or destructive thing, calamity, disease, or malady: (M, K, TA:) [pl. A^asowaA='N , accord. to a general rule.] The saying maA A^unokiruka mino suwo'K means I do not disacknowledge thee in consequence of suwo' [i. e. evilness, &c.,] that I have seen in thee, but only in consequence of my little knowledge of thee. (S.) linaSorifa Eanohu Als~uwo'a waAlfaHo$aA='a , in the Kur [xii. 24], is said by Zj to mean, [ In order that we might turn away from him ] unfaithfulness to hi

99 and xlviii. 6], (TA,) mean Defeat, and evil; (K, TA;) and trial, or affliction, and torment; (TA;) and perdition, and destruction, or corruption: (K, TA:) and in like manner in the saying, A^umoTirato maTara Als~w'i , (K, TA,) in the Kur [xxv. 42]: (TA:) or Als~uwo' means harm, injury, hurt, mischief, or damage; and evilness of state or condition; [as expl. before;] and ↓ , corruption, or destruction, or perdition: (K, * TA:) or Als~uwo' in the phrase daAy^irapu Als~uwo'i means defeat and evil; and the reading ↓ is from [i. e. syn. with ] AlmasaA='ap [as inf. n.]. (S. [See also daAy^irapN , in art. dwr .]) Accord. to Zj, in the saying in the Kur [xlviii. 6], ↓ , (TA,) meaning Zan~a AlA^amori Als~awo'i [i. e. Who opine, of God, the opining of the evil thing ], (Bd,) it is allowable to re
; or insanity, or madness. (M, TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Leprosy, syn. baraSN , (Lth, S, M, K, TA,) is said to be its meaning in the Kur xx.

32. (S, TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The fire: so in the Kur xxx. 9, accord. to the reading Als~uwo'a : (K, TA:) said to mean there Hell: but the reading commonly known is ↓ . (TA.) ― -b5- And (assumed tropical:) Weakness in the eye. (K. [Thus, i. e. with damm to the s , in the CK and TK: in the TA said to be bAlftH ; but this is evidently a mistake for bAlDm~ .])
: see say~iy^N .

The Eaworap [or pudendum ], (S, Mgh, Msb,) i. e. (Msb) the faroj [which means the same, or the external portion of the organs of generation ], (Lth, M, IAth, Msb, K,) of a man, and of a woman: (Lth, Msb, TA:) and the anus: (Az and TA in art. swY :) dual sawo'ataAni : and pl. sawoA=tN : so called because its becoming exposed to men displease [or shames] the owner thereof; (Msb;) or because of its unseemliness. (Ham p.

510.) In the Kur vii. 19, for sawoA=tihimaA , some read sawaAtihimaA ; and some, saw~aAtihimaA . (Bd.) ― -b2- In the Kur v. 34, it means The dead body, or corpse; (Bd, Jel;) because it is deemed unseemly to be seen. (Bd.) ― -b3- Accord. to IAth, the former is the primary signification: and hence it is transferred to denote Any saying, or action, of which one is ashamed when it appears: (TA:) any evil, bad, abominable, foul, or unseemly, saying or action; (S, K, TA;) as also ↓ : (M:) any disgracing action or thing: (Lth, TA:) an evil, abominable, or unseemly, property, quality, custom, or practics; (K, TA;) as also ↓ , or ↓ ; (accord. to different copies of the K; [the latter perhaps fem. of ↓ like the former, of the same class as dafoA^aY and danoA^aY , or fem. of ↓ , like EaTo$aY fem. of

as used in the saying Daraba fulaAnN EalaY fulaAnK saAyapF is held by some to be originally with ' , and of the measure faEolapN , from Als~awo'u ; so that the saying means Such a one did to such a one a thing that caused displeasure to him; and did evil to him: others hold that the saying means such a one made a way to do what he desired to such a one; in which case, sAyp is of the measure faEolapN from saw~ayotu ; originally sawoyapN , which is changed into say~apN , and then into saAyapN , in like manner as diw~aAnN is changed into diywaAnN . (Aboo-Bekr, TA.) [See the same word in art. swY .]
: see sawo'apN , in two places.

is [fem. of ↓ , q. v., as meaning More, and most, evil, bad, abominable, foul, unseemly, unsightly, or ugly: and is also] a subst. signifying an evil, a bad, an abominable, a foul, or an unseemly, action; (Msb, TA;) i. q. faEolapN say~iy^apN [and say~iy^apN alone]: in this sense, [as well as in the former,] (TA,) contr. of HusonaY . (S, M, K, TA.) ― -b2- In the Kur xxx. 9, (S, TA,) accord. to the reading commonly known, (TA,) [as contr. of AlHusonaY ,] Als~uwo'aY means (assumed tropical:) The fire (S, K, TA) of Hell. (TA.) See also suwo'N , last explanation but one.
: see A^asowaA^u (of which it is said by some to be fem.) in two places: ― -b2- and see also sawo'apN , in four places.

is [app. an instance of the alteration of the latter of two epithets to assimilate it to the former, originally xazoyaAnu A^asowaA^u , meaning Ashamed, or base, or vile, or ignominious, and evil, bad, &c.,] from AlquboHu . (M, TA.) ― -b2- See also sawo'apN .

, [originally sayowiy^N (as will be shown below, voce say~iy^apN ), then sayoyiy^N , and then say~iy^N ,] applied to a thing [of any kind], (Lth, TA,) Evil, bad, abominable, foul, unseemly, unsightly, or ugly; (Lth, Msb, TA;) contr. of HasanN : (Msb:) sometimes contracted into ↓ , like as hay~inN is contracted in hayonN , and lay~nN into layonN ; as in the saying of Et-Tuhawee, walaA yajozuwna mino HasanK misaYo'K walaA yajozuwna mino gilaZK biliyni [ And they will not requite good with evil, nor will they requite roughness with gentleness ]. (S.) You say qawolN say~iy^N [ An evil saying

; or] a saying that displeases. (M, TA.) And faEolapN say~iy^apN [ An evil action or deed ]. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [xxxv. 41], wamakora A@ls~ay~iy^i walaA yaHiyqu A@lomakoru A@ls~ay~iy^N A_il~aA biA^aholihi [ And in the plotting of that which is evil; but the evil plotting shall not beset any save the authors thereof ]. (M, TA.) One says also, fulaAnN say~iy^u AlAixotiyaAri [ Such a one is evil in respect of choice, or preference ]. (S.) [See also the next paragraph.]

[fem. of say~iy^N , q. v.: and also a subst., being transferred from the category of epithets to that of substs. by the affix p ], originally sayowiy^apN , (S,) An evil act or action; contr. of HasanapN ; (Msb;) a fault, an offence, or an act of disobedience

; or such as is intentional; a sin, a crime, or an act of disobedience for which one deserves punishment; syn. xaTiyoy^apN : (M, K:) pl. say~iy^aAtN . (TA.) It is said in a trad., AlHasanapu bayona Als~ay~iy^atayoni [ The good act is between the two evil acts ]; meaning that the exceeding of the just bounds is a say~iy^ap , and the falling short thereof is a say~iy^ap , and the pursuing a middle course between these two is a Hasanap . (TA.) [See also sawo'apN and suwo'aY .] ― -b2- Also; tropically, (tropical:) The recompense of a say~iy^ap properly so termed [i. e. as expl. above]. (Msb in art. mkr .) ― -b3- An evil, or evil accident; a calamity; a misfortune; (Ksh in iv. 81;) a trial, or an affliction; opposed to HasanapN ; (Ksh and Bd in iv. 80;) scarcity of herbage, or of the goods, con
80. (Er- Rághib, TA in art. Hsn .)

; fem. suwo'aY : see the latter word. One says, huwa A^asowaA^u Alqawomi He is the most evil, &c., of the people, or party; syn. A^aqobaHuhumo : and hiYa Als~uwo'aY She is the most evil, &c. (Msb.) And the [common] people say A^asowaA^u AlA^aHowaAli , meaning The [ worst, or] most scanty, and weakest, of states or conditions. (Msb.) -A2- [Also,] applied as an epithet to a man, (El-Umawee, M, TA,) Evil, bad, abominable, foul, unseemly, unsightly, or ugly: (ElUmawee, M, K, TA:) fem. ↓ , (El-Umawee, M, K,) which is thus applied to a woman; (ElUmawee, S, M;) or this is an instance of the measure faEElaA='u having no [masc. of the measure] A^afaEalu . (M, TA.) See also sawo'apN , in four places. It is said in a trad. (M, TA) of the Prophet, or of 'Omar, (TA,) waluwdN xayorN mino HasonaA='a Eaqi

an inf. n. of saA='ahu : (S, M, K:) and [also a subst. signifying An evil, as being] a cause of grief or vexation; contr. of masar~apN : originally masowaA^apN : and therefore the pl. is ↓ , for masaAwiy^u ; (Msb;) signifying also vices, faults, defects, or imperfections; (S, Msb, K, TA;) and diseases; (S, TA;) and acts of disobedience: (Msb:) so in the saying, badato masaAwiyhi His acts of disobedience, and vices, faults, &c., appeared: (Msb:) and Alxayolu tajoriY EalaY masaAwiyhaA Horses run, notwithstanding their vices, or faults, &c., (S, Meyd, K,) and diseases; (S, Meyd;) for their generousness impels them to do so: (S, Meyd, K: but omitted in the CK:) and in like manner, the ingenuous generous man bears difficulties, and defends, or protects, what he is bound to defend or protect, or
: see the next preceding paragraph.

senses.text: A long, or far, journey; like suboA^apN ; (K, TA;) of which it is a dial. var.: a short journey is termed surobapN . (TA.)

A well-known [ beverage of the kind called ] nabiy* , prepared from wheat, and much drunk by the people of Egypt, (L, TA,) at their festivals: (TA:) and also prepared from rice: (MF, TA:) [ also from the pips of a species of melon, called in Egypt Eabodal~aAwiY~ ; (see art. Ebd ; and see also White's “ Abdollatiphi Hist. Aegypti Compendium, ” pp. 52-3
; or De Sacy's transl., pp. 34-5;) moistened and pounded, and steeped in water, which is then strained, and sweetened with sugar: ] it is mentioned in a trad. and by several writers. (TA.)

senses.text: 1 , said of a weaver, He passed the misowajap , i. e. the sprinkling instrument, to and fro over his web [ to dress the warps with the preparation termed sawoj ]. (A, TA. *) ― -b2- [

Hence, app., unless the reverse be the case, the inf. n.] sawajaAnN signifies The act of going and coming: (AA, O, K, TA:) asserted by some to be sawojaAnN , [and thus it is in the CK,] but this is a mistake. (TA.) You say, saAja , aor. yasuwju , inf. n. sawojN [and sawajaAnN ], He, or it, went and came. (TA.) ― -b3- And sAj , (IAar, O, K,) aor. as above, (IAar, O,) inf. n. sawojN and suwaAjN and sawajaAnN , He went along gently, softly, or in a leisurely manner. (IAar, O, K.) IAar cites the following [as an ex. of an epithet hence derived]: AljilobiHi ↓ [A female fair in face: she is not the ugly old woman that goes along gently, or softly, by reason of decrepitude]. (O.)

2 (A, Msb) wanaHowihi (Msb) He made a siyaAj , i. e. an enclosure (A, Msb) composed of thorns and the like, (Msb,) around the grape-vines (A, Msb) and the like; as also sy~j , with Y , agreeably with the word syAj [from which it is derived]: (Msb:) and sy~j HaAy^iTahu , inf. n. tasoyiyjN , he made an enclosure (K and TA in art. syj ) of thorns and the like (TA in that art.) around his garden of palm-trees or vines. (S, TA.) $awaY fiY AlHariyqi samakatahu [ He broiled his fish in the fire of a burning house ] is a post-classical prov. of the people of Baghdád, relating to the concealing, disguising, or cloaking, of a fault, for the purpose of seizing an opportunity; orginating from the fact that the thief used, when he saw the fire of a burning house in a place, to go thither for the purpose of theft; and if it were in his power, he did what he desired; and if he were lighted on, he said, I came to broil a fish. He proceeded, or journeyed, in a direct course, not desiring [ to pursue ] any other: as though he had made a vow to do so. ISd says, Th cites this verse, and says in explanation of it, This was a man who swore, saying, If I do not overcome, I will cut off my hand. He seems to consider it as implying the signification of vowing. So in the L. But it requires consideration.
